\section{The Frobenius-Generation Coincidence Identity (FGCI)}
\label{sec:fgci}

The first selection (\S\ref{sec:first_selection}) and the cascade of
Chapter~\ref{chap:mathsubstrate} introduced the lepton seed $b_{L_1} = 73$ as
the output of the GTE arithmetic sieve: the cascade formula evaluated at $N_c = 3$
produces 73 as the first-generation lepton parameter. Here we prove something deeper:
the integer 73 is independently derivable from $N_c = 3$ through two completely
different arithmetic chains, and the chains agree uniquely at $N_c = 3$.

\subsection*{Two Arithmetic Routes to the Lepton Seed}

\paragraph{Route (a) --- Frobenius prime chain.}
The Frobenius prime formula at level $n$ is:
\begin{equation}
  F(n) = n^4 - n^2 + 1.
  \label{eq:frobenius}
\end{equation}
This is the level-2 Frobenius chain formula, ascending from the level-1 formula
$n^2 - n + 1$ that generates the field order $|\mathbb{Z}_7| = 3^2 - 3 + 1 = 7$.
At $n = N_c = 3$:
\[
F(3) = 81 - 9 + 1 = 73.
\]
The Frobenius tower starting at $N_c = 3$ is:
\[
\{|{\mathbb{Z}_7}|,\; b_{L_1}\} = \{7,\; 73\},
\]
generated by $F^{(1)}(3) = 3^2-3+1 = 7$ and $F^{(2)}(3) = 3^4-3^2+1 = 73$.
The tower terminates at level 3: $3^{2\cdot2}-3^2+1 = 703 = 19 \times 37$ is composite.

\paragraph{Route (b) --- GTE cascade arithmetic.}
The cascade-arithmetic formula for the first-generation lepton $b$-value is:
\begin{equation}
  G(n) = n^4 - \frac{n^2+1}{2} - n.
  \label{eq:cascade}
\end{equation}
At $n = N_c = 3$: the tau lepton amplitude $a_\tau = (N_c^2+1)/2 = 5$, so:
\[
G(3) = 81 - 5 - 3 = 73.
\]
This is the formula that appears in the $N_c$-structural chain below.

\paragraph{The coincidence.}
Both routes give 73 at $N_c = 3$. Subtracting the two formulas:
\begin{align}
  F(n) - G(n) &= \left(n^4 - n^2 + 1\right) - \left(n^4 - \tfrac{n^2+1}{2} - n\right) \notag \\
  &\;\propto\; n^2 - 2n - 3 = (n-3)(n+1).
  \label{eq:fgci_poly}
\end{align}
The polynomial $(n-3)(n+1)$ has a unique positive root $n = 3$. For any positive
integer $n \neq 3$, the two routes give different values.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,
  title={The Frobenius-Generation Coincidence Identity (FGCI) (\CatAL)}]
$F(n) = G(n)$ if and only if $n = N_c = 3$.

Both the Frobenius chain formula $F(n) = n^4-n^2+1$ and the cascade-arithmetic
formula $G(n) = n^4-(n^2+1)/2-n$ agree on $b_{L_1} = 73$ uniquely at $n = 3$.

\smallskip\noindent
\textbf{Lean certs} (all \CatAL, zero sorry, \texttt{FrobeniusChain.lean}, ugp-lean,
17 theorems):

\lean{fgci\_unique\_at\_nc} (\texttt{decide}): for all $n \in \{0,\ldots,9\}$,
$F(n) = G(n) \Leftrightarrow n = 3$.

\lean{fgci\_bundle}: FGCI + Frobenius tower $\{7,73\}$ + termination at $703 = 19\times 37$.

\lean{fgci\_polynomial\_zero\_at\_nc}: $F(3) = G(3) = 73$.
\end{tcolorbox}

A structurally independent derivation of $N_c = 3$ is established in
\cite{SpivackOctonionicShadow}: the pencil count of the $(7,3,1)$ combinatorial
design under the embedding $F_{21}\hookrightarrow G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O})$
and the identification $\mathrm{Stab}_{G_2}(\mathrm{apex}) = \mathfrak{su}(3)$
(\CatAL, \lean{apex\_stabilizer\allowbreak\_is\_su3\_certificate}) yields three pencils $=$ three colours
through a geometric route entirely independent of the FGCI arithmetic above.

\subsection*{The $N_c$ Structural Chain}

The FGCI is part of a broader $N_c$-structural chain: from the single integer
$N_c = 3$ alone, the GTE framework derives the entire first-generation lepton
structure~\cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}:
\begin{align}
  \delta &= N_c + \tfrac{N_c^2-1}{2} = 3 + 4 = 7
    \quad \text{(ridge offset $= |\mathbb{Z}_7|$)}, \\
  a_\tau &= \tfrac{N_c^2+1}{2} = 5 \quad \text{(tau lepton amplitude)}, \\
  a_\mu  &= N_c^2 = 9            \quad \text{(muon amplitude)}, \\
  a_e    &= 1                    \quad \text{(electron amplitude, fixed)}, \\
  b_1    &= N_c^4 - a_\tau - N_c = 81 - 5 - 3 = 73 \quad \text{(lepton seed)}.
\end{align}
The fact that $\delta = 7 = |\mathbb{Z}_7|$ is not a coincidence: the ridge offset
equals the field order. The entire first-generation lepton cascade flows from $N_c = 3$.

\textbf{Lean cert:} \lean{N\_c\_determines\_everything} (\CatAL,
\texttt{KoideAngle.lean}, ugp-lean, zero sorry) \cite{Spivack2026_Koide}.

\subsection*{What the FGCI Proves About $N_c$}

The FGCI adds an independent constraint on $N_c$. For the Frobenius prime tower
(a number-theoretic construction rooted in the $F_{21}$ group structure) and the
cascade arithmetic (the GTE orbit sieve formula) to agree on the lepton seed, the
color rank must be exactly 3. Two entirely different mathematical roads to the lepton
seed constrain the color rank to be 3.

Combined with the three additional constraints on $N_c$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},itemsep=2pt]
\item Three-tape CMCA architecture (DPP Theorem);
\item GoE orbit depth forcing;
\item QCD $\beta$-function integrality;
\item FGCI unique coincidence,
\end{enumerate}
the color rank $N_c = 3$ is determined by four independent mechanisms, each via a
distinct mathematical route. The convergence is evidence of structural necessity.

\subsection*{The Cyclotomic Identity Web}

The FGCI formulas are not isolated: every one of the GTE structural constants
satisfies an exact cyclotomic-polynomial identity, organized around the sixth
cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_6(x) = x^2 - x + 1$ --- the norm form of the
Eisenstein ring $\mathbb{Z}[\omega]$.  All of the following are Level-1
arithmetic identities, with no free parameter:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(I\arabic*)},itemsep=2pt]
\item \textbf{The Higgs coefficient:} $c_H = \Phi_3(N_{\rm gen}) = 3^2+3+1 = 13$,
  and equivalently $c_H = \Phi_6(D) = 4^2-4+1$ with $D = 4$ the spacetime
  dimension; the identity $\Phi_3(n) = c_H$ holds uniquely at $n = N_{\rm gen} = 3$
  \mbox{(\lean{c\_H\_eq\_phi3\_ngen}, \lean{cH\_phi3\_unique\_at\_ngen}, \CatAL)}.
\item \textbf{The FGCI formula itself:} $F(n) = n^4 - n^2 + 1 = \Phi_{12}(n) =
  \Phi_6(n^2)$ --- the Frobenius chain ascends the cyclotomic ladder by squaring
  the argument.  The full Frobenius tower is
  $\{7, 73, 703\} = \{\Phi_6(3),\, \Phi_6(3^2),\, \Phi_6(3^3)\}$ (\CatAD).
\item \textbf{The alphabet--Higgs product:} $q \cdot c_H = 7 \times 13 = 91 =
  \Phi_6(10)$ (\CatAD).
\item \textbf{The group order:} $|F_{21}| = 21 = \Phi_6(2)\,\Phi_6(3) = \Phi_6(5)$
  --- the product of the Eisenstein norms $N(1-\omega) = 3$ and $N(3+\omega) = 7$.\\
  (\lean{f21\_order\_eisenstein\_norm\_product},
  \lean{phi6\_identity\_bundle}, \CatAL)
\end{enumerate}
A closing remark on the ladder's base: iterating $\Phi_6$ from 2 generates
Sylvester's sequence $2 \to 3 \to 7 \to 43$, so the alphabet prime is
$7 = \Phi_6(\Phi_6(2))$ --- the second rung of the minimal cyclotomic tower.
The identities (I1)--(I4) are exact theorems; the claim that a single
\emph{mechanism} (the Eisenstein arithmetic of $F_{21}$, §\ref{sec:f21})
underlies all of them is established for (I1) and (I4) and remains \CatB{} for
the web as a whole.  The full mathematical treatment, including the
residue-field model of $F_{21}$ and the null battery, is given in
P49~\cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialWolfram}.

\subsection*{A Fourth Route to $b_1 = 73$: The $\varphi(7)$ Identity}

The Frobenius chain (I2) and the cascade arithmetic of this section already establish
$b_1 = 73$ by two independent routes.  The $\varphi(7)$ corollary of
\S\ref{sec:gf7} supplies a third, structurally distinct route:
\begin{equation}
  b_1 = 2^{\varphi(7)} + N_{\rm gen}^2 = 2^6 + 3^2 = 73.
  \label{eq:b1_totient}
\end{equation}
where $\varphi(7) = |\mathrm{GF}(7)^*| = 6$ is the Euler totient of $7$.
This expression encodes two GTE structural constants simultaneously:
the order of the multiplicative group of the coefficient field ($\varphi(7) = 6$,
giving the Fermat exponent $2^6$), and the generation count ($N_{\rm gen}^2 = 9$).

The identity also reveals why the two historically distinct routes to $1/\alpha_{\rm em}$
are algebraically equivalent.  Setting $1/\alpha_{\rm em} = 2 b_1 - N_{\rm gen}^2$
(the archival route, discovered independently) and $1/\alpha_{\rm em} = 2^7 + N_{\rm gen}^2$
(the current structural route) equal and substituting~\eqref{eq:b1_totient}:
\[
  2 b_1 - N_{\rm gen}^2 = 2(2^6 + N_{\rm gen}^2) - N_{\rm gen}^2 = 2^7 + N_{\rm gen}^2
  = 137.
\]
The equivalence is an exact arithmetic identity, not a coincidence.
\textbf{Lean certs:} \lean{b1\_totient7\_ngen\_identity}\\
\lean{alpha\_inv\_routes\_equivalent}
(\CatAL, zero sorry, \texttt{AlphaEMArchivalIdentities.lean}, ugp-lean).

An additional structural cross-check: $b_1 + 1/\alpha_{\rm em}^{(0)} = 73 + 137 = 210 =
2 \times 3 \times 5 \times 7 = \mathrm{primorial}(7)$.  The sum of the lepton seed and
the fine-structure constant inverse equals the primorial of the coefficient-field
characteristic. \mbox{(\lean{primorial7\_alpha\_b1\_identity}, \CatAL)}

\section{The Master Quadratic of the Master Polynomial}
\label{sec:master_quadratic}

The 19-bit polynomial $p$ is the theory's master object --- the MDL-selected
specification.  Inscribed in its diagonal is a single integer quadratic that
turns out to unify two of the framework's central derivation chains.  Setting
$L = C = R = x$ and asking when the diagonal is self-consistent,
$p(x,x,x) = x$, yields the universal factorization over $\mathbb{Z}$:
\begin{equation}
  p(x,x,x) - x \;=\; -\,x\,(x^2 + x - 1)
  \qquad \mbox{(\lean{gte\_diagonal\_quadratic\_factorization}, \CatAL)}.
  \label{eq:master_quadratic}
\end{equation}
The quadratic $m(x) = x^2 + x - 1$ --- the \emph{master quadratic} --- has
discriminant $\Delta = 5 = \Nfam$: the family count is the discriminant of the
polynomial's diagonal self-consistency core.  The master quadratic is not a
rival of $p$ or a replacement for it; it is $p$'s diagonal self-consistency
core, and its arithmetic completions over different base fields turn out to
carry two crown-jewel results of the framework and one new vacuum theorem.

\begin{description}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=4pt]
\item[Over $\mathbb{R}$ (the archimedean completion).]
The unique positive root is $x^* = (\sqrt{5}-1)/2 = 1/\varphi$, the
golden-ratio conjugate --- precisely the SRRG fixed point that seeds the Higgs
vacuum expectation value (Ch.~\ref{chap:forces},
\lean{gte\_poly\_srrg\_bridge}, \CatAL).  The root is the algebraic input to
the Level-1$\to$Level-2 bridge: the continuum VEV $v = 246.16$~GeV is its
physical output.
\item[Over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$ (the 7-adic completion).]
The quadratic is rootless: its discriminant $5$ is a quadratic non-residue
modulo~7 \mbox{(\lean{disc5\_dichotomy\_gf7}, \CatAL)}.  This rootlessness is
exactly the mechanism that makes the binary floor $\{0,1\}$ the unique
minimal invariant subset and forces Rule~110 universality
(§\ref{sec:gf7}); it is robust 7-adically --- the quadratic has no root
modulo $7^k$ for any $k$, hence none in $\mathbb{Q}_7$
\mbox{(\lean{master\_quadratic\_no\_root\_mod\_seven\_pow}, \CatAL)}.
The same arithmetic explains the GF(5) displaced-vacuum pathology of
§\ref{sec:gf5}: $5$ is the ramified prime of the quadratic
($\Delta \equiv 0 \bmod 5$), producing the repeated root $x = 2$.
\item[In polynomial dynamics (the temporal completion).]
The same quadratic controls vacuum uniqueness at every ring size: the vacuum
is the \emph{only} temporally fixed configuration of the $p$-dynamics on a
ring of any size $n$ --- $\mathrm{Fix}(T_n) = \{\text{vacuum}\}$ for all $n$
--- because any non-vacuum fixed configuration would require a golden
fixed point of the associated Fibonacci--M\"{o}bius map, and the master
quadratic is rootless over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$.\\
(\lean{vacuum\_unique\_temporal\_fixed\_point\_ring}, \CatAL)\\
This is the dynamical complement of the algebraic uniqueness: the spatial
statement \mbox{(\lean{vacuum\_unique\_fixed\_point\_z7})} holds pointwise;
the temporal statement holds for the full ring dynamics at every size.
\end{description}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=gray!5,colframe=gray!55!black,
  title={One Quadratic, Three Completions (\CatAL)}]
The diagonal of the 19-bit polynomial factors as
$p(x,x,x) - x = -x(x^2+x-1)$ over $\mathbb{Z}$, with discriminant
$\Delta = 5 = \Nfam$.  Its three arithmetic completions carry three
independent results:
\begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,topsep=3pt,leftmargin=1.8em]
\item $\mathbb{R}$: root $1/\varphi$ $\to$ SRRG fixed point $\to$ Higgs VEV
  (the L1$\to$L2 bridge input);
\item $\mathrm{GF}(7)$: rootless ($5$ is a QNR mod 7) $\to$ unique binary
  floor $\to$ Rule~110 universality;
\item polynomial dynamics: $\mathrm{Fix}(T_n) = \{\text{vacuum}\}$ for every
  ring size $n$ (vacuum uniqueness).
\end{enumerate}
Supporting arithmetic: the roots live in $\mathrm{GF}(49)$ and are swapped by
Frobenius; the ramified prime $q = 5$ derives the GF(5) pathology; the
rootlessness persists to all powers $7^k$.\\
\mbox{(\lean{golden\_floor\_duality\_bundle},}
\mbox{\lean{gf49\_golden\_roots\_frobenius\_swap}, \CatAL)}\\
The electroweak scale and the computational floor are the two arithmetic
faces of one $\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic inscribed in the diagonal of $p$.  Full
mathematical treatment: P49 \cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialWolfram}.
\end{tcolorbox}

All facts in this section are Level-1 (algebraic-certificate) statements about
the polynomial's arithmetic; the SRRG root is the algebraic input whose
continuum output (the VEV) lives at Level~2.  None of this section is a
continuum-field theorem.

\subsection*{The Annealed Density Map}

The diagonal of $p$ also defines a density-evolution map:
$\rho' = p(\rho,\rho,\rho) = 2\rho - \rho^2 - \rho^3$.  This is the mean-field
(annealed) approximation of Rule~110's density evolution, obtained by assuming
statistical independence of neighbouring cells.  Its unique non-trivial fixed
point satisfies $p(\rho^*,\rho^*,\rho^*) = \rho^*$, i.e.\
$\rho^*(1 - \rho^* - (\rho^*)^2) = 0$, giving $\rho^* = 1/\varphi$ as the non-zero
solution --- precisely the SRRG fixed point
\mbox{(\lean{rule110\_meanfield\_fixed\_point\_golden}, \CatAL)}.  The contraction
eigenvalue at $\rho^*$ is
$\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}\rho\,[p(\rho,\rho,\rho)]\big|_{\rho^*} = -1/\varphi^2$
(using $(\rho^*)^2 = 1 - \rho^*$), matching the certified SRRG contraction
eigenvalue \mbox{(\lean{meanfield\_contraction\_eq\_neg\_inv\_phi\_sq}, \CatAL)}.
The quenched (correlated) Rule~110 density lies near $4/7$ --- the ether density
--- while the annealed (decorrelated) limit is $1/\varphi \approx 0.618$; the
master quadratic $m(x) = x^2 + x - 1$ governs both limits.

\subsection*{The Golden Universality Class}

The master quadratic $m(x) = x^2 + x - 1$ is the governing polynomial at the
minimum-complexity point in multiple independent mathematical domains
\mbox{(\lean{golden\_universality\_class\_theorem}, \CatAD)}.  Two meta-theorems
characterise this universality.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,
  title={Meta-theorem A: Internal GTE Minimality (\CatD)}]

structures simultaneously:

  \mbox{(\lean{gte\_diagonal\_quadratic\_factorization}, \CatAL)};
\item \emph{SRRG fixed point:} the contraction eigenvalue is a root of $m(x)$
  \mbox{(\lean{gte\_poly\_srrg\_bridge}, \CatAL)};
\item \emph{Annealed density:} $p(\rho,\rho,\rho) = \rho$ iff $\rho = 1/\varphi$,
  a root of $m(x)$ (\CatAL);
\item \emph{MDL-minimal field:} $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$ is uniquely MDL-minimal among

\item \emph{Dynamical uniqueness:} $\mathrm{Fix}(T_n) = \{\text{vacuum}\}$ for all

  $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathrm{GF}(49)/\mathrm{GF}(7)) \cong \mathbb{Z}_2$ generates the

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=blue!5,colframe=blue!50!black,

The same polynomial governs the minimal object in six independent external

\begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,topsep=3pt,leftmargin=1.8em]
\item \emph{Modular tensor categories:} the Fibonacci anyon $\tau$ satisfies
  $\tau^2 = 1 + \tau$, i.e.\ $m(-\tau) = 0$; the reflected quadratic
  $m(-x) = x^2 - x - 1$ shares the field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$.  The \GTE\ kink
  fusion category is itself the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ Dijkgraaf--Witten \emph{abelian} MTC
  (§\ref{sec:bps_kinks}); the connection to the Fibonacci MTC is the polynomial

\item \emph{Virasoro minimal models:} the Yang--Lee model $M(2,\Nfam) = M(2,5)$ has

\item \emph{Exactly solvable models:} Baxter's hard-hexagon model has critical

\item \emph{Real quadratic fields:} $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$ has discriminant
  $5 = \Nfam$, the smallest among all real quadratic fields; fundamental unit

\end{enumerate}
\end{tcolorbox}

\GTE's master polynomial sits at the intersection of the deepest extremality
classes across mathematics.  The MDL principle does not merely select a convenient
polynomial --- it selects the uniquely minimal object in every relevant
mathematical universe simultaneously.  This convergence is the content of the
\emph{golden universality class}.

\section{Three Faces of MDL Revisited: Why This Is Not a Loop}
\label{sec:mdl_loop}

A reader who has followed the derivation from Chapter~\ref{chap:principle}
(\S\ref{sec:pi_mdl}) and this chapter may notice that MDL appears more than once:
first as Presentation Invariance (PI~$\equiv$~MDL, \S\ref{sec:pi_mdl}), then in
this chapter as the theory-selection criterion, and Chapters~\ref{chap:spacetime}
and~\ref{chap:qm} will use it a third time. Is the same principle applied repeatedly,
making the framework circular?

The answer is no. \S\ref{sec:mdl_three_faces} gives the full treatment. The essential
point is that the three roles operate on three logically disjoint domains:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}P{2.8cm}P{3.5cm}P{5.0cm}c@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Role} & \textbf{Domain} & \textbf{Application in this monograph} & \textbf{Cert} \\
\midrule
1.\ Theory selection & Theory space: all $\mathbb{Z}_N\times\mathbb{Z}_M$ CAs &
This chapter (MDL Uniqueness Theorem; both sequential applications --- seed and
rule): $\mathbb{Z}_7\times\mathbb{Z}_3$ selected & \CatAL \\[4pt]
2.\ Variational (PMDL) & Field configurations within $\PHIMDL$ &
Chapter~\ref{chap:spacetime} (gravity): operates on fields of the already-selected theory &
\CatAD \\[4pt]
3.\ Adjudication ($[D]$) & Candidate realizations of a dynamical trajectory &
Chapter~\ref{chap:qm} (Born rule): operates on outcomes within already-established dynamics &
\CatAL \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The logical order is strict. Role~2 cannot be applied before Role~1 closes: you
cannot minimize over field configurations before you know which theory defines those
fields. Role~3 cannot be applied before Role~2: you cannot adjudicate measurement
outcomes without the dynamics. The flow is:
\[
\underbrace{\text{Theory space}}_{\text{Role 1, this chapter}}
\;\longrightarrow\;
\underbrace{\text{Field configurations}}_{\text{Role 2, Ch.~\ref{chap:spacetime}}}
\;\longrightarrow\;
\underbrace{\text{Candidate realizations}}_{\text{Role 3, Ch.~\ref{chap:qm}}}.
\]

No role refers back to any prior role's domain. The three applications of MDL are not
three iterations of the same argument; they are one principle manifesting at three
successive levels of physical organization, logically downstream of each other.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=yellow!8,colframe=yellow!45!black,
  title={Non-Circularity Statement (\CatAL)}]
MDL is applied exactly once per domain. Role~1 (this chapter) selects among all
possible theories. Role~2 (Chapter~\ref{chap:spacetime}) operates within the
already-selected theory's field configuration space. Role~3
(Chapter~\ref{chap:qm}) operates within already-established dynamical trajectories.
No role refers back to or re-examines any prior role's domain.

zero custom axioms): formally certifies the domain disjointness and the bundle of
all three roles.
\end{tcolorbox}

\noindent
This closes Chapter~\ref{chap:selection}. The selection is complete --- both of

(\S\ref{sec:first_selection}, \CatAL); the seed's cascade emitted the

$\poly = C+R-CR-LCR$ over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$, interpolated from the orbit's
parity shadow as the closing edge of the UGP--$p$ triangle
(\S\ref{sec:lift}, \CatAL). Chapter~\ref{chap:field}
shows how this algebraic certificate lifts to the physical field $\PHIMDL$ that

\section{The \CMCA: The Algebraic Certificate}
\label{sec:cmca}

Before introducing $\PHIMDL$, we need to understand the algebraic proof system that
certifies what structures the physical field must contain.
That proof system is the Chiral Minkowski Cellular Automaton (\CMCA) --- the
Level~1 algebraic certificate whose rules and consequences lift to the physical
Level~2 field via the Algebraic Lifting Theorem.

\subsection*{What Is a Cellular Automaton?}

A cellular automaton is a grid of discrete cells, each in one of a finite number of
states, that all update simultaneously at each time step according to a fixed local rule.
The rule computes the new state of a cell from the current states of itself and its
nearest neighbors.
The CMCA's update rule is $\poly = C+R-CR-LCR$ over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$,
the Galois field with seven elements.
The three inputs $L$, $C$, $R$ are the left neighbor, center cell, and right neighbor,
all carrying values in $\{0,1,\ldots,6\}$.
This single polynomial is the object from which all of Standard Model physics descends.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=green!5,colframe=green!50!black,
  title={Definition: Chiral Minkowski Cellular Automaton (\CMCA)}]
The \CMCA\ is a 1+1-dimensional cellular automaton whose update polynomial is
$\poly = C+R-CR-LCR$ over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$.
It is the \emph{algebraic certificate} for $\PHIMDL$: it encodes the algebraic structure
that the physical field must inherit, but is not itself the physical substrate.
The physical substrate is the continuum field $\PHIMDL$ (Level~2); the \CMCA\ is
the discrete algebraic specification (Level~1).
\end{tcolorbox}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=blue!5,colframe=blue!55!black,
  title={The GTE Computational Architecture: One System, Four Levels},
  fonttitle=\bfseries]
\small
The polynomial $p(L,C,R) = C+R-CR-LCR$ defines a single physical system
expressed at four levels of description; each level is the same physics
at a different scale of resolution.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Level~0 --- Polynomial} (Object~0; P28, P49).
The raw $k{=}7$, $r{=}1$ CA rule over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$.
Class~3 chaotic on generic $\ZS$ inputs; Class~4 (Rule~110) on
$\{0,1\}$-inputs. MDL$+$PSC select it uniquely from $7^{343}$ candidates
(\lean{mdl\_ca\_rule\_coding\_closed}, \CatAL).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Level~1 --- PSC-projected orbit map} (Object~1, $f_{\rm MDL}$; P28, P37, P41).
The restriction of $p$ to PSC-admissible inputs: $f_{\rm MDL}$ maps 14 of the 343
neighborhoods non-trivially; all others produce the vacuum.
On the isolated 5-cell ring, $f_{\rm MDL}$ runs the SM generation orbit
$\mathrm{GEN}_1\to\mathrm{GEN}_2\to\mathrm{GEN}_3\to\mathrm{VAC}$ (\CatAL).
For quantum mechanics (Hilbert space, Born rule, gauge sectors), $f_{\rm MDL}$ is
used as an abstract ring orbit; for spacetime dynamics it is embedded in a

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Level~2 --- CMCA tape} (P41, P45).
$f_{\rm MDL}$ embedded in a 1D spatial tape with a chiral pair
(Rule~110 forward / Rule~124 backward) and an inner $\tau_c$ first-passage clock that gates
outer updates asynchronously --- the AFCA (Asynchronous Fractal Cellular Automata;

This is the \CMCA: the same Level~1 orbit structure running in $1{+}1$D

\subsection*{The Three-Layer Architecture of a Single Tape}

A single \CMCA\ tape has three causal layers, corresponding to the three irreducible
causal directions of $1{+}1$D Minkowski spacetime.

The \textbf{outer chiral pair} consists of two simultaneous update layers:
Rule~110 ($p(L,C,R)$, right-chiral) and Rule~124 ($p(R,C,L)$, its spatial mirror, left-chiral).
These two layers provide the two null directions $x^+$ and $x^-$ of $1{+}1$D Minkowski
spacetime and implement the V--A chiral structure: only the left-chiral (Rule~124) sector
couples to weak interactions.
Rule~124 is not an independent specification --- it is the free structural consequence of
the lattice's spatial reflection symmetry, costing zero additional MDL bits.

The \textbf{inner clock} is a third Rule~110 automaton that runs per-cell and gates when
the outer layers fire.
It implements proper-time ordering: configurations that move relative to the ether vacuum
tick the inner clock slower, giving the discrete analogue of SR time dilation.
The inner clock is forced by MDL to be Rule~110 (the same polynomial as the outer layer)
--- using any other rule would cost extra bits \cite{SpivackCMCA,SpivackThreeTapeCMCA}.

\subsection*{The Dimensional Protocol Principle and the Three-Tape Architecture}

A single \CMCA\ tape is intrinsically $1{+}1$-dimensional.
Three-dimensional space arises from three independent single-tape \CMCA{}s sharing a single

\subsection*{The Correct Interpretation: Certificate, Not Substrate}

The \CMCA\ is not the physical universe.
It is the algebraic proof system that certifies what structures must exist in the
physical universe.

The thermometer analogy from \cite{SpivackThreeTapeCMCA} captures the relationship:
a thermometer does not contain the gas it measures --- it certifies a property
(temperature) of that gas.
The \CMCA\ certifies algebraic properties of $\PHIMDL$; those properties are then
inherited by the continuum field via the Algebraic Lifting Theorem.

What the \CMCA\ \emph{cannot} do is provide exact Lorentz invariance.
For any finite lattice resolution $M$, the Nyquist residual
$\varepsilon_0(M) = \pi^2/(3M^2)$ measures the Lorentz-invariance error;
it is strictly positive for all finite $M$ and vanishes only as $M\to\infty$
(Lean: \lean{sr\_accuracy\_depends\_on\_M}, \CatAL\ zero sorry).
The physical substrate $\PHIMDL$, as an exact continuum field, is the unique
object in this construction class with zero Lorentz error --- which is why it
is the physical substrate, not the \CMCA\ \cite{SpivackCompleteness}.

The Level~1 / Level~2 architecture is therefore:
\begin{itemize}[itemsep=2pt]
\item \textbf{Level~1 (CMCA):} algebraic properties only --- charge quantization,
  generation count, Turing universality, baryon number, color confinement.
  Certified exactly, $M$-independently, in Lean~4.
\item \textbf{Level~2 ($\PHIMDL$):} the unique continuum realization with exact
  Lorentz invariance, exact kink masses, and the full quantum field theory.
\end{itemize}

\section{What Is a Particle? The Two-Level Picture}
\label{sec:two_levels}

This section answers the question every reader wants answered: what, precisely, is an electron?

\subsection*{The Standard QFT Answer and Its Limitation}

In standard quantum field theory, an electron is an excitation of the electron quantum
field --- a ripple in an abstract mathematical object that permeates all of spacetime.
This is correct but incomplete: it does not explain \emph{why} the electron field exists,
why it has charge $-1$, or why there are three generations of it.

In GTE, the answer is more specific and more derived.
An electron is a second-quantized Fock-space excitation within a $\ZS$ topological
superselection sector: the sector in which the field has wound from one vacuum
configuration to another in a way it cannot unwind without a paired antiparticle.
The topology determines the particle's quantum numbers; the classical kink
configuration that certifies the sector's existence is necessarily extended (never a
spatially compact object, \S\ref{sec:multikink_fock}), and the particle itself is the
normalizable Fock-space state that configuration certifies via the Algebraic Lifting
Theorem.
The field is everywhere; the topology is what identifies the particle.

\subsection*{The Analogy: A Twist in a Rope}

Imagine a rope that can exist in seven colors.
Normally the rope is uniform (vacuum state, color~0).
A kink is a region where the rope permanently changes color --- from color~0 to color~4,
say --- and never returns.
To undo the kink, you need a region where the rope returns from color~4 to color~0;
that is the antiparticle's kink.
When particle and antiparticle meet, the rope returns to uniform color.

The ``color'' here is the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ winding number.
The number of color-steps traversed determines the particle's identity:
two steps gives an up quark, three steps a $W^+$ boson, four steps an electron.
There is no ``substance'' here --- the particle's quantum numbers are set by a
configuration, not a material.
(This one-dimensional rope is a simplifying picture. In the physical $3{+}1$D theory
the certifying kink configuration is necessarily extended rather than a compact
region, and the particle itself is the Fock-space excitation it certifies ---
\S\ref{sec:multikink_fock} makes this precise.)

\subsection*{Level 1: What the \CMCA\ Certifies}

At Level~1, a particle is an \textbf{algebraic equivalence class} of PSC-admissible
\CMCA\ beable configurations sharing the same three algebraic invariants:
(1)~$\mathbb{Z}_7$ winding number $w \in \{0,2,3,4,6\}$,
(2)~$\mathbb{Z}_3$ color charge $Q_\chi \in \{0,1,2\}$,
(3)~generation orbit position (gen$_1$, gen$_2$, or gen$_3$).

The \CMCA\ certifies:

\begin{itemize}[itemsep=4pt]
\item \textbf{Which winding sectors exist.}
  The five PSC-admissible sectors $\{0,2,3,4,6\}$ are forced by the dark-mirror
  structure of $F_{21}$; sectors $\{1,5\}$ are PSC-forbidden (they correspond to
  stable dark-sector mirrors not present in the SM branch)
  \cite{SpivackCompleteness,SpivackPhiMDLField}.
  Lean: \lean{psc\_admissible\_sectors} (\CatAL, zero sorry).

\item \textbf{That exactly three generations exist.}
  The five-cell $\ZS^5$ orbit under $f_{\rm MDL}$ has exactly three non-vacuum
  orbit types cycling with period~3: gen$_1 \to$ gen$_2 \to$ gen$_3 \to$ gen$_1$.
  This is not an input --- it is a consequence of the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ arithmetic
  and the Garden-of-Eden property of the first generation.
  Lean: \lean{three\_generations\_physical}, \lean{sm\_period3\_orbit\_chain}
  (\CatAL, zero sorry).

\item \textbf{That the first generation is the lightest.}
  Gen$_1$ is a Garden of Eden (GoE) under $f_{\rm MDL}$: it has zero predecessors
  in the orbit dynamics.
  This means it is algebraically ``most stable'' and corresponds to the lightest
  generation.
  Lean: \lean{fmdl\_gen1\_is\allowbreak\_garden\_of\_eden} (\CatAL, zero sorry).

\item \textbf{Charge quantization and the charge formula.}
  $Q = w_{\rm centered}/3$ where $w_{\rm centered}$ is the centered representative
  of $w$ in $\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}$.
  Lean: \lean{gte\_charge\_is\_linear\_projection} (\CatAL, zero sorry).

\item \textbf{Fermionic vs.\ bosonic statistics.}
  Sectors $\{2,4,6\}$ are non-primitive roots of $\mathbb{Z}_7^*$ (multiplicative order~3)
  and carry fermionic statistics.
  Sector $\{3\}$ is the unique generator of $\mathbb{Z}_7^*$ (order~6) and carries
  bosonic statistics.
  Lean: \lean{gte\_winding\_identifies\_charged\_fermions} (\CatAL, zero sorry).
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What Level~1 cannot certify:} mass values (those come from the Level~2 orbit cascade),
specific CA patterns at Compton scale (the Glider-to-Fermion Map is open), and exact
Lorentz invariance (requires $M\to\infty$).
The key point is that we do not need to identify which Rule~110 glider pattern
corresponds to the electron in order for the theory to be complete at Level~1.
The Lifting Theorem (below) certifies \emph{existence} without identifying the
specific microstructure.

\subsection*{The Technical Bridge: How Discrete Arithmetic Becomes Continuous Gauge Theory}
\label{subsec:technical_bridge}

A physicist who knows gauge theory but not GTE will have a natural question: how does
arithmetic in the finite group $F_{21} = \ZS\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_3$ constrain a Lie-group
gauge theory in $3{+}1$ dimensions?  The answer is a three-step argument.

\subsubsection*{Step 1: Gauging an Exact Discrete Symmetry}

The $\PHIMDL$ Lagrangian
$\mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_\mu\Phi)^2 - V(\Phi)$
with $V(\Phi) = (m^2/49)(1-\cos 7\Phi)$ has an \emph{exact} discrete shift symmetry:
\[
  \Phi \;\to\; \Phi + \tfrac{2\pi}{7}
\]
leaving both kinetic and potential terms invariant ($\cos 7(\Phi + 2\pi/7) = \cos(7\Phi+2\pi) = \cos7\Phi$).
This is not an approximate or emergent symmetry — it is an exact arithmetic fact about
the cosine potential.  It is machine-certified as the $\ZS$ conservation law
(\lean{gte\_winding\_sm\allowbreak\_vertex\_conserved}, \CatAL, zero sorry).

Now apply the gauge principle: make the transformation parameter spacetime-dependent,
$\epsilon(x) = n(x)\cdot 2\pi/7$ for $n(x):\mathbb{R}^{3,1}\to\mathbb{Z}_7$.
A \emph{local} version of this symmetry requires introducing a connection field
$A_\mu$ to define the covariant derivative
$D_\mu\Phi = \partial_\mu\Phi - A_\mu$.
This is the standard logic of the gauge principle: exact symmetry $\Rightarrow$ gauging
is consistent $\Rightarrow$ gauge field $A_\mu$ is required.

\subsubsection*{Step 2: Why SU(3)\texorpdfstring{$\times$}{x}SU(2)\texorpdfstring{$\times$}{x}U(1) Specifically}

The discrete structure $F_{21} = \ZS\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_3$ imposes two simultaneous
constraints on the gauge field:
\begin{enumerate}[itemsep=3pt]
\item \textbf{From $\ZS$:} the connection must implement a $\mathrm{U}(1)$ holonomy
  consistent with $\mathbb{Z}_7$ winding ($\mathbb{Z}_7 \subset \mathrm{U}(1)$ since
  $\mathbb{Z}_7$ is cyclic).  The $\ZS$ part forces a $\mathrm{U}(1)$-type structure
  for electromagnetism.  Color charge arises from the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ Sylow subgroup
  (the abelianization $F_{21}^{\rm ab} = \mathbb{Z}_3$), forcing $\mathrm{SU}(3)$-type
  color gauge structure.

\item \textbf{From the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ twist in $F_{21}$:} the non-abelian semidirect
  product $\ZS\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_3$ means $\mathbb{Z}_3$ acts on $\ZS$ by the unique
  non-trivial automorphism of order 3.  This forces a non-abelian component in the
  gauge group, and specifically the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ weak structure from the
  chiral (V$-$A) asymmetry of the CMCA.
\end{enumerate}

The MDL-minimal Lie group that simultaneously implements both constraints --- the
$\ZS$ holonomy and the $F_{21}$ non-abelian extension --- is
$\mathrm{SU}(3)\times\mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{U}(1)$
(\CatAD, conditional on the TSpace domain assumption).

\subsubsection*{Step 3: Uniqueness — Why No Other Gauge Group Works}

Any other gauge group would require additional specification beyond what $F_{21}$
prescribes.  For example:
\begin{itemize}[itemsep=3pt]
\item $\mathrm{SU}(5)$ (GUT) introduces a rank-5 group with 24 generators, requiring
  at least $\log_2(24/8) \approx 1.6$ extra bits of specification compared to
  $\mathrm{SU}(3)\times\mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{U}(1)$.
\item $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ alone: replacing $F_{21}$ with $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ would cost
  $\geq 38$ additional MDL bits (\lean{algebraic\_necessity\_master\_bundle}, \CatAL).
\item Any $\mathbb{Z}_N$ structure with $N\neq 7$ is eliminated by exhaustive
  machine proof (\lean{unique\_cubic\_gravity\_coupling}, T96-02, \CatAL, zero sorry).
\end{itemize}

The MDL Uniqueness Theorem therefore certifies: among all $\mathbb{Z}_N\times\mathbb{Z}_M$
arithmetic structures, $\ZS\times\mathbb{Z}_3$ is the unique MDL-minimal one (\CatAL),
and $\mathrm{SU}(3)\times\mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{U}(1)$ is the unique MDL-minimal
Lie group implementing its constraints.

\subsubsection*{Algebraic Descent Concretely}

The Descent direction makes this physically precise: if $\ZS$ winding conservation
holds at every CMCA vertex (machine-certified), then the $\PHIMDL$ Lagrangian with
$F_{21}$ gauge structure must also conserve winding at every Compton-scale interaction.
Computing the Noether charges of the resulting conserved currents gives exactly the
SM electric charges ($Q = w_{\rm centered}/3$, machine-certified as
\lean{gte\_charge\_is\_linear\_projection}, \CatAL), color charges from $\mathbb{Z}_3$,
and weak isospin from the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ sector.

The gauge group is not assumed; it is forced by the arithmetic skeleton.
(\lean{algebraic\_descent\_theorem}, \CatAL; full derivation: Chapter~\ref{chap:forces}.)

\subsection*{Level 2: What $\PHIMDL$ Certifies}

At Level~2, a particle's mass, charge, and spin are certified by a \textbf{topological
BPS kink background} of $\PHIMDL$, characterized by its winding number
$w\in\{0,2,3,4,6\}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_3$ color charge $Q_\chi\in\{0,1,2\}$; the particle
itself is the Fock-space excitation this background certifies via the Algebraic
Lifting Theorem (\S\ref{sec:multikink_fock} establishes this precisely and proves the
certifying background is necessarily extended, never spatially compact).
Its mass, charge, and spin are entirely determined by these two numbers.
The full derivation follows in \S\ref{sec:bps_kinks}; here we give the key facts:

\begin{itemize}[itemsep=4pt]
\item \textbf{Identity is topology, not substance.}
  What makes an electron an electron is its winding number $w=4$, not any
  intrinsic material.
  Change the winding number and you have a different particle.
  The same $\PHIMDL$ field supports all SM particles; they differ only in
  their topological configuration.

\item \textbf{Topological protection.}
  A kink cannot spontaneously unwind: the transition $w=4\to w=0$ requires
  crossing an infinite energy barrier in the $M\to\infty$ limit.
  Particle stability is a consequence of topology, not of any protective symmetry
  imposed by hand.

\item \textbf{The kink mass is the field scale, not the particle mass.}
  The BPS kink mass is $\Mkink = (8/49)m_\tau = 290.10$~MeV (\CatAL).
  This sets the strong-interaction energy scale.
  The physical lepton masses ($m_e = 0.511$~MeV, $m_\mu = 105.7$~MeV,
  $m_\tau = 1776.86$~MeV) come from the GTE orbit cascade arithmetic at
  Level~1 --- not directly from the BPS energy.
  Distinguishing these two is essential: the kink mass tells us the
  \emph{scale} of the substrate; the orbit cascade tells us the
  \emph{hierarchy} of the particles living on that substrate.

\item \textbf{Elementary particles vs.\ composites.}
  A single BPS kink is one elementary particle (one electron, one quark, etc.).
  Composite particles --- protons, neutrons, pions --- are bound states of multiple
  kinks, exactly as they are bound states of quarks in QCD.
  The kink is not a point object, but it is also not a spatially compact field
  envelope: \S\ref{sec:multikink_fock} proves that any winding-carrying $\PHIMDL$
  configuration in three spatial dimensions is necessarily extended (domain-wall-like)
  and that mass, charge, spin, and stability are realized instead as a normalizable
  Fock-space excitation within the kink's topological superselection sector, certified
  by that extended classical background via the Algebraic Lifting Theorem (\CatAL).
  Lattice cells (Level~1 language) do not appear at Level~2; the Level-2 kink is this
  Fock-space object living on $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$, not a localized classical profile.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{The Worked Example: The Electron}

To make the two-level picture concrete, we trace the electron through both levels.

\textbf{Level~1:} The electron corresponds to the gen$_1$ beable with
orbit configuration $[1,5,2,2,1]$ in $\ZS^5$.
Its algebraic invariants are: $W_B = 4$ (SM interaction winding, CatAL via orbit arithmetic),
GoE stability (zero predecessors, \lean{fmdl\_gen1\_is\allowbreak\_garden\_of\_eden}, CatAL),
and fermionic statistics (ord$(4) = 3$ in $\mathbb{Z}_7^*$,
\lean{gte\_winding\_identifies\_charged\_fermions}, CatAL).
The charge follows from the formula: $Q = (4-7)/3 = -1$
(\lean{gte\_charge\_is\_linear\_projection}, CatAL).

\textbf{Level~2:} The electron's quantum numbers are certified by a BPS kink
background in $\PHIMDL$ with winding number $w=4$, connecting the fourth vacuum of the
$\ZS$ potential to the zeroth; the electron itself is the normalizable Fock-space
excitation this background certifies in the $w=4$ superselection sector
(\S\ref{sec:multikink_fock}).
Its charge is $Q = -1$ (from the same formula, now applied to the winding sector), its spin
$J = 1/2$ follows from the Lean-certified exchange statistics~\mbox{(\lean{gte\_triple\_kink\_exchange\_statistics}, \CatAL)}, and its mass
$m_e = 0.511$~MeV from the Level-1 orbit cascade ($N_{\rm eff}=73$ seed,
Chapter~\ref{chap:mathsubstrate} \S\ref{sec:gte_cascade}; worked physically in
\S\ref{sec:nvalues_to_masses}, \CatA).
The sector is topologically stable: to annihilate the electron requires pairing it
with a positron ($w=3$), since $4 + 3 = 7 \equiv 0 \pmod{7}$ restores the vacuum.

\xrightarrow{\lean{algebraic\_lifting\_theorem}\;(\CatAL)}\\

\xrightarrow{\text{orbit cascade}}

\subsection*{Why the Two-Level Description Is Essential}

If we described particles only at Level~1 (CA orbit classes), the theory would
seem to lack a physical realization.
If we described them only at Level~2 (kinks), we would seem to have abandoned
the algebraic certificate that makes the quantum numbers provable.
The two-level description is essential:
Level~1 proves existence and certifies quantum numbers;
Level~2 provides the physical realization with exact masses, Lorentz invariance, and
a complete quantum field theory.
The Algebraic Lifting Theorem is the formal statement that the two levels
refer to the same physical object.

\section{The \texorpdfstring{$\Phi_{\mathrm{MDL}}$}{Phi-MDL} Lagrangian}
\label{sec:lagrangian}

The $\PHIMDL$ field is a $\mathbb{Z}_7$-symmetric Klein-Gordon gauge field on Minkowski
spacetime.
(The Level~1 certificate and Level~2 field law are displayed side by side in the ``Two Laws'' box in the \nameref{chap:glance} chapter.)
Before writing down the equations, let us describe the physical picture they encode.

The field $\PHIMDL$ can sit in any of seven degenerate ground states (vacua), equally
spaced around the unit circle in field space.
In empty space, the field sits in one of these seven vacua --- it costs zero energy.
A kink is a region where the field has permanently shifted to a different vacuum; it
is the classical background that certifies a particle's quantum numbers
(\S\ref{sec:multikink_fock} establishes precisely what the particle itself is).
The potential energy landscape is like seven evenly-spaced valleys arranged in a ring:
to move from one valley to another, you must climb over a ridge.
The kink is the smooth interpolation between two adjacent valleys.

\subsection*{The Lagrangian}

The $\PHIMDL$ Lagrangian density is \cite{SpivackPhiMDLField,SpivackCompleteness}:

\begin{equation}
\mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_\mu\Phi)^2 - V(\Phi),
\qquad
V(\Phi) = \frac{m_\varphi^2}{49}\bigl(1 - \cos 7\Phi\bigr).
\label{eq:phimdl_lagrangian}
\end{equation}

The kinetic term $\tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_\mu\Phi)^2$ is the standard Lorentz-invariant
Klein-Gordon kinetic energy.
The potential $V(\Phi)$ is a $\ZS$-symmetric sine-Gordon potential with seven degenerate
minima at $\Phi_k = 2\pi k/7$ for $k\in\{0,1,\ldots,6\}$, all with $V(\Phi_k) = 0$.
The factor $1/49$ ensures that the curvature $V''(\Phi_k) = m_\varphi^2$ --- the mass
parameter equals the field's oscillation frequency around each vacuum.
The coefficient $7$ in $\cos 7\Phi$ enforces the $\ZS$ symmetry:
$V(\Phi + 2\pi k/7) = V(\Phi)$ for all $k\in\mathbb{Z}_7$.

This is not a free scalar field.
It is an exactly integrable, non-perturbative field theory --- the $\ZS$ sine-Gordon
model --- with an infinite tower of conserved charges, exact BPS solitons, and a
$\mathbb{Z}_7$ superselection rule.
Its richness is precisely what makes it capable of encoding all of SM physics
in a single object.

\subsection*{The Self-Consistency Condition: $m_\varphi = m_\tau$}

The mass parameter $m_\varphi$ is not a free parameter.
It is fixed by the Self-Consistency Condition (SCC): the theory must be self-consistent
in the sense that the single dimensionful parameter equals the mass of the heaviest
stable composite in the leptonic (colour-singlet, pure $\ZS$) sector.

The argument runs as follows \cite{SpivackPhiMDLField}:
(1) The Frobenius decomposition $F_{21} = \ZS\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_3$ shows that the
leptonic sector inherits only the $\ZS$ kernel, with no $\mathbb{Z}_3$ colour charge.
(2) The three-generation orbit closure (certified \CatAL) terminates the cascade at
gen$_3$; no fourth generation exists.
(3) MDL minimality forbids unused dimensionful capacity: $m_\varphi$ must equal an
observable mass, and the unique candidate is the heaviest lepton in the
three-generation cascade.
(4) The GTE cascade (developed in full in
Chapter~\ref{chap:mathsubstrate}, \S\ref{sec:gte_cascade}) gives lepton $N$-values
$\{73,42,275\}$ for gen$_1$, gen$_2$,
gen$_3$; the heaviest ($b=275$) is the tau lepton.
Therefore:
\[
m_\varphi = m_\tau = 1776.86\text{ MeV}.
\]

\subsection*{The $F_{21}$ Gauge Sector}
\label{subsec:f21_gauge_sector}

The complete Lagrangian includes the $F_{21} = \ZS\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_3$ gauge structure.
The abelianization $F_{21}^{\rm ab} = \mathbb{Z}_3$ provides the colour gauge field
$\chi$ with coupling constant $\varepsilon$.
This coupling is fully derived from $F_{21}$ representation theory
(vertex coupling, \CatA\ and \CatAL; $\varepsilon$ derivation,
\CatAL): there are no free coupling constants.

The covariant derivative for the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ gauge field is
$D_\mu = \partial_\mu + ig\chi_\mu$, and the gauge coupling term in the Lagrangian
takes the form $\varepsilon|\Phi|^2(D_\mu\chi)^2$.
Every coefficient is derived from GTE orbit arithmetic;
$\varepsilon$ from $F_{21}$ group theory; $m_\varphi$ from the SCC.
The remaining coupling-sector parameters complete the zero-free-parameter
accounting at their honest claim levels: the gauge coupling at the EFT
boundary is the Sylow rational $e^2(\Lambda_{\GTE}) = 7/2$ (\CatAD-consistency
with the PDG-run $\overline{\rm MS}$ coupling at the $1.3$--$1.5\sigma$ level
after the non-perturbative kink-broadening correction; the comparison is
scheme-aware, see Ch.~\ref{chap:forces}), and the $\chi$-sector mass parameter
is $g = m_\varphi = m_\tau$ (\CatB, the zero-new-scale completion: the $\chi$
and $\varphi$ sectors share the single derived mass scale in canonical
sine-Gordon normalization).
The $\PHIMDL$ Lagrangian has zero free parameters \cite{SpivackPhiMDLField}.

A scope note on the $\ZS$ vacuum degeneracy: the equal-kink-mass and
vacuum-degeneracy theorems of the $\PHIMDL$ potential hold exactly in the
pure-$\varphi$ sector (the Lean certificates are hypothesis-scoped to
$\ZS$-periodic observables).  $V_{\rm coupling}$ is not $\ZS$-shift invariant:
the seven vacua carry inequivalent $\chi$-sector kinetic normalizations
$Z_k = 1 + 2\varepsilon\varphi_k^2$, which distinguishes the vacuum labels in
the full Lagrangian.  This distinction is physically consequential --- it is
the mechanism that annihilates the cosmological domain-wall foam and selects
the unique vacuum $k = 0$ (Ch.~\ref{chap:cosmology},
§\ref{sec:defect_cosmology}) --- while leaving the kink mass spectrum
unaffected today (the dressing from $V_{\rm coupling}$ vanishes in the $k = 0$
vacuum, where $\varphi^2 = 0$).

\section{BPS Kinks: The Physical Particles}
\label{sec:bps_kinks}

A kink is a field configuration that interpolates between two adjacent vacua.
To visualize it: in the ring of seven valleys described above, start at valley~0,
and smoothly transition to valley~1 (or 2, or 3, or 4, or 6) over some spatial region.
The field stays near valley~0 for $x\ll 0$, transitions through the ridge, and
sits at the new vacuum for $x\gg 0$.
That transition region is the kink.
Its spatial width is set by the inverse mass $1/m_\varphi \approx 0.111$~fm.
\emph{A note on what follows:} this section develops the kink as a genuine
one-dimensional profile, which is exact in the $1{+}1$D reduction analyzed here.
\S\ref{sec:multikink_fock} proves that the physical, $3{+}1$D winding-carrying
configuration is necessarily extended rather than compact, and that the particle
itself is a Fock-space excitation certified by that background. The mass, charge,
and stability results derived below from this profile are unaffected by that
refinement --- they are exactly the quantities the Algebraic Lifting Theorem
carries over to the Fock-space particle.

\subsection*{The BPS Kink Profile}

The static kink solution connecting adjacent vacua is \cite{SpivackPhiMDLField}:
\begin{equation}
\Phi_{\rm kink}(x) = \frac{4}{7}\arctan\!\bigl(e^{m_\varphi x}\bigr),
\qquad
\frac{d\Phi_{\rm kink}}{dx} = \frac{2m_\varphi}{7}\,\mathrm{sech}(m_\varphi x).
\label{eq:kink_profile}
\end{equation}

The kink center is at $x=0$.
The field approaches vacuum~0 as $x\to-\infty$ and vacuum~1 as $x\to+\infty$.
The derivative $d\Phi/dx$ is a sech function peaked at the kink center with width $\sim 1/m_\varphi$:
in this $1{+}1$D profile, the energy density is concentrated in a region of femtometer
scale (comparable to the proton radius, $\sim 0.84$~fm) --- the kink's characteristic
length scale, not the physical particle's spatial extent (which, per
\S\ref{sec:multikink_fock}, is that of an extended, non-compact background).

\subsection*{BPS Saturation and the Energy Bound}

The \textbf{BPS condition} is the saturation of the Bogomolny energy bound:
\begin{equation}
\frac{d\Phi}{dx} = \sqrt{2V(\Phi)}.
\label{eq:bps_condition}
\end{equation}

A solution satisfying this first-order equation automatically satisfies the full
second-order equation of motion, and achieves the \emph{minimum possible energy}
for its topological class.
One can verify directly that the profile~(\ref{eq:kink_profile}) satisfies~(\ref{eq:bps_condition}):
inserting the kink profile into the right-hand side and applying a trigonometric identity
reproduces the left-hand side exactly.

\textbf{Physical meaning:} A BPS-saturated kink is a ``no-pressure'' solution with
$T_{11} = 0$ (zero longitudinal stress).
It is exactly stable against perturbation: any local deformation increases its energy.
BPS kinks are the minimum-energy representatives of their topological sector, which is why
they certify the physical particles as Fock-space excitations
(\S\ref{sec:multikink_fock}).

\subsection*{The Kink Mass}

The kink mass is the total energy of the kink configuration:
\begin{equation}
\Mkink
= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\!\left[\tfrac{1}{2}\Phi'^2 + V(\Phi)\right]dx
= \frac{4m_\varphi^2}{49}\!\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\!\mathrm{sech}^2(m_\varphi x)\,dx
= \frac{8m_\varphi}{49}
= \frac{8\,m_\tau}{49}.
\label{eq:kink_mass}
\end{equation}

Using $m_\tau = 1776.86$~MeV and the SCC identification $m_\varphi = m_\tau$:

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,
  title={Result: BPS Kink Mass (\CatAL)}]
\[
\Mkink = \frac{8}{49}\,m_\tau = \frac{8}{49}\times 1776.86\text{ MeV} = 290.10\text{ MeV}.
\]
Zero free parameters.
This is the energy of a single-step topological excitation of $\PHIMDL$
--- the scale at which the strong interaction operates.

\smallskip\noindent
\textbf{Lean cert:} \lean{mkink\_from\_scc} (\CatAL, \texttt{GUTStructure.lean}, ugp-lean,
zero sorry);
\lean{phimdl\_kink\_masses\_equal} (\CatAL, zero sorry): all non-vacuum sectors have equal BPS mass.
\end{tcolorbox}

The equal-mass result deserves emphasis.
The $\ZS$ symmetry of the potential guarantees that every inter-vacuum transition
$k\to k{+}1$ has the same potential ridge height $\max V = 2m_\varphi^2/49$,
and therefore the same BPS bound.
All six non-vacuum kink sectors have the same mass $\Mkink$, regardless of winding number.
This is a non-trivial prediction: a theory with an arbitrary potential of lower symmetry
would generically have different kink masses for different sectors.

\subsection*{PSC-Admissible Sectors and the Standard Model Particle Assignments}

The $\ZS$ potential has seven vacuum states and thus six non-trivial kink sectors
($w \in \{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$).
Not all six are physically admissible.
PSC-admissibility (forced by the dark-mirror structure of $F_{21}$) restricts to
five sectors, eliminating $\{1,5\}$ (the dark-sector mirror partners, not stable
asymptotic states in the SM branch) \cite{SpivackPhiMDLField,SpivackCompleteness}.
The resulting five sectors $\{0,2,3,4,6\}$ map exactly to the SM particle classes.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}cclcc@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Winding $w$} & \textbf{Charge $Q = w_{\rm c}/3$} & \textbf{Particle type} &
\textbf{Statistics} & \textbf{Cert} \\
\midrule
$0$ & $0$ & Vacuum / photon / neutrino & bosonic & \CatAL \\
$2$ & $+2/3$ & Up-type quarks ($u,c,t$) & fermionic & \CatAL \\
$3$ & $+1$ & $W^+$ boson / positron & bosonic & \CatAL \\
$4$ & $-1$ & Charged leptons ($e^-,\mu^-,\tau^-$), $W^-$ & fermionic & \CatAL \\
$6$ & $-1/3$ & Down-type quarks ($d,s,b$) & fermionic & \CatAL \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent
The charge $Q = w_{\rm c}/3$ uses the centred representative
$w_{\rm c} = w$ for $w\leq 3$ and $w_{\rm c} = w-7$ for $w\geq 4$,
so that $w=4$ gives $Q = (4{-}7)/3 = -1$ (electron)
and $w=6$ gives $Q = (6{-}7)/3 = -1/3$ (down quark).
All charge assignments are algebraic consequences of the GTE polynomial;
no additional assignment rule is needed.

\textbf{Lean cert:} \lean{psc\_admissible\_sectors} (\CatAL, zero sorry, ugp-lean):
$\{0,2,3,4,6\}$ are the PSC-admissible sectors.

\subsection*{Three Generations from Three Orbit Types}

The three SM fermion generations correspond to the three non-vacuum orbit types
of the $\ZS^5$ ring under $f_{\rm MDL}$.
In 3+1D (three-tape architecture), particles are described by uniform winding triples
$(w,w,w)$ for $w$ in the PSC-admissible set --- all three spatial tapes carry the
same winding, ensuring rotational ($S_3$) invariance.
The generation index (first, second, third) is the orbit position within each
species class.
All three generations of charged leptons have $w=4$; the distinction between $e$, $\mu$,
$\tau$ is their generation index and the corresponding $b$-value from the GTE cascade,
not their winding number.

\noindent
Three generations arise from one field \cite{SpivackCMCA,SpivackThreeTapeCMCA}.
No additional field is needed for each generation.

\subsection*{Topological Stability and Superselection}

The topological charge is:
\[
Q_{\rm top} = \frac{7}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\Phi'(x)\,dx
= \frac{7}{2\pi}\bigl[\Phi(+\infty)-\Phi(-\infty)\bigr] \in \mathbb{Z}_7.
\]

This charge is exactly conserved: changing it requires the field to globally
rewind, which costs infinite energy.
The $\ZS$ superselection rule follows:
$\mathcal{H} = \bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_7}\mathcal{H}_k$,
with no quantum tunneling between sectors
(tunneling amplitude $\sim e^{-S_E}$ with $S_E\approx 0.163$~GeV~$\gg 1$ in natural units).
Particle identity is an exact quantum number, not a statistical tendency.

\begin{openprob}
The kink width $1/m_\varphi \approx 0.111$~fm matches the QCD scale.
The derivation of the physical lepton mass $m_e = 0.511$~MeV as an energy of a specific
kink composite configuration in the three-tape $\PHIMDL$ field theory
--- going beyond the Level-1 orbit cascade --- is an open problem in the GTE programme.
The connection is structurally understood via the orbit cascade (\CatA) but has not
yet been derived directly from the $\PHIMDL$ Lagrangian.
\end{openprob}

\subsection*{The Kink Fusion Category}

The kink superselection sectors carry $\mathbb{Z}_7$ topological winding, and their
fusion is additive: $w_1 \otimes w_2 = w_1 + w_2 \pmod{7}$
\mbox{(\lean{kink\_fusion\_rule\_additive\_mod7}, \CatAL)}.  The resulting fusion
category is the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ Dijkgraaf--Witten \emph{abelian} modular tensor
category: all quantum dimensions equal $1$ and the braiding phases are
$e^{2\pi i\,ab/7}$ \mbox{(\lean{kink\_category\_is\_abelian\_dw}, \CatAL)}.  The
PSC-admissible restriction to $\{0,2,3,4,6\}$ is not a closed sub-MTC --- fusion can
produce the dark-sector classes $\{1,5\}$.  Consequently \GTE\ is \emph{not} a
universal topological quantum computer via Fibonacci-anyon braiding: the
Fibonacci-anyon hypothesis is definitively excluded by three independent
discriminators (the fusion is abelian, not the Fibonacci rule
$\tau \otimes \tau = 1 \oplus \tau$; the object count is $7$, not $2$; and all quantum
dimensions are $1$, not $\varphi$).  The only connection to the Fibonacci MTC is the
polynomial kinship $m(-x) = x^2 - x - 1$ (§\ref{sec:master_quadratic}); the master
polynomial is the common algebraic ancestor of both the GTE vacuum dynamics and the
Fibonacci MTC.

\GTE\ implements quantum computation by a distinct mechanism: transputation.  Each
adjudication event is a quantum computation --- an MDL-optimal selection among the 5
PSC-admissible sector alternatives, governed by the $[D]$-measure axioms $D_1$--$D_5$
(\S\ref{sec:transputation}).  The computation is not topologically protected via
non-abelian braiding but is informationally protected via MDL minimality: the
adjudicator selects the Born-rule outcome, which is the unique minimum of the
$[D]$-functional.  Fault-tolerant quantum memory is
available via the $\ZS$ Dijkgraaf--Witten abelian toric code at code distance $d = 7$;
universal topological quantum computation would require activating the $F_{21}$ gauge
holonomy in 2+1D, beyond the present framework.

\section[Exact Multi-Kink Dynamics and Particle Characterization]{Exact Multi-Kink Dynamics and the Definitive Particle Characterization}
\label{sec:multikink_fock}

Two questions remain after \S\ref{sec:bps_kinks}'s single-kink analysis.
First: is the pure-$\varphi$ theory computable beyond one particle --- what happens
when many kinks interact, and does the theory support the annihilation/creation
phenomenology expected of a genuine particle theory?\footnote{The figures in
this section are still frames from a live, browser-based, interactive
implementation of the $\PHIMDL$ 1+1D, 2+1D, and (static, illustrative)
2+1+1D extended-structure views discussed below, available at
\url{https://novaspivack.github.io/ugp-physics/visualizations/phimdl_kink_dynamics/}.
The application lets a reader reproduce every simulation in this section
directly (drag-to-place kinks, preset initial conditions, adjustable
dynamics), and runs entirely client-side with no installation required.}
Second, and more fundamental: exactly what is the spatially-resolved, Level-2
content of a kink?
\S\ref{sec:two_levels} established that a kink's \emph{quantum numbers} are certified
algebraically and lifted to Level~2 by the Algebraic Lifting Theorem, but left the
spatial question --- is a kink a compact, localized classical object in three
dimensions, or something else? --- as an implicit gap.
This section closes both questions completely: the pure sector is exactly solvable
to arbitrary particle number; a general theorem proves that no compact, finite-energy,
topologically-protected classical particle exists in three spatial dimensions; and a
machine-checked theorem identifies exactly what a $\PHIMDL$ particle is instead.

\subsection*{The Pure-\texorpdfstring{$\varphi$}{phi} Sector Is Exactly Integrable}

The pure-$\varphi$ Lagrangian (Eq.~\eqref{eq:kink_profile}'s parent theory,
$\mathcal{L} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial\Phi)^2 - (m_\varphi^2/49)(1-\cos 7\Phi)$) is related
to the standard sine-Gordon model by the exact rescaling $\psi = 7\Phi$:
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{L}[\Phi] \;=\; \frac{1}{49}\,\mathcal{L}_{\rm SG}[\psi;\,m_\varphi]
\;=\; \frac{1}{49}\Bigl[\tfrac{1}{2}(\partial\psi)^2 - m_\varphi^2(1-\cos\psi)\Bigr].
\label{eq:z7_sg_rescaling}
\end{equation}
This is an exact symbolic identity (verified to zero residual with a computer-algebra
system): the equation of motion $\Phi_{tt}-\Phi_{xx}+(m_\varphi^2/7)\sin 7\Phi=0$ is
identical, term by term, to the standard sine-Gordon equation
$\psi_{tt}-\psi_{xx}+m_\varphi^2\sin\psi=0$ under $\psi=7\Phi$; only the overall energy
normalization changes ($E_\Phi = E_{\rm SG}/49$).

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,
  title={Result: The Pure-$\varphi$ Sector Is Standard Sine-Gordon (\CatAD)}]
Every exact multi-soliton solution of the standard, integrable sine-Gordon model
carries over to the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ pure-$\varphi$ sector under $\Phi=\psi_{\rm SG}/7$,
with energies rescaled by $1/49$.
In particular, in GTE normalization (kink amplitude $2\pi/7$):
\begin{align}
\Phi_{\rm KK}(x,t) &= \frac{4}{7}\arctan\!\left[\frac{v\sinh(\gamma m_\varphi x)}{\cosh(\gamma m_\varphi v t)}\right]
&&\text{(kink--kink)},\\
\Phi_{\rm KA}(x,t) &= \frac{4}{7}\arctan\!\left[\frac{\sinh(\gamma m_\varphi v t)}{v\cosh(\gamma m_\varphi x)}\right]
&&\text{(kink--antikink)},\\
\Phi_{\rm br}(x,t) &= \frac{4}{7}\arctan\!\left[\frac{\sqrt{1-\omega^2}}{\omega}\,
\frac{\sin(\omega m_\varphi t)}{\cosh(\sqrt{1-\omega^2}\,m_\varphi x)}\right]
&&\text{(breather)},
\label{eq:breather_exact}
\end{align}
with $\gamma=(1-v^2)^{-1/2}$.
Each satisfies the $\Phi_{\rm MDL}$ equation of motion exactly, verified symbolically
to residual $<10^{-51}$ at 50-digit precision, and reproduced by direct leapfrog
integration of the field equation at second-order convergence with energy conserved
to $\sim10^{-5}$ relative and radiated energy $<3\times10^{-8}$ of the total (i.e.\
genuinely elastic, integrable collisions).
The asymptotic scattering phase shift is $\delta=\ln(1/v)/\gamma$, matching the
direct numerical trajectories to $\leq10^{-6}$.
The breather's mass--frequency relation is exact:
$M_{\rm br}(\omega) = 2\Mkink\sqrt{1-\omega^2}$, confirmed by direct energy
integration to $10^{-10}$--$10^{-12}$ relative error; it is a genuine, rigorously
non-radiating (checked over 40 oscillation periods to the discretization floor),
time-periodic, spatially-localized classical solution --- but it carries zero net
$\ZS$ winding (a bound kink--antikink pair), so it is a charge-neutral composite,
not a candidate elementary particle.
\end{tcolorbox}

method \cite{Hirota1972SineGordon}: writing
$\tau=\sum_{\mu\in\{0,1\}^N}\prod_j\bigl(i\epsilon_j e^{\eta_j}\bigr)^{\mu_j}

$\eta_j = \cosh\theta_j\,(x-x_{0,j}) - \sinh\theta_j\, t$, the GTE-normalized field is
$\Phi = (4/7)\arg\tau$.
This closed form was verified against the equation of motion to $5\times10^{-14}$
(analytic derivatives, mixed kink/antikink configurations through $N=8$) and against
direct PDE evolution ($N=6$, distinct velocities and charges) to $7\times10^{-4}$ at
second-order convergence; the total energy is exactly additive,
$E=\sum_i\gamma_i\Mkink$ --- there is no binding energy in the pure sector.

A direct many-kink simulation (24 elementary kinks/antikinks, random velocities,
net winding $+2$, evolved over 400 natural time units) confirms this analytically:
$\ZS$ winding is conserved to $8.9\times10^{-16}$ (machine precision), energy drifts
by only $1.1\times10^{-6}$, and every one of $\sim40$ close encounters is a
transmission with the analytic phase shift --- \textbf{the pure sector never
annihilates}; kinks and antikinks pass through one another at every velocity tested.
This many-body behaviour, together with the exact $N$-soliton closed form, means the
pure-$\varphi$ sector's kink dynamics at arbitrary particle number is fully solved
in closed form (\CatAD\ substrate; \CatA\ numerical confirmation).

\subsection*{Non-Integrable Corrections: The Annihilation Channel}

The pure-$\varphi$ sector's perfect transmissivity is a consequence of integrability,
which is broken by the physical $F_{21}$ gauge coupling
$\varepsilon|\Phi|^2(D_\mu\chi)^2$ of \S\ref{subsec:f21_gauge_sector}.
Deriving the coupled $\Phi$--$\chi$ equations of motion symbolically shows the coupling
is purely \emph{kinetic}: it modifies $\chi$'s effective metric,
$Z(\Phi)=1+2\varepsilon\Phi^2$, but carries no source current for $\chi$, so
$\chi\equiv0$ is an \emph{exact} classical solution for every classical $\Phi(x,t)$ ---
moving kinks, kink--antikink pairs, or a many-kink gas alike (\CatA, verified both
symbolically and by direct residual evaluation).
Quantum corrections from this coupling (Bogoliubov pair production, a $\chi$-Casimir
force between kink--antikink pairs) are computable and small: pair production is
exponentially suppressed for collision velocities below $\sim0.7c$, and the derived
$\chi$-Casimir kink-mass dressing at typical separations is $\lesssim0.1\%\,\Mkink$ ---
too weak to produce a capture window at accessible velocities.
The physical $\varepsilon=7/9$ coupling is therefore \emph{structurally protected}
against non-integrable annihilation at practical kink velocities.

The qualitative annihilation-via-radiation mechanism generic to non-integrable
kink--antikink dynamics --- capture into a radiating bound state below a threshold
relative velocity, with the radiated energy fraction growing with perturbation
strength --- is nonetheless a genuine feature of this class of field theory, and is
illustrated here with a symmetry-class proxy perturbation (a $\ZS$-degeneracy-preserving
double-sine-Gordon term, \emph{not} a first-principles calculation of the derived
$\varepsilon$-coupling's effect): kink--antikink collisions below a threshold velocity
capture into a radiating bion, converting a growing fraction of the collision energy
into outgoing radiation as the perturbation strength increases, while faster
collisions remain transmissive (\CatA, illustrative proxy model only).
This is the physically correct qualitative picture of particle annihilation in this
field content; its physical rate is set by the derived, structurally suppressed
$\varepsilon$-coupling above, not by the proxy's numerical values.

\subsection*{The General \texorpdfstring{$D\geq2$}{D>=2} Winding-Localization No-Go Theorem}
\label{subsec:nogo}

The single-scalar $\PHIMDL$ field extruded to $3{+}1$D has no static, spatially
localized soliton: a single kink profile extended along the transverse directions is
an infinite planar domain wall of tension $\sigma=(8/49)m_\varphi^3$ (natural units),
whose energy grows without bound as the transverse area increases --- an instance of
Derrick's classical no-go for static solitons in $D\geq2$ \cite{Derrick1964}.
This raises the natural question of whether some \emph{other} construction ---
a differently shaped wall, a genuinely time-dependent configuration, a
lower-codimension defect, or a gauge-sector (hedgehog-type) mechanism --- could
still support a compact, finite-energy, winding-carrying particle.
The following theorem settles this completely and rigorously, for every ansatz.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!55!black,
  title={\textbf{Theorem: No Compact Winding-Carrying $\PHIMDL$ Configuration in $D\geq2$} (\CatAD)}]
\small
\textbf{Topological part.}
Let $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^D\to\mathbb{R}$ ($D\geq2$) be continuous, and suppose its limit
as $|\mathbf{x}|\to\infty$ is independent of direction --- i.e.\ $\Phi$ approaches the
same vacuum value along every ray to spatial infinity.
Then the $\ZS$ winding charge of $\Phi$ is exactly zero.
\smallskip

\noindent\textit{Proof.} The restriction of $\Phi$ to a large sphere of radius $R$
converges, by hypothesis, to the constant map into the discrete seven-point vacuum
set $\{2\pi k/7 : k=0,\dots,6\}$ as $R\to\infty$.
Since $S^{D-1}$ is connected for $D\geq2$ and the continuous image of a connected
space is connected, and the only connected subsets of a discrete space are single
points, the boundary map on a sufficiently large sphere must itself be constant.
A configuration whose boundary data at infinity is a single point cannot thread
through more than one vacuum, so its net winding is zero.
$\blacksquare$
\smallskip

\noindent\textbf{Corollary.} Any $\PHIMDL$ configuration carrying nonzero winding in
$D\geq2$ must therefore have a \emph{direction-dependent} limit at spatial infinity ---
it is necessarily extended (wall-like), never asymptotically spherically symmetric.
This single elementary argument subsumes, as special cases, the Derrick no-go above
(any static soliton has a direction-independent limit), the gauge-sector hedgehog
obstruction ($\pi_2(\ZS)=0$ forbids a monopole-type boundary map), and the
nonexistence of a genuinely 3D time-periodic (``oscillon''-type) winding-carrying
solution, consistent with the generalized (higher-dimensional) extension of the
radiative-decay mechanism first identified for near-breather configurations of
nonlinear Klein--Gordon equations \cite{SegurKruskal1987}: no symmetry class, static
or time-dependent, evades it.
\smallskip

\noindent\textbf{Energy part.} Granting that a winding-carrying configuration must be
extended, no shape achieves \emph{finite} energy while remaining topologically
protected. Flat or conical walls diverge as (transverse extent)$^2$. Pinched walls
--- surfaces of revolution $\rho(z) = c\,z^p$, $p\in[0,1)$, shrinking cross-section as
$z\to\infty$ --- reduce the divergence rate to (extent)$^{p+1}$ but diverge for every
tested $p\geq0$ (confirmed analytically and by direct three-dimensional energy
integration). Codimension-2 (string/vortex) defects are excluded on two independent
grounds: a vortex-loop reading is impossible outright, since a single-valued real
scalar field has $\oint_{\rm loop}d\Phi=0$ identically around any closed loop
(Stokes' theorem for an exact one-form); and the alternative cylindrical-tube reading
is topologically \emph{unprotected} --- a Derrick-type scaling analysis,
$E(\lambda)=I_{\rm kin}+I_{\rm pot}\lambda^2$, shows the energy decreases
monotonically as the core radius $\lambda\to0$, with zero energy barrier, unlike the
genuine 1D kink whose two vacuum boundaries are topologically disconnected.
\end{tcolorbox}

\noindent\textbf{Conclusion.}
A classical, spatially-compact, finite-energy, topologically-protected particle does
not exist in the single-real-scalar $\PHIMDL$ field --- for any ansatz, symmetry
class, or defect codimension tested.
This is a proven impossibility, not an unconstructed gap: every concretely realizable
classical configuration carrying nonzero $\ZS$ winding in three spatial dimensions is
an extended, domain-wall-like structure whose energy diverges with its transverse
extent.
\emph{Level framing:} this theorem is a Level-2 statement about the classical
$\PHIMDL$ continuum field (no CMCA algebraic content enters the proof); its
consequence for what a $\PHIMDL$ particle physically \emph{is} is drawn next.

\subsection*{The Definitive Particle Characterization: Fock-Space Excitations in Superselection Sectors}

The theorem above rules out a literal reading of ``kink = compact 3D lump.''
It does \emph{not} threaten anything established about particle mass, charge,
spin-statistics, generation count, or stability: every one of those results
(\S\ref{sec:two_levels}, \S\ref{sec:bps_kinks}) is a Level-1 algebraic or
orbit-cascade fact --- the mass comes from the GTE cascade, the charge from the
linear projection $Q=w_{\rm centered}/3$, the statistics from the multiplicative
order of $w$ in $\ZS^*$, and the stability from superselection non-mixing --- none of
which was ever shown to require, and none of which in fact requires, the classical
compact configuration the theorem above excludes.
What remained open was the precise \emph{physical} realization of a kink's quantum
numbers at Level~2, given that a compact classical profile is unavailable.
The following machine-checked theorem supplies it.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,
  title={Theorem: $\PHIMDL$ Fock-Space Particle Realization (\CatAL, zero sorry, zero new axioms)}]
For every PSC-admissible $\ZS$ winding sector $w\in\{0,2,3,4,6\}$, there exists a
normalizable one-particle Fock-sector state (or, equivalently, a unit-weight
normalized sector amplitude on the certified beable partition) carrying exactly the
winding, color, and generation quantum numbers certified at Level~1.
Every $[D]$-weighted physical beable inherits this Fock-space lift in its winding
sector via the Algebraic Lifting Theorem --- this Fock state \emph{is} the physical
realization the Lifting Theorem promises, constructed using only the algebraic Fock
layer, with no spatially-compact classical field profile entering the construction.

\smallskip\noindent
\textbf{Lean certs} (module \lean{PhiMDLFockSpaceParticles.lean}, ugp-lean):\\
\lean{psc\_admissible\_sector\_has\_normalizable\_fock\_state} --- every PSC-admissible
sector has a normalizable Fock-sector state.\\
\lean{fock\_state\_realizes\_algebraic\_lifting} --- every $[D]$-weighted beable's
Fock lift realizes \lean{algebraic\_lifting\_theorem}.\\
\lean{phimdl\_fock\_particle\_master\_bundle} --- master bundle: sector totality,
lifting, algebraic-only construction, and the gen$_1$ mass/Garden-of-Eden stability
result of \S\ref{sec:bps_kinks}, all in one certified statement.
\end{tcolorbox}

\noindent\textbf{The correct, certain characterization:} a $\PHIMDL$ particle is a
second-quantized Fock-space excitation within a $\ZS$ topological superselection
sector.
The classical background that certifies a sector's existence via the Algebraic
Lifting Theorem is \emph{extended} --- an infinite planar domain wall in the simplest
realization --- never spatially compact.
Mass, charge, spin-statistics, generation count, and stability are Level-1
algebraic/orbit-cascade facts realized in this Fock-space picture; none of them ever
secretly depended on the classical compact lump the no-go theorem above rules out.
This resolves \S\ref{sec:two_levels}'s open spatial-structure question definitively,
without weakening any certified particle-identity claim in this monograph.
\emph{Level framing:} this theorem is the Level-1$\to$Level-2 bridge statement ---
the quantum numbers are certified at Level~1 (the algebraic certificate); their
physical realization as a normalizable Fock-space state is the Level-2 content the
Algebraic Lifting Theorem supplies.

\section{\texorpdfstring{$F_{21}$}{F21} vs.\ SU(3): Why the Frobenius Group Is Forced}
\label{sec:f21}

Standard QCD uses $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ as the colour gauge group.
Why does GTE use $F_{21} = \ZS\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_3$ instead?
The answer is MDL.

\subsection*{Why MDL Forces $F_{21}$ Over $\mathrm{SU}(3)$}

$\mathrm{SU}(3)$ is a continuous Lie group with infinitely many generators.
Postulating it as the colour gauge group costs many bits: you must specify that the
gauge group is $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ (as opposed to $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ for other $N$,
$\mathrm{U}(N)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(N)$, etc.), the coupling constant $g_s$, the
Casimir structure, and the representation assignments for each fermion species.

$F_{21} = \ZS\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_3$ is the unique non-abelian group of order~21.
It has only 21 elements and is completely specified by its semidirect product structure.
The Frobenius prime identity certifies its arithmetic uniqueness:

\begin{equation}
|F_{21}| = |\ZS| = |\mathbb{Z}_3|^2 - |\mathbb{Z}_3| + 1 = 9 - 3 + 1 = 7.
\label{eq:frobenius_prime}
\end{equation}

This identity --- that 7 is the unique prime of the form $p^2 - p + 1$ for $p=3$ ---
certifies that $\ZS$ and $\mathbb{Z}_3$ form a Frobenius pair.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,
  title={Result: $F_{21}$ Is MDL-Forced (\CatA\ and \CatAL)}]
$F_{21} = \ZS\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_3$ is the MDL-minimal group with the required properties:

\subsection*{Eisenstein Arithmetic: The Residue-Field Model of $F_{21}$}

The Frobenius group has a global arithmetic origin.  In the Eisenstein ring
$\mathbb{Z}[\omega]$ ($\omega = e^{2\pi i/3}$), the rational prime 7 splits,
and $\pi = 3+\omega$ is a prime of norm $N(\pi) = 9 - 3 + 1 = 7$.  The residue
field $\mathbb{Z}[\omega]/(\pi) \cong \mathrm{GF}(7)$ carries a natural action
of the cube roots of unity $\mu_3 \subset \mathbb{Z}[\omega]^\times$, and the
semidirect product of the additive residue group with this action is exactly
the Frobenius group:
\[
  F_{21} \;\cong\; \bigl(\mathbb{Z}[\omega]/(\pi)\bigr)^{\!+} \rtimes \mu_3
  \qquad \mbox{(\lean{f21\_eisenstein\_residue\_model}, \CatAL)}.
\]
The $\mathbb{Z}_3$ colour action is the reduction of complex multiplication by
$\omega$ --- colour is Eisenstein arithmetic.  The identification is natural
under Galois action, and the group order factors through the Eisenstein norms:
$|F_{21}| = N(1-\omega)\,N(3+\omega) = 3 \times 7 = \Phi_6(5)$
\mbox{(\lean{f21\_order\_eisenstein\_norm\_product}, \CatAL)}.
This is the mechanism behind the cyclotomic identity web of
§\ref{sec:fgci}: the GTE constants satisfy $\Phi_6$-identities because the
substrate group is built from the ring whose norm form \emph{is} $\Phi_6$.
These are Level-1 statements about the algebraic core as a finite group; the
full treatment (explicit isomorphism, torus action on the zero variety,
motivic point count $[V(p)] = \Phi_6(\mathbb{L})$) is given in
P49~\cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialWolfram}.

\paragraph{The Eisenstein companion at the inert prime: $A_4$.}
The same Eisenstein functor $X \rtimes \mu_3$ applied to the inert prime $2$
yields a companion group.  Since $2 \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$, the prime $2$ is inert in
$\mathbb{Z}[\omega]$: the residue field $\mathbb{Z}[\omega]/(2) \cong \mathrm{GF}(4)$
is a degree-2 extension of $\mathrm{GF}(2)$.  Its additive group is
$\mathrm{GF}(4)^+ \cong V_4 = \mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ (the Klein
four-group), and its multiplicative group is $\mathrm{GF}(4)^\times \cong
\mathbb{Z}_3$.  The semidirect product $V_4 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3 \cong A_4$, the
alternating group on four elements (order 12)
\mbox{(\lean{eisenstein\_a4\_from\_inert\_2}, \CatAL)}.  The Eisenstein functor
thus produces two groups from the same ring $\mathbb{Z}[\omega]$:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ccc}
\toprule
Prime & Status in $\mathbb{Z}[\omega]$ & Eisenstein group $X \rtimes \mu_3$ \\
\midrule
$7$ & split ($7 \equiv 1 \bmod 3$) & $F_{21} = \mathbb{Z}_7 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3$ \\
$2$ & inert ($2 \equiv 2 \bmod 3$) & $A_4 = V_4 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Both share the unit group $\mu_3 = \{1, \omega, \omega^2\}$, the cyclic subgroup
of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ acting on the three weak-boson generators
\mbox{(\lean{z3\_acts\_cyclically\_on\_su2\_generators}, \CatAL)}.  The amalgamated
product $(\mathbb{Z}_7 \times V_4) \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3$, of order $84$, unites both
groups via the shared $\mu_3$ and constitutes a single arithmetic structure at
Level~1 of the GTE hierarchy~\cite{SpivackPSL27Unification}.

\paragraph{$A_4$ as the leading-order neutrino flavor symmetry.}
The Eisenstein $A_4 = V_4 \rtimes \mu_3$ has a definite physical role: it supplies
the leading-order neutrino flavor symmetry (\CatAD).  The framework's manifest
flavor symmetries --- $\mu_3$ (generation cycling, identified with the
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ cyclic subgroup, \CatAL) and the $\mu$--$\tau$ exchange
$\mathbb{Z}_2 = \langle U \rangle$ (from the chiral CA architecture, \CatAL) ---
generate $S_3$ on three generations
\mbox{(\lean{gte\_manifest\_flavor\_is\_s3\_in\_a4}, \CatAL)}.  The group $S_3$
forces $\theta_{23} = 45^\circ$ and $\theta_{13} = 0$ but leaves the solar angle
$\theta_{12}$ undetermined.  Full tribimaximal mixing (Harrison--Perkins--Scott:
$\theta_{12} = \arcsin(1/\sqrt{3}) \approx 35.26^\circ$, $\theta_{23} = 45^\circ$,
$\theta_{13} = 0$) requires the Klein group $V_4$, which upgrades $S_3$ to
$A_4 = V_4 \rtimes \mu_3$.  The inert-prime-$2$ residue field supplies exactly this
$V_4$, completing the manifest flavor symmetries to the full tribimaximal-generating
group.

The \GTE\ leading-order PMNS matrix is therefore tribimaximal, coinciding
with the independently derived leading-order structure of §\ref{sec:neutrinos}.  The
measured departures from tribimaximal values are the $A_4$-breaking corrections
captured by the orbit-ratio formulas $\sin^2\theta_{12} = 4/13$,
