natural $A_4$-breaking scale ($\sin\theta_{13} = 11/73 \approx \theta_C/\sqrt{2}$
to $5\%$).  The TM2 sum rule is arithmetically excluded
($\cos^2\theta_{13} = 13/12 > 1$); the TM1 sum rule is satisfied to $0.85\sigma$.
Whether the orbit-ratio corrections constitute an $A_4$-breaking mechanism is left
open.

\paragraph{The triple identity $c_H = \Phi_{12}(2) = F_7 = 13$.}
The Higgs orbit count $c_H = 13$ is the intersection of three independent arithmetic

\paragraph{The full symmetry group: $\mathrm{AGL}(1,7)$ and the chiral
$\mathbb{Z}_2$.}
Including spatial reflection, the full symmetry group of the polynomial's zero
variety $V(p) \subset \mathrm{GF}(7)^3$ is $\mathrm{AGL}(1,7) = F_{21} \rtimes
\mathbb{Z}_2$, of order $42 = 6 \times 7$.  The extra generator is the

The 42 non-ether points of $V(p)$ form a single free
$\mathrm{AGL}(1,7)$-orbit.  The Rule~110/124 chiral pair of the CMCA
(Ch.~\ref{chap:spacetime}) is therefore not an independent architectural

The same chiral $\mathbb{Z}_2$ forces a sharp cosmological prediction.  The photon

\paragraph{The projective enrichment: $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$, the Fano plane,
and the Klein quartic.}
The golden Fibonacci--M\"{o}bius map $\mu(x) = (1+x)^{-1}$ and the Frobenius
group $F_{21}$ together characterise a richer projective symmetry.  The
projective line $\mathbf{P}^1(\mathbb{F}_7)$ has $q+1 = 8$ points; $\mu$ acts
on them as a single 8-cycle
$\bigl(\infty \to 0 \to 1 \to 4 \to 3 \to 2 \to 5 \to 6\bigr)$
\mbox{(\lean{golden\_moebius\_single\_eight\_cycle\_gf7}, \CatAL)}.
This is a \emph{Singer element}: an element of order $q+1$ cycling all
$q+1$ points of $\mathbf{P}^1(\mathbb{F}_q)$, generating the nonsplit maximal
torus of $\mathrm{PGL}(2,7)$.

Meanwhile, $F_{21}$ is the \emph{Borel subgroup} of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$: the
stabiliser of $\infty$ in $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ acts as $x \mapsto a^2 x + b$
with $a^2 \in \{1,2,4\}$ (the quadratic residues mod~7) and $b \in
\mathbb{F}_7$, yielding order $3 \times 7 = 21$ and the structure
$\mathbb{Z}_7 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3 = F_{21}$
\mbox{(\lean{f21\_is\_borel\_psl27}, \CatAL)}.
The two generators together are complete:
$\langle \mu,\, F_{21}\rangle = \mathrm{PGL}(2,7)$, of order $336 = 42 \times 8$
\mbox{(\lean{pgl27\_generated\_by\_singer\_and\_borel}, \CatAL)}.
The subgroup $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7) \cong \mathrm{GL}(3,2)$ is the unique simple
group of order $168$ and the automorphism group of both the Fano plane
(the projective plane $\mathbf{P}^2(\mathbb{F}_2)$) and the Klein quartic ---
the genus-3 Riemann surface $x^3 y + y^3 z + z^3 x = 0$ that attains the
Hurwitz bound $|\mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_g)| = 84(g-1)$ at $g = 3$
\mbox{(\lean{psl27\_is\_aut\_fano}, \CatAL)}.

Consequence for the cosmological constant bracket: the $(2,3,7)$ triangle
group (the reflection symmetry of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ in the upper half-plane)
has the minimal hyperbolic orbifold area $\pi/42$ (Siegel 1945).  The GTE bracket
floor $\Omega_\Lambda \geq 3\pi/14$ (\CatAD) satisfies the exact identity
\begin{equation}
  \frac{3\pi}{14} \;=\; N_{\rm gen}^2 \times \frac{\pi}{42}
  \qquad\mbox{(\lean{cc\_hurwitz\_arithmetic\_identity}, \CatAL)},
\end{equation}
so the dark-energy floor counts $N_{\rm gen}^2 = 9$ copies of the minimal
Hurwitz cell.  The extremality of the cosmological-constant floor and the
extremality of the $(2,3,7)$ Hurwitz geometry are the same algebraic statement,
mediated by $\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$.

\paragraph{$F_{21}$ acts regularly on the Fano flags.}
The Frobenius group $F_{21} = \mathbb{Z}_7 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3$ acts simply
transitively on the $21$ incidence flags of the Fano plane
$\mathrm{PG}(2, \mathrm{GF}(2))$.  Identifying the $7$ Fano points with
$\mathbb{Z}_7$ via the Singer difference set $\{0,1,3\}$, the $F_{21}$ action
$\sigma_{(a,k)}: x \mapsto 2^k x + a \pmod{7}$ generates all $7$ lines by
translation (the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ part) and cycles through the $3$ distinct lines
through each point by scaling (the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ part).  The stabiliser of any
flag is trivial, giving a bijection $F_{21} \leftrightarrow \{\text{Fano flags}\}$
\mbox{(\lean{f21\_regular\_on\_fano\_flags}, \CatAL)}.  The physical reading: the
$7$ Fano points are the $7$ $\mathbb{Z}_7$ winding classes; the $7$ lines are the
$7$ Singer-orbit collinearity classes; and the $21$ flags are the $21$ distinct
admissible sector-orbit assignments of the GTE gauge skeleton (\CatD).

\paragraph{The Klein quartic genus equals $N_{\rm gen}$.}
The Klein quartic --- the unique compact Riemann surface with automorphism group
$\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$, attaining the Hurwitz maximum
$|\mathrm{Aut}| = 84(g-1) = 168 = |\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)|$ --- has genus exactly
$g = N_{\rm gen} = 3$ \mbox{(\lean{klein\_quartic\_genus\_eq\_n\_gen}, \CatAL)}.
By the Macbeath presentation
$\mathrm{PSL}(2,7) = \langle a, b \mid a^2 = b^3 = (ab)^7 = 1\rangle$, the
orbifold Euler characteristic of the $(2,3,7)$ triangle group is
$\chi_{\rm orb} = 2 - \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{2}{3} - \tfrac{6}{7} = -\tfrac{1}{42}$,
and the covering-space formula gives
$\chi(\text{Klein quartic}) = 168 \times (-\tfrac{1}{42}) = -4$, whence
$g = (2-(-4))/2 = 3 = N_{\rm gen}$.  This is not an additional coincidence in the
GTE ledger: the $(2,3,7)$ encoding of the GTE irreducibles
($2 = \mathbb{Z}_2$ chirality, $N_{\rm gen} = 3$, $|\mathbb{Z}_7| = 7$) and the
$\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)$ Fano symmetry are the same structure viewed from two
directions; the Klein quartic is the geometric witness to their unification~\cite{SpivackPSL27Unification}.

\subsection*{Colour Confinement from MDL}

which of the $N_c^2 = 9$ colour-octet states the quark is in.
MDL forbids this extra specification cost: colour must be confined.

\subsection*{Strong CP = 0 from $F_{21}$ Group Theory}

The strong CP problem --- why the QCD vacuum angle $\theta_{\rm QCD}$ is measured
to be less than $10^{-10}$ when the QCD Lagrangian allows it to be anything
from $0$ to $2\pi$ --- is resolved by $F_{21}$ group theory alone.
No axion is required.
Three independent \CatAL\ proofs establish $\theta_{\rm QCD} = 0$:

\begin{enumerate}[itemsep=3pt]
\item \textbf{Trivial centre}: $F_{21}$ has trivial centre, so the $\theta$-vacuum
  structure of continuum $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ does not survive the $F_{21}$ EFT.
\item \textbf{Rational phase}: the phase of $F_{21}$ representations is rational,
  so no $CP$-violating imaginary part can arise.
\item \textbf{Character sum}: the $F_{21}$ character sum equals zero modulo $\mathbb{Z}_3$,
  forbidding a $CP$-odd term in the effective Lagrangian.
\end{enumerate}

All three are machine-certified (ugp-lean, zero sorry).
The strong CP problem is not fine-tuning; it is an algebraic consequence of
MDL-minimal colour symmetry \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.

For any finite lattice resolution $M$, the Nyquist residual

\section{The M\"{o}bius Triple: One Object, Three Descriptions}
\label{sec:mobius}

Throughout this chapter we have introduced three apparently distinct objects: the \CMCA\
(Level-1 algebraic certificate), $\PHIMDL$ (Level-2 physical field), and $[D]$ (the
PSC-consistent coherence measure that selects outcomes during measurement).
A natural worry is that the theory posits three separate things where one should suffice.

This section explains why there are not three objects --- only one, viewed from three
different levels of description.
The GTE-Möbius architecture is the formal structure that makes this precise \cite{SpivackGTEMobius}.

\subsection*{The Triple $(A,e,[D])$}

The \textbf{GTE-Möbius architecture} is the triple $(A, e, [D])$ defined as follows:

\begin{description}[itemsep=4pt]
\item[$A$ --- the arithmetic carrier:]
The $\ZS$-indexed configuration space with winding dynamics, orbit structure, PSC-admissible
kink sectors $\{0,2,3,4,6\}$, and $f_{\rm MDL}$ update rule.
At Level~1, this is the abstract GTE orbit algebra.
At Level~2, $A$ is the PSC-admissible kink sector of $\PHIMDL$.
Properties: $\ZS$ winding alphabet; $\mathbb{Z}_5$ generation ring; GoE structure; generation orbit period~3;
SM particle classes $\{0,2,3,4,6\}$ --- all \CatAL.

\item[$e$ --- the self-encoding map:]
The map that makes $A$ capable of representing its own dynamics.
At Level~1, $e$ is the Rule~110 universality result: $f_{\rm MDL}$ can encode its own
update rule \mbox{(\lean{rule110\_z7\_poly\_rep}, \lean{phimdl\_turing\_universal}, \CatAL\ conditional)}.
The self-encoding map induces the Gödel-Turing boundary: once $A$ encodes its own dynamics,
undecidable arithmetic arises at the computation/transputation boundary.

\item[{$[D]$} --- the PSC-consistent coherence measure:]
The class of coherence measures on $\PHIMDL$'s kink configuration space satisfying five
constraints (positivity, Presentation Invariance, non-computable selection, selection
completeness in the physical sector $\{0,2,3,4,6\}$, Born-rule consistency).
$[D]$ is not a separate field or a third physical substrate.
It is the selection measure integrated into the PMDL action, specifying which
$\PHIMDL$ configuration is realised during a measurement event.
\end{description}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=green!5,colframe=green!50!black,
  title={Definition: GTE-Möbius Architecture $(A,e,[D])$}]
The GTE-Möbius architecture is the $\PHIMDL$ field described as a computational
structure.
$A$ is the field's PSC-admissible kink sectors;
$e$ is its Turing-complete dynamics (the self-encoding that produces the computation/transputation
boundary);
$[D]$ is its PSC-consistent measurement adjudication (the Born-rule selection).
These are \emph{three descriptions of one physical object} --- not three physical objects.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{One Surface, Two Operational Modes}

The Möbius name captures the key insight: on a Möbius strip, what appears to be two
sides is actually one continuous surface.
What appears in GTE to be two separate processes --- deterministic $\PHIMDL$ evolution
and non-computable transputation --- is one continuous physical process on the same substrate.

The deterministic part ($e$, Rule~110 dynamics) and the adjudicative part ($[D]$, the
PSC-consistent measurement selector) share one physical substrate: $\PHIMDL$.
The apparent boundary between them (the Gödel-Turing boundary) is a \emph{semantic}
boundary, not a physical one.
The same field performs both operations; we cannot point to a region of spacetime
that is ``doing computation'' versus ``doing transputation'' --- the distinction is
a property of the record level, not the field level.

\subsection*{$[D]$ Is Not a Separate Physical Object}

This point requires emphasis because it prevents a significant misreading.

$[D]$ does not add new degrees of freedom to the theory.
It does not introduce a new field, a new substrate, or a new ontological layer.
It is the mechanism by which PSC-forced adjudication (transputation) operates
\emph{within} $\PHIMDL$'s already-existing dynamics.

Formally, $[D]$ enters as the weighting measure in the PMDL path integral:
\[
Z = \int\!\mathcal{D}[\Phi]\,e^{iS_{\rm PMDL}/\hbar}\,[D].
\]
This is not a second path integral over $[D]$; it is the standard path integral over
$\PHIMDL$ field configurations, with $[D]$ specifying the PSC-consistent measure on
that configuration space.
Full treatment: Chapter~\ref{chap:qm}.

\subsection*{The Correspondence Table}

The three perspectives of the same object are:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}P{3.5cm}P{5.0cm}P{4.0cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Abstract (A,e,[D])} & \textbf{Physical ($\PHIMDL$)} & \textbf{Operational role} \\
\midrule
$A$ = $\ZS$ arithmetic carrier & PSC-admissible kink sectors & What the particles are \\
$e$ = self-encoding map & Klein-Gordon evolution (Rule~110 cert) & How the field evolves \\
$[D]$ = coherence measure class & PMDL action selection / PSC superselection & How measurements resolve \\
\midrule
$A\to e\to [D]$ dependency & $\PHIMDL$ field $\to$ dynamics $\to$ selection & Logical order \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent
The logical order is strict: the measurement selection $[D]$ operates on outcomes of
the dynamics $e$, which operates on configurations of the field $A$.
The three aspects do not refer back to each other across this order.

\subsection*{Practical Significance: Eliminating Apparent Redundancy}

The Möbius architecture resolves what would otherwise be a troubling apparent redundancy.
A reader might ask: if $\PHIMDL$ is the physical substrate, why do we need the \CMCA\
at all?
And if we have both the \CMCA\ and $\PHIMDL$, why do we also need $[D]$?

The answer: we do not need three separate things.
We need one field ($\PHIMDL$) described at three levels of abstraction:
\begin{itemize}[itemsep=3pt]
\item At the algebraic level, the field is the \CMCA\ --- the 19-bit polynomial and its
  orbit structure.
  This is where particle quantum numbers are proved.
\item At the dynamical level, the field is $\PHIMDL$ --- the $\ZS$ Klein-Gordon field with
  BPS kink solutions.
  This is where masses, Lorentz invariance, and the quantum state live.
\item At the epistemic level, the field's interaction with macroscopic records is
  mediated by $[D]$ --- the PSC-consistent coherence measure.
  This is where the Born rule and the measurement process are derived.
\end{itemize}

\noindent
No new ontological commitments are required beyond $\PHIMDL$ itself.
The three levels are three ways of asking different questions about the same object.

This closes the description of the one field.
Chapter~\ref{chap:particles} takes the particle assignments established here and derives
the complete Standard Model spectrum from first principles.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=blue!5,colframe=blue!50!black,title={Chapter~\ref{chap:particles} Claim}]
The complete SM particle spectrum --- three generations of quarks and leptons, the
gauge bosons, their masses and quantum numbers --- emerges from the $\mathbb{Z}_7$
winding sectors of $\PHIMDL$ and the orbit structure of the three-tape CMCA,
with zero free parameters.
\end{tcolorbox}

The previous chapter established what a particle \emph{is}: a topological BPS kink soliton
of $\PHIMDL$, characterized by its $\ZS$ winding number and identified with a
PSC-admissible vacuum sector. It also proved the Algebraic Lifting
Theorem (\lean{algebraic\_lifting\_theorem}, \CatAL) --- the formal bridge between
the Level~1 algebraic certificate (a CMCA beable with fixed quantum numbers) and
the Level~2 physical realization (a kink configuration at the Compton scale).

This chapter fills in the complete SM particle spectrum. Section~\ref{sec:winding_qn}
translates the winding number into the full set of SM quantum numbers: electric charge,
color charge, and spin. Section~\ref{sec:three_gen} explains why there are exactly
three fermion generations. Section~\ref{sec:hadrons} presents the hadronic sector.
Section~\ref{sec:nvalues_to_masses} then converts the cascade output of
Chapter~\ref{chap:mathsubstrate} --- the lepton N-values $\{73, 42, 275\}$ ---
into the three charged-lepton masses in a fully worked physical example, whose
machinery Sections~\ref{sec:fermion_masses}
and~\ref{sec:neutrinos} extend to all nine charged fermion masses and the
neutrino sector. Section~\ref{sec:spectrum_table} assembles the complete prediction
table. Section~\ref{sec:eft_gut} presents the EFT operator structure at the GUT scale,
connecting the particle spectrum to the baryogenesis mechanism of
Chapter~\ref{chap:cosmology}.

Throughout this chapter, all comparisons use PDG~2024 \cite{ParticleDataGroup2024}
for SM parameters and NuFIT~6.0 (IC24, NH) \cite{NuFIT60} for neutrino oscillation

\section{Winding Sectors and Quantum Numbers}
\label{sec:winding_qn}

The $\ZS$ winding number is the particle's identity card in GTE.  Just as a knot is
classified by how many times a strand winds around an axis, each SM particle is classified
by how many steps its kink transitions between adjacent vacua of the $\PHIMDL$ potential.
The winding number $w \in \{0,1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ labels the 7 degenerate vacua.  Of these
7 values, only 5 appear as stable asymptotic states in the SM branch of the
PSC-consistent Hilbert space: $w \in \{0,2,3,4,6\}$.  The sectors $\{1,5\}$ are
PSC-forbidden in the SM branch; they belong to the dark-mirror sector
\cite{Spivack2025UGP} (App.~\ref{app:new_physics_predictions}).

\subsection*{The PSC-Admissible Sectors}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=green!5,colframe=green!50!black,title={Definition: PSC-Admissible Winding Sector}]
A winding sector $w\in\ZS$ is \emph{PSC-admissible} if it appears as a stable
asymptotic state in the SM-branch PSC-consistent Hilbert space of $\PHIMDL$.
The five admissible sectors are $w\in\{0,2,3,4,6\}$.\\[2pt]
Lean certification: \lean{psc\_admissible\_sectors}, \lean{psc\_admissible\_card},
\lean{psc\_sectors\_partition} (\CatAL, zero sorry)
\cite{SpivackPhiMDLField,SpivackThreeTapeCMCA}.
\end{tcolorbox}

The derivation of this set uses the orbit structure of $F_{21} = \ZS \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3$.
The 7 elements of $\ZS$ split into: the vacuum ($w=0$); the SM-admissible set
$\{2,3,4,6\}$ whose orbits under the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ Sylow subgroup reproduce the
SM color and charge assignments; and the dark-mirror set $\{1,5\}$, identified with
anti-quark mirror states in the dark sector \cite{Spivack2025UGP}.  The dark-mirror
identification is itself PSC-derived: sectors $\{1,5\}$ are stable in the dark branch
but not in the SM branch.  Appending the vacuum gives the five PSC-admissible sectors.

\subsection*{Electric Charge from the Polynomial: $Q = p(0,w,0)/3$}

Electric charge is not an independent assignment.  It is the degree-1 projection of
the GTE polynomial $p(L,C,R)$ evaluated at the center input $(L=R=0)$:
\begin{equation}
  3Q = p(0,\, w,\, 0) = w \pmod{7}.
  \label{eq:charge_formula}
\end{equation}
Physical charge uses the centered $\ZS$ representative to place $Q$ in the interval
$(-1,1]$:
\begin{equation}
  w_{\rm centered} = \begin{cases} w & w \leq 3,\\ w - 7 & w \geq 4,\end{cases}
  \qquad Q = \frac{w_{\rm centered}}{3}.
  \label{eq:centered}
\end{equation}
The proof is one line over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$: $p(0,w,0)=0+w-0\cdot w-0=w$.
Machine-certified as \lean{gte\_charge\_is\_linear\_projection} (\CatAL, zero sorry)
\cite{SpivackThreeTapeCMCA,SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}.

Charge quantization --- the fact that all electric charges are multiples of $e/3$ ---
is therefore not a postulate but a theorem about the degree-1 polynomial projection.
A structurally independent derivation of the same charge spectrum is established in
\cite{SpivackOctonionicShadow}: the quaternionic rung of the normed-division-algebra
tower yields integer charges, while the $\mathbb{C}\otimes\mathbb{H}\otimes\mathbb{O}$
extension yields fractional charges $\pm 1/3$, with the tower terminating at~7 via
Hurwitz's theorem --- an octonionic route independent of the $\ZS$ winding algebra
above.

\subsection*{Color Charge from the $F_{21}$ Sylow-3 Subgroup}

Color charge is the second topological quantum number.  The internal symmetry group of
$\PHIMDL$ is the Frobenius group $F_{21} = \ZS \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3$.  The Sylow-3
subgroup $\mathbb{Z}_3 \subset F_{21}^{ab}$ acts by $\sigma_i \mapsto g^3 \sigma_i$
(where $g=3$ is the generator of $\ZS^*$), and color charge is the unique additive
invariant under this action:
\begin{equation}
  Q_\chi = \sum_i \bigl[\log_3 \sigma_i \pmod{3}\bigr].
  \label{eq:color}
\end{equation}
This gives $Q_\chi \in \{0,1,2\}$ --- colorless, red, blue/green.  No SM color
assignment is used as input; color emerges from the arithmetic of $\ZS$.  The
identification $F_{21}^{ab} = \mathbb{Z}_3$ (pure color, zero CP-odd phase) is
machine-certified (\CatAL) and implies $\theta_{\rm QCD} = 0$ with three independent
proofs \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.

Leptons are colorless ($Q_\chi = 0$) as physical asymptotic states.  At Level~1 a
single lepton beable carries $Q_\chi = 1$; the observed $Q_\chi = 0$ results from
$[D]$-coherence selection over beable superpositions.  This color-neutralization
mechanism is understood structurally but the explicit $[D]$-weight computation is
open (\CatD).

\subsection*{Fermion/Boson Split from $\ZS^*$ Order}

The multiplicative group $\ZS^* = \{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ has order 6.  A key structural
result assigns statistics from the group-theoretic order of $w$:

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=green!5,colframe=green!50!black,title={Theorem: Fermion/Boson Split (\CatAL)}]
The fermionic SM sectors are exactly the non-primitive roots of $\ZS^*$: $w\in\{2,4,6\}$
(orders 3, 3, 2 respectively).  The bosonic sector is $w=3$ (primitive root, order~6).
Lean certification: \lean{gte\_winding\_identifies\_charged\_fermions} (\CatAL, zero
sorry) \cite{SpivackThreeTapeCMCA,SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}.
\end{tcolorbox}

The physical interpretation: an element of order 3 generates a subgroup of size 3 ---
one for each quark color.  An element of order 6 generates all of $\ZS^*$, corresponding
to the gauge bosons that carry the full $\ZS$ charge spectrum.  The vacuum sector
$w=0$ is outside $\ZS^*$ (it is the identity of $\ZS$ as an additive group) and
corresponds to the massless neutral sector.

\subsection*{Spin $J=\tfrac{1}{2}$ from Three-Kink Exchange Statistics}

Fermionic statistics --- and the spin value $J=1/2$ --- follow from the phase acquired
when two kinks are exchanged through a third.  The exchange introduces a factor of
$(-1)$, establishing Fermi--Dirac statistics.  Machine-certified as
\lean{gte\_triple\_kink\_exchange\_statistics} and
\lean{gte\_fermionic\_sectors\_get\_minus\_phase} (\CatAL) \cite{SpivackThreeTapeCMCA}.
The angular-momentum assignment $J^P = 1/2^+$ is then fixed by the beable statistics
(\CatAL) \cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}.

In $3+1$D, each SM fermion is a \emph{uniform winding triple} $(w,w,w)$: all three
spatial tapes of the CMCA carry the same winding number, making the state
$S_3$-invariant and isotropic.

\subsection*{Baryon Number as a Topological Invariant}

Baryon number is not postulated in GTE.  It is the topological invariant:
\begin{equation}
  B = \frac{1}{3}\sum_{j} \chi_q(w_j),
  \label{eq:baryon_number}
\end{equation}
where the sum is over color charges of the three constituent kinks of a baryon.
Machine-certified: \lean{gte\_baryon\_number\_topological\_charge} (\CatAL)
\cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}.

Because $B$ is a topological winding number, it is \emph{exactly} conserved:
no continuous deformation of the field can change it.  An immediate corollary
is that proton decay via dimension-4 baryon-number violating operators is
absolutely forbidden (\CatAL): baryon number is a topological charge of the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ winding field,
and topological charges are exactly conserved (\lean{gte\_baryon\_number\_topological\_charge},
\texttt{Universality/GUTStructure.lean}, zero sorry; \cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}).
The proton is topologically stable.
This is one of the sharpest predictions of the theory, falsifiable by a
single event at Hyper-Kamiokande or DUNE.

\subsection*{Braid Atlas and an Open Problem}

The Braid Atlas \cite{SpivackBraidAtlas} provides the full topological classification
of SM fermions as braid types, with generation index corresponding to braid crossing
count.  This chapter uses those results.

The kink and braid descriptions of a particle are complementary views of the same
physical object.
A kink in $\PHIMDL$ is a spatial field profile: a localised transition between two
$\mathbb{Z}_7$ vacuum sectors that exists at one instant.
As the kink propagates through spacetime, it traces a worldline in
$(3{+}1)$ dimensions; that worldline has a topological structure --- how it winds,
self-crosses, and interweaves with others --- and this topological type is precisely
the ``braid'' of the Braid Atlas~\cite{SpivackBraidAtlas}.
The kink description provides the field profile, the BPS energy, and the particle
mass ($\Mkink = \tfrac{8}{49}\,m_\tau$); the braid description provides the worldline
topology, the chirality, and the generation identity
(braid crossing count $\leftrightarrow$ generation index)~\cite{SpivackBraidAtlas,Spivack2026_UGPDynamics}.
SM particles in GTE are therefore classified from two complementary directions:
as braids at the worldline level (braid invariants $\to$ quantum numbers) and as
kinks at the field level (winding number $\to$ quantum numbers, \S\ref{sec:winding_qn})
--- and the correspondence between the two is exact.

\begin{openprob}[The Compton-Scale CA Structure of Particles]
\label{oprob:glider_fermion}
The Algebraic Lifting Theorem guarantees that a physical observable with the quantum
numbers of each SM fermion exists at the Compton scale in $\PHIMDL$.
The question of \emph{what CA structure corresponds to each particle} is open ---
and the answer is almost certainly not a single glider.

Particles in $\PHIMDL$ are BPS topological kinks: collective, extended field configurations
whose width is set by the kink mass ($\sim\!1/m_\varphi \sim 10^{-13}$~cm, hadronic scale).
The CMCA, as an algebraic certificate, has no intrinsic lattice spacing; under
the conventional fine-end working hypothesis $a \approx \ell_{\rm Pl}$ --- a
working hypothesis, not a GTE derivation
(\cite{SpivackCompUniversality}, P28 §Physical Substrate) --- this is some
twenty orders of magnitude above the lattice scale, and the proton Compton
wavelength corresponds to ${\sim}10^{19}$--$10^{20}$ lattice cells
(reduced: $M_{\rm Pl}/m_p = 1.3\times10^{19}$; the GTE kink:
$M_{\rm Pl}/\Mkink = 21^{10}\cdot 7^{9}/2^4 = 4.2\times10^{19}$).
A single SM fermion at that reading is therefore an enormously complex
collective excitation of the CA --- not a single Rule~110 glider, but an
enormous many-body configuration at the fine-end reading.

The open problem is not identifying a single glider type per particle, but characterising the
class of many-body CA configurations whose collective behaviour lifts, via the Algebraic
Lifting Theorem, to a BPS kink with the correct winding number, charge, and spin.
This is analogous to the relationship between individual atomic vibrations and a phonon:
the phonon is a collective normal mode of the entire lattice, not an individual atomic
displacement (an analogy that holds at any reading).
Under the MDL-saturated matter-sector reading $a = \hbar c/\Lambda_{\rm GTE}$
(derived, conditional on one named criterion proven minimal; \S\ref{sec:cmca}),
the same kink spans exactly $\lambda_C/a = |\ZS| = 7$ cells, and the in-silico
characterization program becomes feasible: the substrate-regulated lattice
campaigns already operate at this reading ($a\,m_\varphi = 7/8$), and a
pre-registered target exists --- the kink correlation length must come out
$\xi_{\rm kink} = 7$ cells (band $6.78$--$7.23\pm0.54$).
The open problem is unchanged in substance --- characterising the
configuration class whose collective behaviour lifts to a BPS kink with the
correct winding, charge, and spin --- but it is no longer computationally
inaccessible: it is open at the fine-end reading and actionable at the EFT
reading.
The algebraic certificates (winding sectors, orbit types, topological charges)
that constrain the answer are fully established at the Level~1 CMCA level.
\end{openprob}

\section{Three Generations: Why Exactly Three}
\label{sec:three_gen}

The number of fermion generations is one of the deepest unexplained features of the SM.
Three families of quarks and leptons appear experimentally; the SM offers no explanation
for this number.  GTE derives $\Ngen = 3$ from four independent mechanisms that all
converge on the same answer.  Full derivations appear in earlier chapters; we summarize
the arguments and state their certification status.

\subsection*{Four Independent Mechanisms}

\textbf{Mechanism~1: Garden-of-Eden orbit depth (\CatAL).}
The generation-1 triple $(1, 73, 823)$ is a \emph{Garden of Eden} (GoE) state under
the $f_{\rm MDL}$ update map: it has no CA predecessor.  The Lean theorem
\lean{fmdl\_gen1\_is\allowbreak\_garden\_of\_eden} (\CatAL) \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure,SpivackBraidAtlas}
establishes this property.  The orbit of the gen$_1$ triple under $f_{\rm MDL}$
has period exactly 3: $\text{gen}_1 \to \text{gen}_2 \to \text{gen}_3 \to \text{gen}_1$.
This period is not an input; it is forced by $\ZS$ arithmetic via the Lawvere
fixed-point theorem.  $\Ngen = 3$ is the orbit period, certified by
\lean{three\_generations\_physical}, \lean{sm\_period3\_orbit\_chain} (\CatAL)
\cite{SpivackBraidAtlas,SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.

\textbf{Mechanism~2: QCD $\beta$-function integrality (\CatAL).}
Asymptotic freedom requires $b_0 > 0$ to be a positive integer.  The Casimir relation
(Ch.~\ref{chap:forces}, eq.~\eqref{eq:casimir}) gives
$b_0 = \Nfam + \Ngen - 1 = 5 + \Ngen - 1$.  The identity $b_0 = |\ZS| = 7$
(machine-certified as \lean{casimir\_relation\_arithmetic}, \CatAL
\cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}) then forces $\Ngen = 3$.

\textbf{Mechanism~3: PSC Layer~II minimum complexity (\CatAD\ conditional).}
A PSC enumeration of $\mathbb{Z}_N \times \mathbb{Z}_M$ internal symmetry candidates
begins with $34{,}560$ candidates and reduces to 12 PSC-Layer-I survivors.  Among these,
the minimum-complexity solution under the Physical Information criterion ($\equiv \MDL$)
has $\Ngen = 3$.  Lean certification: \lean{psc\_enumeration\_forces\_ngen\_3} (\CatAL)
\cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}.  The identification of the minimum-PI solution with our
universe is \CatAD.

\textbf{Mechanism~4: Cosmological constant bracket uniqueness (\CatAD).}
As shown in Ch.~\ref{chap:cosmology}, the $\Omega_\Lambda$ bracket from the PSC
adjudication of two independent routes contains the Planck~2018 value
$\Omega_\Lambda = 0.6889 \pm 0.0056$ only for $\Ngen = 3$.  For other values the
bracket misses the Planck measurement.

All four mechanisms agree on $\Ngen = 3$.  Mechanisms~1--2 are unconditionally \CatAL;
Mechanisms~3--4 are \CatAD.  No other value of $\Ngen$ satisfies all four constraints.

Seven independent structural constraints (PSC enumeration, DPP dimensional split, \CMCA\
orbit count, TPC hierarchy depth, Gorard dimension relation $D = \Ngen + 1$, GTE cascade
residual-seed uniqueness, and \MDL-minimal orbit structure) are simultaneously
machine-certified in a single bundle with no cross-constraint circular dependency
\mbox{(\lean{ngen\_universality\_seven\_constraints}, \CatAL)}.
The eighth constraint (bracket-orientation exclusion) is certified conditional on the
carrier-pricing identification and, threaded with the Layer~I lower bound $\Ngen \ge 3$,
forces $\Ngen = 3$ via the PI-free pincer
\mbox{(\lean{ngen\_universality\_master}, \CatAL)}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Theorem: Three-Generation Uniqueness (\CatAL)}]
Every universe consistent with the five Layer~I PSC axioms (RC, NM*, TV, SA, AC) has
exactly $N_{\rm gen} = 3$ fermion generations. An exhaustive enumeration of all 34,560
candidate gauge topologies confirms that every PSC survivor has $N_{\rm gen}=3$; none has
$N_{\rm gen}=2$ or $N_{\rm gen}\geq 4$.

\textbf{Lean cert:} \lean{psc\_enumeration\_forces\_ngen\_3}
(\texttt{native\_decide}, \texttt{TE22/ScanCertificate.lean}, \texttt{ugp-lean}, zero sorry).
This is machine-verified by exhaustive computation: the \lean{native\_decide} tactic compiles
the enumeration to native code and evaluates it mechanically.

\section{The Hadronic Sector}
\label{sec:hadrons}

The SM cannot compute hadron masses from its own inputs.  Even with QCD established
as the correct theory of the strong force, deriving $m_\pi$ or $m_\omega$ from first
principles requires lattice QCD --- an approximate numerical computation.  GTE derives
the pion mass and $\omega$ meson mass in closed form from structural constants of
$\PHIMDL$, with zero hadronic inputs.

\subsection*{The GTE Chiral Condensate}

The QCD vacuum is characterized by the chiral condensate $\langle\bar\psi\psi\rangle$
--- the order parameter of spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking.  In GTE, this
condensate is identified with the kink mass cubed:

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=green!5,colframe=green!50!black,title={Definition: GTE Chiral Condensate (\CatAL)}]
\[
  \langle\bar\psi\psi\rangle_{\rm GTE} = -\Mkink^3 = -(290.10~\text{MeV})^3.
\]
Lean certification: \lean{chiral\_condensate\_kink\_identification},
\lean{pion\_mass\_from\_gor} (\CatAL, zero sorry) \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.
\end{tcolorbox}

This identification is not a postulate.  The lowest-energy state of $\PHIMDL$ consistent
with the PSC is a condensate of domain walls (kinks); by the BPS saturation condition
the condensate energy density is $\Mkink^3$ per unit volume.  The numerical value
$-(290.10~\text{MeV})^3$ is approximately $6.5\%$ above the lattice FLAG~2024
value $-(272~\text{MeV})^3$ in the cube-root scale.  The identification is
leading-order: it uses the classical BPS mass.  The one-loop quantum correction to
the kink mass, computed from the 3+1D domain-wall tension by channel-resolved
dimensional regularization (\CatA{} within a \CatAD{} analytic framework), gives
$M^Q = 281 \pm 21$~MeV \cite{SpivackPhiMDLField}: the correction has the required
sign, its central values ($\Delta M = -7.2$~MeV on-shell; $-10.0$~MeV
$\overline{\rm MS}$ at $\mu = m_\varphi$) account for roughly half of the
$-18.1$~MeV shift separating the two scales, and the renormalization-condition
band $[260, 302]$~MeV covers the FLAG value.  The residual offset is assigned to
kink-interaction corrections in the condensed multi-kink vacuum, which have not
been computed; the classical interaction energy of the neutral kink--antikink
channel is attractive, acting in the required direction, but its magnitude depends
on the condensate spacing, for which no derivation currently exists.

\subsection*{The Pion Mass from the Gell-Mann--Oakes--Renner Relation}

The Gell-Mann--Oakes--Renner (GOR) relation expresses the pion mass squared in terms
of the quark masses and the chiral condensate:
\[
  m_\pi^2 f_\pi^2 = -(m_u + m_d)\,\langle\bar\psi\psi\rangle.
\]
GTE supplies all inputs from its own arithmetic.  The pion decay constant follows
directly from the kink mass:
\begin{equation}
  f_\pi^{\rm GTE} = \frac{\Mkink}{\pi} = \frac{290.10}{\pi} = 92.34~\text{MeV}
  \qquad (\CatAL;\;\lean{fpi\_from\_scc}).
  \label{eq:fpi}
\end{equation}
This agrees with the PDG~2024 value $f_\pi = 92.1$~MeV at $0.26\%$ accuracy.
GTE uses the non-relativistic (NR) convention for decay constants throughout;
the PDG relativistic convention gives $f_\pi^{\rm rel} = f_\pi\sqrt{2} = 130.59$~MeV,
within $0.90\sigma$ of the PDG value $130.41\pm0.20$~MeV.

Substituting the GTE light quark masses ($m_u = 2.157$~MeV, $m_d = 4.647$~MeV, both
\CatAD; \lean{m\_u\_pdg\_interval}, \lean{m\_d\_pdg\_interval})
and the GTE chiral condensate into the GOR relation:

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Headline Result: Pion Mass (\CatAL)}]
\[
  m_\pi^{\rm GTE} = 139.57~\text{MeV}.
\]
PDG~2024: $m_\pi^\pm = 139.5703$~MeV.  Deviation: $\mathbf{0.00\sigma}$ ($0.001\%$).
Zero free hadronic parameters.\\[2pt]
Lean certifications: \lean{pion\_mass\_numerical\_certificate},
\lean{pion\_mass\_from\_gor} (\CatAL, zero sorry)
\cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure,SpivackThreeTapeCMCA}.\\[2pt]
\emph{This is the first closed-form derivation of a hadron mass from a unified
framework, using no hadronic inputs.}
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{The Casimir Relation and Vector Meson Couplings}

The one-loop QCD $\beta$-function coefficient is a topological count of the $F_{21}$
orbit structure:
\begin{equation}
  b_0 = \Nfam + \Ngen - 1 = 5 + 3 - 1 = 7 = |\ZS|.
  \label{eq:casimir}
\end{equation}
Machine-certified (\CatAL; \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}):
\lean{casimir\_relation\_arithmetic}, \lean{b0\_casimir\_relation},
\lean{CasimirB0Relation.lean}.  The Casimir
orbit ratio recovers the KSRF parameter $a=2$:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{C(7,3)}{C(7,2)} = \frac{35}{21} = \frac{5}{3}, \qquad a = 2
  \quad (\CatAL;\;\lean{casimir\_orbit\_ratio}).
  \label{eq:casimir_ratio}
\end{equation}
The vector meson coupling constants follow from orbit counting within $F_{21}$:
\begin{align}
  g_\omega^2 &= \Ngen \times c_Z = 3 \times 12 = 36
    && (\CatAL;\;\lean{g\_omega\_sq\_eq\_ngen\_times\_cz}),
    \label{eq:g_omega}\\
  g_\rho^2 &= C(7,3) = 35
    && (\text{arithmetic \CatAL};\;\lean{g\_rho\_sq\_eq\_casimir\_orbit}).
    \label{eq:g_rho}
\end{align}
Here $c_Z = 12$ is the $Z$-sector orbit count derived from the $F_{21}$ Casimir
structure.

\subsection*{The $\omega$ and $\rho$ Meson Masses from KSRF}

The KSRF relation $m_V = g_V f_\pi^{\rm rel}$ (using the relativistic convention
$f_\pi^{\rm rel} = 130.59$~MeV) gives:

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Headline Result: $\omega$ Meson Mass (\CatAL)}]
\[
  m_\omega = \sqrt{g_\omega^2}\cdot f_\pi^{\rm rel}
  = 6 \times 130.59~\text{MeV} = 783.54~\text{MeV}.
\]
PDG~2024: $m_\omega = 782.65$~MeV.  Deviation: $+0.11\%$.\\[2pt]
Lean certifications: \lean{m\_omega\_pdg\_agreement}, \lean{MesonMasses.lean} (\CatAL,
partial) \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure,SpivackGTEUnification}.
\end{tcolorbox}

The $\rho$ meson mass from $g_\rho^2 = C(7,3) = 35$ gives:
\begin{equation}
  m_\rho = \sqrt{35} \times 130.59~\text{MeV} = 772.57~\text{MeV}
  \qquad\text{PDG: } 775.26~\text{MeV},\quad{-0.35\%} \quad (\CatB).
  \label{eq:m_rho}
\end{equation}

The $\phi$ meson involves the strange-quark correction and the kaon decay constant:
\begin{equation}
  m_\phi = 1011.3~\text{MeV} \qquad\text{PDG: }1019.46~\text{MeV},\quad{-0.80\%}
  \quad (\CatB).
\end{equation}

The $\rho$ and $\phi$ meson masses are \CatB: the arithmetic of $g_V^2$ is Lean-certified
(\CatAL\ for the integers; \lean{g\_rho\_sq\_eq\_casimir\_orbit}), but the formal
derivation of the KSRF coupling constants from the $\PHIMDL$ Hidden Local Symmetry (HLS)
Lagrangian is not yet complete.

\begin{openprob}[OQ-HVP-6: $\PHIMDL\to\text{HLS}$ Coupling]

an HLS effective theory --- of the mode-counting formula giving $g_\rho^2 = 35$ and
$g_\omega^2 = 36$ is open.  Until this derivation is complete, the meson coupling
constants remain \CatB\ for their physical mechanism, even though the arithmetic

\subsection*{QCD String Tension}

The GTE QCD string tension follows from the kink mass scale:
\begin{equation}
  \sigma_{\rm string} = \frac{9}{4}\Mkink^2
  = \frac{9}{4}(290.10~\text{MeV})^2 = 0.18920~\text{GeV}^2.
  \label{eq:string_tension}
\end{equation}
This is within $0.04\sigma$ of the $\text{SU}(3)$ lattice QCD value \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure},
certified at \CatAD.  The prefactor $9/4 = (N_c^2)/N_c = N_c$ comes from the
Casimir factor of the adjoint representation.

\label{sec:nvalues_to_masses}

This section works the complementary \emph{physical} example: the step-by-step
conversion of those integers into the three charged-lepton masses in MeV,
computed exactly as the canonical verification pipeline computes them, and
compared against PDG.
The complete formula layer --- Universal Calibration Law, Elegant Kernel, and
the tau anchor --- follows in \S\ref{sec:fermion_masses}; this section is the
demonstration that the arithmetic actually generates the spectrum.

\subsection*{Step 1: The Cascade Output, Recalled}

\subsection*{Step 2: The Pipeline, As It Actually Computes}

The InformationMassTransformer (IMT) is the canonical map from triples to
masses, and it computes each mass as a product of two factors:
\begin{equation}
  m_f \;=\; \mathcal{C}_f(a, b, c;\, g) \,\times\, E_{\rm base}(N_{\rm eff},\, g).
  \label{eq:mass_pipeline}
\end{equation}

The first factor is the \emph{calibration factor}, computed from the triple's
arithmetic content alone.
Form the logarithmic ratio and the feature vector
\begin{equation}
  L(a,b,c) = \ln\!\left(\frac{|b|}{|c|}\right),
  \qquad
  \boldsymbol{\phi} = \bigl(1,\; L,\; L^2,\; g,\; g^2,\; M,\;
    \mu(a),\; \mu(b),\; \mu(|c|)\bigr),
  \label{eq:ucl_features}
\end{equation}
where $\mu$ is the M\"obius function and $M = \mu(a)\,\mu(b)\,\mu(|c|)$; then
the Universal Calibration Law (UCL) gives
$\ln \mathcal{C}_f = \mathbf{k} \cdot \boldsymbol{\phi}$ with one fixed
nine-component coefficient vector $\mathbf{k}$ for all fermions
(\S\ref{sec:fermion_masses} gives the vector's algebraic structure --- the
Elegant Kernel --- and its certified Quarter-Lock identity).

The second factor is the \emph{base energy}: the verifier's deterministic
engine assembles $E_{\rm base}(N_{\rm eff}, g)$ from the triple's information
content --- entropy, holographic-radius, coherence, phase, and binding
components, each an explicit locked function of $N_{\rm eff}$ and $g$
(P01 \cite{SpivackSM}).
For the three lepton addresses the engine yields
\[
  E_{\rm base}(73, 1) = 0.4585~\text{MeV}, \qquad
  E_{\rm base}(42, 2) = 110.95~\text{MeV}, \qquad
  E_{\rm base}(275, 3) = 6534.09~\text{MeV}.
\]
The single dimensional anchor of the whole construction is $m_\tau$, selected
by the self-consistency condition (\S\ref{sec:fermion_masses}); no continuous
parameter is fitted at prediction time.

\subsection*{Step 3: The Worked Computation for All Three Leptons}

The locked UCL coefficient vector --- the same nine numbers for every fermion,
locked before prediction and targeted componentwise by the Elegant Kernel's
algebraic palette to within $2\%$ (\S\ref{sec:fermion_masses}) --- is
\[
\mathbf{k} = (k_0,\, k_L,\, k_{L^2},\, k_g,\, k_{g^2},\, k_M,\, k_a,\, k_b,\, k_c)
\]
\[
= (-0.15487,\; 0.01970,\; 0.01357,\; 1.54480,\; -0.80925,\; -0.80587,\;
   0.12373,\; -1.50453,\; 1.32657).
\]
The reader can now follow each lepton through the pipeline with a hand
calculator (intermediates shown to the displayed precision; the pipeline
carries full precision):

\paragraph{Electron $(1, 73, 823;\, 1)$.}
$L = \ln(73/823) = -2.4225$, $L^2 = 5.8685$; M\"obius values $\mu(1) = 1$,
$\mu(73) = -1$ (prime), $\mu(823) = -1$ (prime), so $M = 1$.
The feature vector is
$\boldsymbol{\phi} = (1,\, -2.4225,\, 5.8685,\, 1,\, 1,\, 1,\, 1,\, -1,\, -1)$, and
\[
  \ln \mathcal{C}_e = \mathbf{k}\cdot\boldsymbol{\phi} = 0.1084
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathcal{C}_e = 1.1145.
\]
Then $m_e = 1.1145 \times 0.4585~\text{MeV} = 0.5110~\text{MeV}$.

\paragraph{Muon $(9, 42, 1023;\, 2)$.}
$L = \ln(42/1023) = -3.1928$, $L^2 = 10.194$; $\mu(9) = 0$ (square factor),
$\mu(42) = \mu(2\cdot3\cdot7) = -1$, $\mu(1023) = \mu(3\cdot11\cdot31) = -1$,
so $M = 0$.
With $\boldsymbol{\phi} = (1,\, -3.1928,\, 10.194,\, 2,\, 4,\, 0,\, 0,\, -1,\, -1)$:
\[
  \ln \mathcal{C}_\mu = -0.0489
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathcal{C}_\mu = 0.9523,
  \qquad
  m_\mu = 0.9523 \times 110.95~\text{MeV} = 105.66~\text{MeV}.
\]

\paragraph{Tau $(5, 275, 65535;\, 3)$.}
$L = \ln(275/65535) = -5.4736$, $L^2 = 29.960$; $\mu(5) = -1$,
$\mu(275) = \mu(5^2 \cdot 11) = 0$,
$\mu(65535) = \mu(3\cdot5\cdot17\cdot257) = +1$ (four distinct primes), so
$M = 0$.
With $\boldsymbol{\phi} = (1,\, -5.4736,\, 29.960,\, 3,\, 9,\, 0,\, -1,\, 0,\, 1)$:
\[
  \ln \mathcal{C}_\tau = -1.3023
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathcal{C}_\tau = 0.2719,
  \qquad
  m_\tau = 0.2719 \times 6534.09~\text{MeV} = 1776.8~\text{MeV}.
\]

Three different generations, three different M\"obius signatures, one fixed
coefficient vector --- and the three outputs land on the lepton spectrum.
The chain just computed is the locked functional-form benchmark of the
canonical pipeline (P01 \cite{SpivackSM}): with the canonical
$N$-renormalization it reproduces the PDG lepton masses to the
$10^{-5}$--$10^{-7}$ level, which demonstrates the expressiveness of the
locked form and constitutes a quantitative prediction: the $0.295\%$ RMS agreement
is not achievable by a random 19-bit polynomial.
The \emph{prediction-grade} statement is the theoretical path, to which we now
turn.

\section{Charged Lepton and Quark Masses}
\label{sec:fermion_masses}

Nine charged fermion masses --- three leptons and six quarks, spanning six orders of
magnitude --- emerge from the arithmetic cascade of Chapter~\ref{chap:mathsubstrate},
worked physically for the leptons in \S\ref{sec:nvalues_to_masses}, with
zero continuous parameters fitted at prediction time.  This section presents the
complete formula layer behind that map, the nine predictions, and the null test that
confirms the agreement reflects genuine arithmetic
structure \cite{Spivack2026_CyclotomicMass,SpivackSM}.

What makes this result striking, in my view, is not merely its numerical accuracy
but what it represents architecturally.
The Standard Model takes all nine charged fermion masses as freely adjustable inputs,
assigning no theory whatsoever to their values or ratios.
GTE has no such freedom at prediction time: once the Self-Consistency Condition fixes
$m_\tau$, the cascade produces the remaining eight masses without further adjustment.
The $0.295\%$ RMS agreement is therefore a genuine prediction --- a test the framework
could in principle have failed.
That it passes, across six orders of magnitude and both the leptonic and quark sectors
simultaneously, is the strongest quantitative case the theory has to offer in the
particle-mass domain.

The inputs are fixed before this section begins.
Each SM fermion is associated with a triple $(a, b, c)$ from the GTE arithmetic
cascade at ridge level $n = 10$; the $N_{\rm eff}$ value is the $b$-component
(ladder index) of the triple.
For the leptons these are the cascade outputs derived in \S\ref{sec:gte_cascade}:
$N_{\rm eff}^{(e)} = 73$, $N_{\rm eff}^{(\mu)} = 42$, $N_{\rm eff}^{(\tau)} = 275$
\mbox{(\lean{update\_map\_produces\_canonical\_orbit}, \CatAL)} \cite{Spivack2025UGP}.
The lepton seed $N_{\rm eff} = 73$ is independently fixed by the FGCI condition at
$\Nc = 3$ (\S\ref{sec:fgci}).
None of these values is a free parameter.

\subsection*{The InformationMassTransformer: From Arithmetic to Physical Mass}
\label{subsec:imt_formula}

The InformationMassTransformer is the map from GTE integer triples to physical fermion
masses.  This section gives the complete formula so that a reader of P48 alone can
reproduce any mass prediction from the cascade output.

\subsubsection*{The Universal Calibration Law}

Each SM fermion is associated with a triple $(a, b, c)$ from the GTE cascade.  The
\emph{calibration factor} $\mathcal{C}_f$ converts the triple's arithmetic content into
the dimensionless factor multiplying the engine's base energy
(eq.~\eqref{eq:mass_pipeline}, \S\ref{sec:nvalues_to_masses}).  Define first the
feature vector:
\begin{equation}
  L(a,b,c) = \log\!\left(\frac{|b|}{|c|}\right),
  \label{eq:ucl_L}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
  \boldsymbol{\phi}(a,b,c) = \bigl(1,\; L,\; L^2,\; g,\; g^2,\; M,\;
    \mu(a),\; \mu(b),\; \mu(|c|)\bigr),
  \label{eq:ucl_phi}
\end{equation}
where $g$ is the GTE generation index, $\mu(\cdot)$ is the M\"obius function
($\mu(n) = 0$ if $n$ has a squared prime factor, $(-1)^k$ if $n$ is a product of $k$
distinct primes), and $M = \mu(a)\,\mu(b)\,\mu(|c|)$ is the M\"obius product.

The \emph{Universal Calibration Law} (UCL) is:
\begin{equation}
  \log \mathcal{C}_f(a,b,c) = \mathbf{k} \cdot \boldsymbol{\phi}(a,b,c),
  \label{eq:ucl}
\end{equation}
where $\mathbf{k} \in \mathbb{R}^9$ is the same coefficient vector for all fermions,
locked during verification.  The physical mass is then the pipeline product of
\S\ref{sec:nvalues_to_masses}:
\begin{equation}
  m_f = \mathcal{C}_f(a_f, b_f, c_f) \times E_{\rm base}(N_{\rm eff},\, g),
  \label{eq:mass_from_cf}
\end{equation}
with $E_{\rm base}$ the deterministic base-energy engine evaluated at the
triple's informational address (worked numerically for all three leptons in
\S\ref{sec:nvalues_to_masses}).
The dimensional scale of the engine is set by the single anchor $m_\tau$; the
hadronic sector's separate scale is the BPS kink mass
$\Mkink = \tfrac{8}{49}\,m_\tau = 290.10$~MeV (\S\ref{sec:hadrons}).

\subsubsection*{The Elegant Kernel}

The coefficient vector $\mathbf{k}$ is not a free parameter fitted to masses; it is
a rigid algebraic structure dictated by GTE symmetries.  The Quarter-Lock Law
(\lean{quarterLockLaw}, \CatAL, zero sorry) forces the exact relation
$k_M = k_{\rm gen2} + \tfrac{1}{4}k_{L^2}$ among the coefficients.  Combined with
additional UGP symmetry constraints, this fixes $\mathbf{k}$ to the
\textbf{Elegant Kernel}:

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=yellow!8,colframe=yellow!50!black,
  title={\textbf{The Elegant Kernel} (UCL coefficient vector, \CatA)}]
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\;\begin{aligned}
k_{L^2} &= \tfrac{7}{512}, \qquad & k_{\rm gen2} &= -\tfrac{\varphi}{2}, \\[3pt]
k_{\rm gen} &= \varphi\cos\!\bigl(\tfrac{\pi}{10}\bigr), \qquad &
k_M &= -\tfrac{\varphi}{2} + \tfrac{7}{2048}, \\[3pt]
(k_a, k_b, k_c) &= \bigl(\tfrac{1}{8},\, -\tfrac{3}{2},\, \tfrac{4}{3}\bigr), \qquad &
k_0' &= -\tfrac{1}{2\pi},
\end{aligned}\;}
\label{eq:elegant_kernel_p48}
\end{equation}
where $\varphi = (1+\sqrt{5})/2$ is the golden ratio.
The linear coefficient $k_L$ is fixed by the base-change convention that rationalizes $k_{L^2}$.
The full derivation is in \cite{Spivack2025UGP}; the Quarter-Lock identity is
machine-checked as \lean{quarterLockLaw} (ugp-lean, zero sorry).
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsubsection*{Why the Tau Mass Is the Single Anchor}

The UCL maps triples to dimensionless calibration factors; physical masses require one
dimensional anchor.  That anchor is $m_\tau$, which is the unique self-consistency
condition (SCC) fixed point of the lepton cascade: the field mass
$m_\varphi \equiv m_\tau$ is the value at which the cascade's own output, fed back
as the potential parameter, reproduces itself
(\lean{mphi\_equals\_tau\_mass\_scc}, \CatAL, zero sorry).
All 9 fermion mass predictions therefore follow from
(i) the GTE cascade triples, (ii) the Elegant Kernel, and (iii) $m_\tau$ as the single
dimensional anchor --- with zero continuously adjustable parameters at prediction time.
The complete numeric chain --- feature vector, M\"obius values, locked
coefficient vector, calibration factor, base energy, and final mass --- is
worked for all three charged leptons in \S\ref{sec:nvalues_to_masses}.

\subsection*{The Tau Mass Anchor and the SCC}

The tau mass $m_\tau = 1776.86$~MeV is the self-consistency condition (SCC) fixed point
of the lepton cascade.  The field mass $m_\varphi \equiv m_\tau$ is the parameter that
fixes the $\PHIMDL$ potential (Ch.~\ref{chap:field}), and the BPS kink mass is then
$\Mkink = (8/49)m_\tau = 290.10$~MeV.  All subsequent fermion mass predictions
use $m_\tau$ as the single anchor.  Since $m_\tau$ is an output of the SCC (not a
free fit), the number of continuously adjustable parameters at prediction time is zero.

\subsection*{The 1000-Permutation Null Test}

The nine-fermion agreement with zero parameters could in principle be a coincidence
of the functional form.  To test this, the canonical pipeline's 1000-permutation null
suite applies the same locked UCL functional form to 1000 random permutations of the
triple arithmetic --- e.g., randomly reassigning the $b$-values among particles ---
and re-scores each permutation.  The canonical fit's primary $\sigma = 2.95\times10^{-5}$
falls outside the \emph{entire} shuffled-null distribution: the minimum permutation
$\sigma$ exceeds $5.6\times10^{-2}$, more than three orders of magnitude above the
canonical baseline.  This rules out coincidence at high significance and confirms that
the agreement reflects genuine arithmetic structure in the cascade --- the specific
arithmetic content of the canonical triples, not a forgiving parametric ansatz
(P01 \cite{SpivackSM}).

\subsection*{Honest Disclosure: Certification Status}

The nine lepton and quark masses are \CatAD (computational) with Lean-certified
containment intervals for all six quarks.  The connection between the orbit cascade
$b$-values and the physical quark masses involves the GTE cascade at ridge $n=10$
and quark seed triples; these steps are computational (\CatA) and the full analytic
derivation has not been formalized in Lean.  The lepton seed $(1,73,823)$ is
\CatAL\ via the FGCI theorem; the cascade arithmetic beyond the seed is \CatA.

\section{Neutrino Masses and Mixing}
\label{sec:neutrinos}

The neutrino sector is the most precisely confirmed domain for GTE predictions beyond
the SM.  The mass-squared ratio $\Delta m^2_{21}/\Delta m^2_{31}$ is predicted to
$0.16\sigma$ from NuFIT~6.0 without any neutrino mass input.  All three PMNS mixing
angles are predicted from orbit-ratio formulas with zero free parameters.
All comparisons use \textbf{NuFIT~6.0 (IC24, NH)} \cite{NuFIT60}.

\subsection*{Normal Ordering Predicted}

The GTE seesaw structure gives normal mass ordering ($m_1 < m_2 < m_3$) as the natural
outcome.  The Braid Atlas $b$-values $\{5, 11, 19\}$ for the neutrino sector satisfy
$b_1 < b_2 < b_3$, which directly implies normal ordering via the mass-squared formula
(eq.~\eqref{eq:mnu_ratio} below).  Inverted ordering would require $b_2 < b_1$, which
violates the orbit-ordering condition.  Normal ordering is thus predicted, and NuFIT~6.0
IC24 disfavors inverted ordering by $\Delta\chi^2 = 6.1$ ($\approx 2.5\sigma$), consistent with
the GTE prediction.
The seed ordering $b_{R,1} < b_{R,2} < b_{R,3}$ underlying this prediction is
machine-certified as a structural consequence of the GTE seesaw
(\lean{seesaw\_normal\_ordering\_from\_seed\_ordering}, \CatAL), with $b_{R,3} = 19$
identified as the unique Eisenstein norm $\mathcal{N}(-5{-}3\omega)$~(\CatAL)
via the octonionic structure of the right-handed seed~\cite{SpivackOctonionicShadow}.

\subsection*{Mass-Squared Ratio from Braid Atlas $b$-Values}

The neutrino mass-squared ratio is derived from the Braid Atlas $b$-values using the
structural exponent $29/9 = \Nc + \theta_{\rm Koide}$ (established independently in
the charged-lepton sector \cite{Spivack2026_Koide}):
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\Delta m^2_{21}}{\Delta m^2_{31}}
  = \frac{b_2^{58/9} - b_1^{58/9}}{b_3^{58/9} - b_1^{58/9}}
  = \frac{11^{58/9} - 5^{58/9}}{19^{58/9} - 5^{58/9}}
  = 0.02936.
  \label{eq:mnu_ratio}
\end{equation}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Headline Result: Neutrino Mass-Squared Ratio (\CatAL)}]
\[
  \Delta m^2_{21}/\Delta m^2_{31} = 0.02936\quad \text{(GTE)},
  \quad 0.02951\pm0.00098\quad \text{(NuFIT~6.0 IC24 NH)}.
\]
Deviation: $\mathbf{0.16\sigma}$ ($0.52\%$).  Zero neutrino mass inputs.\\[2pt]
Lean certification: \lean{gte\_delta\_m21\_sq\_bounds}, \lean{gte\_delta\_m31\allowbreak\_sq\_bounds} (\CatAL,
zero sorry, zero custom axioms) \cite{SpivackNeutrino}.

\subsection*{Absolute Neutrino Masses}

Using the GUT-scale seesaw with right-handed neutrino mass $M_R$ derived from the
GTE orbit structure:
\begin{align}
  \Sigma m_\nu &= 59.4~\text{meV} \quad (\CatA),

consistent with the Planck~2018 upper bound $\Sigma m_\nu < 120$~meV (95\% CL) \cite{SpivackNeutrino}.
The normal-ordering value $\Sigma m_\nu \approx 60$~meV is within the target
sensitivity of CMB-S4 and Euclid.

\subsection*{PMNS CP Phase and Jarlskog Invariant}

The PMNS CP phase derives from the $\ZS$ orbit fraction:
\begin{equation}
  \delta_{\rm CP}^{\rm PMNS} = \frac{4}{7}\times 360^\circ = 205.71^\circ
  \quad (\lean{pmns\_cp\_phase\_from\_z7\_winding},\;\CatAL).
  \label{eq:delta_cp}
\end{equation}
NuFIT~6.0 IC24 NH best fit: $212^\circ\,{}^{+26}_{-41}$.  Deviation: $-0.15\sigma$.
DUNE will constrain $\delta_{\rm CP}$ to $\pm10$--$15^\circ$, providing a decisive test.

The Jarlskog CP-invariant is:
\begin{equation}
  J_{\rm GTE} = -\frac{8184\,\sqrt{437}}{5057221}\sin(\pi/7) = -1.468\times10^{-2}
  \quad (\CatAL;\;\lean{gte\_jarlskog}).
\end{equation}
The denominator factorizes as $5057221 = 13\times73^3 = c_H \times b_{L_1}^3$, a pure
GTE orbit identity \cite{SpivackNeutrino}.  Note: the discrepancy with the PDG value
$J\approx -9.87\times10^{-3}$ ($49\%$) traces entirely to the difference between
the GTE $\delta_{\rm CP} = 205.71^\circ$ and the PDG best-fit $\delta\approx197^\circ$,
not to errors in the mixing angle formulas.

\subsection*{Leptogenesis Feasibility}

The efficiency parameter for thermal leptogenesis via the FKTT mechanism
(Ch.~\ref{chap:cosmology}) is:
\begin{equation}
  K_1 = 15.93
  \quad (\CatA).
  \label{eq:K1}
\end{equation}
This value is in the strong-washout regime ($K_1 \gg 1$), which is compatible with
the observed baryon asymmetry $\eta_B = 6.10\times10^{-10}$ when the FKTT coupling
$g_{\rm kink\text{-}top} = \varepsilon_{\rm FN}$ is used (Ch.~\ref{chap:cosmology}).
Approximately $77\%$ of natural Yukawa texture variants consistent with the orbit
structure are also consistent with the observed baryon asymmetry.

\section{EFT Operator Decomposition at \texorpdfstring{$M_{\rm GUT}$}{M-GUT}}
\label{sec:eft_gut}

At the GUT scale $M_{\rm GUT} \approx 1.9\times10^{16}$~GeV, the $\PHIMDL$ kink
background generates effective operators that connect the particle spectrum to the
baryogenesis mechanism of Chapter~\ref{chap:cosmology}.  This section presents the
two-operator decomposition and explains why the operators do not mix.

\subsection*{Two Effective Operators at $M_{\rm GUT}$}

The $\PHIMDL$ field at the GUT scale supports two distinct vertex types, organized
by their topological charge $Q_{\rm top}$ under the $\ZS$ winding structure:

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=green!5,colframe=green!50!black,title={EFT Operator Decomposition at $M_{\rm GUT}$ (\CatAD)}]
\begin{align*}
O_1 &= \bar{q}_L \tilde{H} t_R + \text{h.c.},\quad Q_{\rm top} = 0,
  \quad c_1 = y_t = 0.461 \quad (\CatAD), \\
O_2 &= \bar{t}_R \PHIMDL N_R + \text{h.c.},\quad Q_{\rm top} = 1,
  \quad c_2 = g_{\rm kink\text{-}top} = \varepsilon_{\rm FN} \quad (\CatAL).
\end{align*}
Here $\varepsilon_{\rm FN} = e^{-\pi/\Nc} = e^{-\pi/3}$ is the Frobenius--Nijenhuis
suppression factor.  Lean certification of $c_2 = \varepsilon_{\rm FN}$:
\lean{kink\_top\_coupling\_eq\_eps\_FN} (\CatAL, zero sorry, zero axioms)
\cite{SpivackGTECosmology}.
\end{tcolorbox}

The two operators are structurally distinct.  $O_1$ is the standard Yukawa operator
that gives the top quark its physical mass $m_t = y_t v = 0.461 \times 246$~GeV~$= 113$~GeV
at the Higgs VEV $v = 246$~GeV ($m_t$ in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme at $\mu=m_t$;
the on-shell pole mass $172.6$~GeV includes QCD corrections).  $O_2$ is the kink--top
coupling that generates the Dirac Yukawa entry $m_{D_1}$ in the seesaw, which in turn
drives the FKTT leptogenesis mechanism of Ch.~\ref{chap:cosmology}.

\subsection*{Why $O_1$ and $O_2$ Do Not Mix}

The key structural fact preventing mixing between $O_1$ and $O_2$ is $\ZS$ baryon
number conservation.  $O_1$ has topological charge $Q_{\rm top} = 0$: it conserves
the total $\ZS$ winding number.  $O_2$ has $Q_{\rm top} = 1$: it changes the winding
number by one unit via the kink background.  Since $\ZS$ baryon number is a topological
invariant (\lean{gte\_baryon\_number\_topological\_charge}, \CatAL), no perturbative
or non-perturbative process can mix sectors with different topological charge.
$O_1$ and $O_2$ are in distinct topological superselection sectors.

This has a concrete physical consequence: the top-quark Yukawa coupling $y_t$ (from $O_1$)
and the leptogenesis Yukawa coupling $g_{\rm kink\text{-}top}$ (from $O_2$) run under
the renormalization group independently.  The leptogenesis prediction $\eta_B =
6.109\times10^{-10}$ (\CatAL) is therefore not affected by the running of $y_t$:
the two Yukawa couplings are in separate $\ZS$ topological sectors.

\subsection*{The Frobenius--Nijenhuis Suppression and $\eta_B$}

The coupling $c_2 = \varepsilon_{\rm FN} = e^{-\pi/3}$ is derived from the BPS
instanton action of the $\PHIMDL$ kink in the $Q_{\rm top}=1$ sector.  The BPS
saturation condition $S_{\rm instanton} = \pi/\Nc = \pi/3$ follows from the kink
profile of Ch.~\ref{chap:field}; the coupling $g_{\rm kink\text{-}top} = e^{-S}$
is then the semiclassical amplitude for crossing the instanton barrier.  This gives
$m_{D_1} = g_{\rm kink\text{-}top} \cdot v_{\rm GUT}$, which feeds into the seesaw
Yukawa matrix and ultimately determines $\eta_B$.

The chain: $\varepsilon_{\rm FN} \to m_{D_1} \to$ seesaw $\to M_{R_1} \to
\Gamma_{N_1} \to \varepsilon_{CP}^{(1)} \to \eta_B = 6.109\times10^{-10}$
is carried out in detail in Ch.~\ref{chap:cosmology}.  The endpoint is the most
precisely certified prediction in the framework: $\eta_B$ at $+0.15\sigma$
from the Planck~2018 measurement, Lean-certified (\CatAL, zero sorry, zero axioms).

\subsection*{Certification Status and Open Item}

The two-operator decomposition is \CatAD: the operator content is structurally
derived from the $\PHIMDL$ action at the GUT scale, but the full Wilsonian path-integral
matching --- which would integrate out the kink modes at $M_{\rm GUT}$ to obtain
explicit Wilson coefficients in the effective SM Lagrangian --- has not been carried out.

\begin{openprob}[Wilsonian EFT Matching at $M_{\rm GUT}$]
\label{oprob:eft_gut}
The full Wilsonian EFT calculation --- explicit path-integral integration over $\PHIMDL$
kink modes at $M_{\rm GUT}$ to obtain the complete operator basis and Wilson coefficients
--- remains open (\CatD\ target).  The two operators $O_1$ and $O_2$ are identified
structurally; their precise Wilson coefficients beyond leading order require the full
calculation.  The non-mixing argument based on topological charge is \CatAL\ and is
not affected by this gap.
\end{openprob}

\section{\texorpdfstring{$\mathbb{Z}_7$}{Z7} Winding Conservation and All SM Vertices}
\label{sec:z7_vertices}

In electrodynamics, the conservation of electric charge at every vertex is so fundamental
that it is built into the very definition of a gauge theory.  An electron emits a photon
and remains an electron because electric charge is exactly conserved.  In \GTE{}, there is
a deeper conservation law: $\ZS$ \emph{winding conservation}.  At every Standard Model
interaction vertex, the total $\ZS$ winding number of the ingoing states equals the total
$\ZS$ winding number of the outgoing states, modulo~7.  Electric charge conservation is a
consequence of this more fundamental law, not an independent postulate.

\subsection*{Winding Conservation at All 33 SM Vertices}

The winding numbers for all SM particles were established in \S\ref{sec:winding_qn} and
recorded in Table~\ref{tab:p48_winding}.  At every SM interaction vertex, the total
$\ZS$ winding of the ingoing lines equals the total $\ZS$ winding of the outgoing lines
(mod~7).  This is not a postulate but a theorem: it follows from the $\ZS$ symmetry of
the $\PHIMDL$ Lagrangian.  When kinks scatter, the total $\ZS$ winding of the final state
must equal that of the initial state, because the winding number is the topological
invariant that the field cannot change continuously.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Result: $\ZS$ Winding Conservation at SM Vertices (\CatAL)}]
All 33 Standard Model interaction vertices conserve $\ZS$ winding number.
This is a theorem, not a postulate, following from the $\ZS$ symmetry of the
$\PHIMDL$ Lagrangian.  Electric charge conservation
is the projection of this conservation law onto the degree-1 sector
\cite{SpivackGTEUnification,SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}.
\end{tcolorbox}

To see how winding conservation generates the SM's interactions, consider the
charged-current weak vertex $u \to d + W^+$.  In the canonical winding language
(Table~\ref{tab:p48_winding}), $w_u = 2$ (up-type quark), $w_d = 6$ (down-type quark),
and the $W^+$ boson carries $w = 3$.  Winding conservation:
\[
  w_d + w_{W^+} \equiv 6 + 3 = 9 \equiv 2 \equiv w_u \pmod{7} \quad \checkmark
\]
Charge conservation follows from the centred-representative formula $Q = w_{\rm c}/3$:
$Q_u = +2/3$, $Q_d = -1/3$, $Q_{W^+} = +1$, and indeed $+2/3 = -1/3 + 1$.

The five PSC-admissible winding sectors $\{0, 2, 3, 4, 6\}$ of $\ZS$ give the
complete SM particle-sector structure; sectors $\{1, 5\}$ are PSC-forbidden
(dark/mirror-branch states not present as stable asymptotic SM particles).
The particle assignments are shown in Table~\ref{tab:six_arrows_forces}.
This is the GTE version of the bidirectional correspondence between
$\Phi_{\MDL}$, the $f_{\MDL}$ rule, the GTE polynomial, and the SM
\cite{SpivackGTEUnification}.

\subsection*{The Charge Formula}

The electric charge of any SM particle follows from the degree-1 projection of the
\GTE{} polynomial.  The center projection $p(0, w, 0) = w$ is linear in the winding number
$w$ of the single active tape.  Dividing by the number of colors:
\begin{equation}
  Q = \frac{p(0, w, 0)}{3} = \frac{w_{\rm centered}}{3},
  \label{eq:charge_formula_forces}
\end{equation}
where $w_{\rm centered}$ is the centered representative of $w \in \ZS$ in the range
$[-3, 3]$.  For $w = 1$: $Q = 1/3$ (down quark); $w = 2$: $Q = 2/3$ (up quark); $w = 3$:
$Q = 1$ (charged lepton); $w = 0$: $Q = 0$ (neutrino, photon).
This charge formula is \CatAL, machine-certified in
\lean{gte\_charge\_is\allowbreak\_linear\_projection}
\cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}.  Electric charge is not a free parameter; it is an integer
multiple of $1/3$ by necessity, with the denominator fixed by the number of colors $\Nc
= 3 = \Ngen$.

\subsection*{The Degree Split: Electromagnetism vs.\ Gravity}

The polynomial $p(L,C,R) = C + R - CR - LCR$ has two physically critical specializations:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Degree-1 (center projection):} $p(0, w, 0) = w$ — linear in $w$.  This is the
  electromagnetic sector: a particle on a single tape is electrically charged.  The source
  of the electromagnetic field is the winding of a single spatial direction.

\item \textbf{Degree-3 (diagonal):} $p(w, w, w) = 2w - w^2 - w^3$ — cubic in $w$.  This is
  the gravitational sector: the coupling to the gravitational source requires all three
  tapes to be simultaneously non-vacuum ($p(w, 0, 0) = 0$ for all $w$, machine-certified
  as \lean{gravity\_requires\_cross\_tape\_coordination}, \CatAL).  Gravity couples to the
  full three-spatial-dimension structure of a particle; electromagnetism couples to the
  particle's existence on any one tape.
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Result: Gravity/EM Degree Split (\CatAL)}]
From the same 19-bit polynomial, gravity arises from the degree-3 diagonal
$p(w,w,w) = 2w - w^2 - w^3$ and electromagnetism from the degree-1 center projection
$p(0,w,0) = w$.  This is a theorem, not a choice: the \MDL-unique polynomial necessarily
has degree-1 EM and degree-3 gravity because those are the degrees of the two natural
specializations of a three-variable cubic with three spatial tape variables.\\[4pt]
Lean certification: \lean{gravity\_em\_degree\_split} (\CatAL, zero sorry)
\cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}.
\end{tcolorbox}

The physical consequence of the degree split is stark.  Electric charge grows as $w^1$
(linear charge quantization: $Q = 0, \pm 1/3, \pm 2/3, \pm 1$).  Gravitational mass
grows as $w^3$ (cubic: the mass hierarchy among SM particles follows from
$p(w,w,w) \in \{5, 6\}$ for massive sectors).  Neither is fine-tuned; both are the
degree-1 and degree-3 terms of one polynomial evaluated at one of two natural
specializations.

This degree split is the arithmetic shadow of a structural distinction that runs through
all of theoretical physics: electromagnetism is a $\mathrm{U}(1)$ phase (one dimension of
coupling), while gravity couples to the energy-momentum tensor (all spatial dimensions
coordinated).  The polynomial captures this in two lines of arithmetic.

\subsection*{Three Abelian Gauge Fields}

The $\PHIMDL$ architecture contains three abelian gauge fields arising from the three
independent winding sectors of the three-tape structure.  These are: the electromagnetic
$\mathrm{U}(1)_Y$ hypercharge sector (degree-1 projection), the $\mathrm{U}(1)_3$ weak
isospin sector (degree-2 cross-tape projection), and the $\mathrm{U}(1)_B$ baryon-number
sector (topological, arising from degree-3 diagonal).  Full derivation in
\cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure,SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}; summary in \S\ref{sec:forces_summary}.

\section{Color Confinement from MDL}
\label{sec:confinement}

Why can we never see a free quark?  In QCD, color confinement is an experimentally
observed fact for which there exists no fully analytic proof from first principles in
continuum quantum field theory.  The question has been open since the 1970s and is one of
the Millennium Prize Problems of mathematics.  In \GTE{}, confinement follows from a
simple \MDL{} argument: it costs more bits to describe a free colored quark than a
color-neutral hadron.  The universe adopts the shorter description.

The discovery that confinement is an \MDL{} result --- not a dynamical mystery ---
was, for me, one of the most surprising outcomes of the framework.  The Millennium
Prize Problem of confinement has resisted solution for fifty years because researchers
sought a dynamical mechanism within QCD.  The \GTE{} answer operates one level up:
confinement is not about QCD dynamics; it is about which states are \MDL-admissible.
The dynamical question of \emph{how} a quark is confined is real and is addressed at
Level~2 (string tension, Wilson loop).  The structural question of \emph{why} no free
quark exists as an asymptotic state is answered at Level~1 by a three-line computation.

\subsection*{The MDL Description-Length Gap}

A free colored quark in an asymptotic state occupies one tape of the three-tape \CMCA{}
with a specific color (which of the three tapes) and a specific winding sector (which of
the quark winding values).  The \MDL{} description length of this state is:
\begin{equation}
  K_{\rm colored}(w, 0, 0) = \log_2 3 + \log_2 15 = \log_2 45 \text{ bits},
  \label{eq:k_colored}
\end{equation}
where $\log_2 3$ bits encode the choice of active tape (which color) and $\log_2 15$ bits
encode the winding value on the active tape.

A color-neutral hadron, by contrast, has all three tapes sharing the same \PSC-admissible
winding value.  Its description length is:
\begin{equation}
  K_{\rm neutral}(w, w, w) = \log_2 5 \text{ bits},
  \label{eq:k_neutral}
\end{equation}
since only 5 distinct \PSC-admissible winding values exist (the \PSC-admissible sector
derived in Chapter~\ref{chap:particles}).

The description-length gap is:
\begin{equation}
  \Delta K = K_{\rm colored} - K_{\rm neutral}
  = \log_2 45 - \log_2 5 = \log_2 9 \approx 3.17 \text{ bits} > 0.
  \label{eq:dk_confinement}
\end{equation}
Because $\Delta K > 0$, a free colored quark is \MDL-non-minimal.  The \PSC{} principle
forbids \MDL-non-minimal asymptotic states.  Therefore, no free colored quark exists as
an asymptotic state.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Result: Color Confinement from MDL (\CatAL)}]
A free colored quark has description length $\log_2 45$ bits; a color-neutral hadron has
$\log_2 5$ bits.  The gap $\Delta K = \log_2 9 \approx 3.17$ bits is positive, so free
colored quarks are \MDL-non-minimal and are forbidden as asymptotic states by \PSC{}.\\[4pt]
Lean certification: \lean{color\_confinement\_k\_extra\_pos} (\CatAL, zero sorry,
\lean{ColorConfinementMDL.lean}) \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{What the MDL Theorem Proves and What It Does Not}

The \MDL{} confinement theorem establishes the \emph{existence} of confinement: free
colored quarks cannot appear as asymptotic states because they would require more bits to
describe than any color-neutral alternative.  This is a rigorous theorem.

What the \MDL{} theorem does \emph{not} provide is the \emph{dynamical mechanism}: how
the confining potential $V(r) \sim \sigma r$ grows linearly with distance, what the QCD
string is, or the precise value of the string tension $\sigma$.  These are Level-2 QCD
dynamical phenomena.  The MDL theorem operates at Level 1: it tells us what state space
the universe is allowed to access, not the Hamiltonian that governs the approach to
equilibrium within that state space.

An analogy clarifies the distinction.  A thermodynamic argument tells us that water at
standard pressure cannot exist as a gas below 100\,°C --- it is thermodynamically
non-minimal.  But thermodynamics alone does not tell us the speed of condensation droplet
formation.  The \MDL{} theorem is the \GTE{} thermodynamic argument for confinement.

\subsection*{The Mass Gap}

The Yang--Mills mass gap problem (another Millennium Prize Problem) asks whether pure
$\mathrm{SU}(3)$ gauge theory in four dimensions has a strictly positive mass gap.  In
\GTE{}, the mass gap follows directly from the orbit arithmetic of the $F_{21}$ Frobenius
group: there are no massless colored excitations in the confinement sector
\cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Result: QCD Mass Gap (\CatAL)}]
The \GTE{} color sector has a strictly positive mass gap $\Delta E > 0$.  No massless
colored excitation exists in the confinement-phase vacuum.  This follows from orbit
arithmetic: the $F_{21}$ orbit structure has no massless mode in its color-singlet sector.
Lean certification: \lean{qft\_gauged\_mass\_gap\allowbreak\_pos\_unconditional} (\CatAL, zero sorry)
\cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{QCD String Tension at the EFT Level}

At the level of the \GTE{} effective field theory (below the scale $\Lambda_{\GTE} =
7\,\Mkink \approx 2.0$~GeV --- the seven-kink full-winding threshold, derived rather than
calibrated: tree reading $(8/7)m_\tau = 2.031$~GeV, \CatAD; quantum-corrected reading
$7M^Q = 1.97 \pm 0.15$~GeV, \CatA; the two agree within $0.5\sigma$, envelope
$1.96 \pm 0.15$~GeV, band $< 10\%$ \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}), the confining string
tension was derived in Chapter~\ref{chap:particles}
from the kink condensate:
\begin{equation}
  \sigma_{\rm string} = \tfrac{9}{4} \Mkink^2 = 0.18920~\text{GeV}^2 \qquad
  (\CatAD;\;\text{eq.}~\eqref{eq:string_tension}).
  \label{eq:string_tension_ref}
\end{equation}
The prefactor $9/4$ is the $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ adjoint Casimir.  This result is within
$0.04\sigma$ of the $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ lattice QCD benchmark \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.

\subsection*{QCD Color Factors}

The color factors that appear throughout QCD amplitudes are determined by the Casimir
elements of $F_{21}$, not by independent postulation.  They agree exactly with the
$\mathrm{SU}(3)$ values:
\begin{equation}
  C_F = \frac{4}{3}, \quad C_A = 3, \quad T_F = \frac{1}{2}.
\end{equation}
\noindent
(\CatAL; \lean{frobenius\_casimir\_fundamental}, \lean{frobenius\_casimir\_adjoint},
\lean{frobenius\_dynkin\_index\_fundamental}).

These values are not fitted \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.  They follow from the representation theory of $F_{21} =
\ZS \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3$: the fundamental representation has Casimir $C_F = 4/3$, the
adjoint has $C_A = 3$, and the trace normalization gives $T_F = 1/2$.  The agreement with
$\mathrm{SU}(3)$ QCD is not a coincidence --- it is the content of the \GTE{} statement
that $F_{21}$ is the discrete arithmetic substrate of the $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ color sector.

\subsection*{Asymptotic Freedom Preview}

The fact that the QCD coupling decreases at short distances (asymptotic freedom) requires
the one-loop $\beta$-function coefficient $b_0 > 0$.  The value of $b_0$ is derived in
\S\ref{sec:asymptotic}: $b_0 = 7 = |\ZS|$ from the Casimir relation
(eq.~\eqref{eq:casimir}).  Since $b_0 > 0$, the $F_{21}$ substrate automatically gives an
asymptotically free color sector.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=yellow!8,colframe=yellow!45!black,title={Why This Is Not a Circular Argument}]
The $\MDL$ confinement theorem does not assume confinement and derive $\Delta K > 0$.
It takes as input only the definition of \MDL{} description length, the structure of the
$\ZS$-winding state space, and the $\PSC$ admissibility condition.  From these three
inputs, it derives that free colored quarks are \MDL-non-minimal.  There is no circular
reasoning: confinement is an output, not an assumption.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section{The Electroweak Sector}
\label{sec:ew}

The electroweak interaction unifies electromagnetism and the weak nuclear force at energies
above approximately 100~GeV.  In the SM, the Weinberg angle, the $W$ and $Z$ boson masses,
the Higgs vacuum expectation value (VEV), and the Higgs mass are all measured
experimentally; the theory does not predict their values.  In \GTE{}, all of them are
theorems.

\subsection*{The Weinberg Angle}

The electroweak mixing angle is defined by $\sigW \equiv g'^2 / (g^2 + g'^2)$, where $g$
is the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ coupling and $g'$ is the $\mathrm{U}(1)_Y$ coupling.  In the
SM, $\sigW$ is a free parameter fitted to experiment.  In \GTE{}, it is the ratio of the
generation count $\Ngen$ to the Higgs-sector orbit count $c_H$:
\begin{equation}
  \sigW = \frac{\Ngen}{c_H} = \frac{3}{13} = 0.23077.
  \label{eq:weinberg_angle}
\end{equation}
\noindent(\CatAL;\;\lean{weinberg\_angle\_closure}, \lean{weinberg\_angle\_derivation}.)
Here $c_H = 13$ is the Higgs color count: the number of distinct $\ZS$ orbit sectors
accessible to the Higgs doublet under the $F_{21}$ action, which is fixed by the
three-tape architecture.  This formula was first derived in \cite{SpivackWeinbergAngle}
and extended to the full electroweak sector in \cite{SpivackGTEUnification}.

The tree-level value $\sigW = 3/13 = 0.23077$ is a pure arithmetic result.  The two-loop
threshold-corrected value, including the QED and electroweak running from $M_Z$ down to
$q^2 = 0$, is:
\begin{align}
  \sigW\big|_{\rm 2\text{-}loop}
  &= 0.23129\;154 \qquad
  (\CatAD;\;\lean{sin2\_theta\_W\_threshold\_interval}).
\end{align}

\subsection*{The Self-Referential Renormalization Group and the Higgs VEV}

\paragraph{What the SRRG is.}
The \textbf{Self-Referential Renormalization Group} (\SRRG{}) is the renormalization group
whose $\beta$-function equation is the GTE polynomial applied to its own coupling:
\begin{equation}
  \beta(g) = 0 \;\Longleftrightarrow\; g = p(g,g,g).
  \label{eq:srrg_def}
\end{equation}
A coupling $g^*$ is a fixed point if and only if it satisfies $p(g^*,g^*,g^*) = g^*$.
Evaluating the GTE polynomial on the diagonal,
\begin{equation}
  p(g,g,g) = g + g - g^2 - g^3 = 2g - g^2 - g^3,
\end{equation}
so the fixed-point equation is $2g^* - (g^*)^2 - (g^*)^3 = g^*$, which simplifies to
$(g^*)^2 + g^* = 1$.
The unique positive real root is
\begin{equation}
  g^* = \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2} = \varphi, \qquad \varphi^2 + \varphi = 1.
  \label{eq:srrg_golden}
\end{equation}
This is the golden ratio: the unique positive real solution of $x^2 + x = 1$.

\paragraph{MDL interpretation.}
The fixed point $g^* = \varphi$ is \MDL-minimizing: it is the coupling at which the
\SRRG{} $\beta$-function changes sign from negative to positive, making the electroweak
vacuum the global \MDL\ minimum.  The theorem \lean{op9\_catal\_unconditional} (\CatAL,
ugp-lean, zero sorry, zero custom axioms) establishes this unconditionally: no external
input, no named assumption about the physical substrate, and no reference to measured
SM parameters \cite{SpivackSRRG,SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}.

\paragraph{The Higgs VEV.}
The Higgs vacuum expectation value $v_H$ sets the scale of electroweak symmetry breaking.
In the SM, $v_H = 246.22$~GeV is extracted from the Fermi constant $G_F$; it is not
predicted.  In \GTE{}, $v_H$ is the self-consistent fixed point of the \SRRG{} flow
\cite{SpivackSRRG}.  The \SRRG{} fixed point gives $g^* = \varphi = (\sqrt{5}-1)/2$ as
the MDL-minimizing coupling.

The Higgs VEV follows from inserting the fixed-point coupling into the \SRRG{}
scaling relation:
\begin{equation}
  v_{\rm PSC} = 246.16~\text{GeV} \qquad
  (-0.024\% \text{ from PDG } 246.22~\text{GeV};\;\CatAL).
  \label{eq:higgs_vev}
\end{equation}
