\subsection*{The $V{-}A$ Structure of the Charged Current}

The chiral structure of the weak charged current --- the empirical fact that the $W$
boson couples only to left-handed fermions, with vector and axial couplings in the
ratio $g_A/g_V = -1$ --- is a derived consequence of the \CMCA\ tape topology.  The two
chiral tapes of the \CMCA\ carry opposite topological winding numbers: the right-moving
tape (Rule~110 kink, $0 \to +2\pi/7$) has $w_R = +1$, and the left-moving tape
(Rule~124 anti-kink, $0 \to -2\pi/7$) has $w_L = -1$.  The chiral $\mathbb{Z}_2$
spatial reflection $s \in \mathrm{AGL}(1,7)$ that swaps Rule~110 with Rule~124
(§\ref{sec:f21}) forces $w_L = -w_R$ exactly
\mbox{(\lean{tape\_chiral\_signs\_opposite}, \CatAL)}.

The topological vector current is the symmetric combination
$J_V \propto w_R + w_L = 0$, which vanishes identically
\mbox{(\lean{j\_vector\_tape\_sum\_zero}, \CatAL)}, while the axial current is the
antisymmetric combination $J_A \propto w_R - w_L = 2 \neq 0$
\mbox{(\lean{phimdl\_axial\_current\_discrete\_constant}, \CatAL)}.  The right-handed
(symmetric) sector of the weak current therefore carries exactly zero topological
charge; the left-handed (antisymmetric) sector carries the full charge.  Via the
Algebraic Lifting Theorem this yields, at \CatAD,
\[
  g_R = 0 \quad\text{exactly}, \qquad \frac{g_A}{g_V} = -1,
\]
i.e.\ pure $V{-}A$ with zero free parameters
\mbox{(\lean{va\_coupling\_exact\_from\_tape\_topology}, \CatAD;}
\mbox{\lean{va\_op6\_bundle}, \CatAD)}.  The derivation is in fact stronger than the
SM statement: the vector current vanishes at the \CMCA\ level ($V = 0$), so the
charged-current interaction is purely axial --- a statement equivalent to $V{-}A$
after normalisation.  This closes the quantitative half of the weak-chirality problem;
the qualitative $V{-}A$ theorem was established in the three-tape construction
\cite{SpivackThreeTapeCMCA}.

\section{Strong CP: Zero by Structure}
\label{sec:strong_cp}

The QCD Lagrangian admits a topological term:
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{L}_{\theta} = \theta_{\rm QCD}
  \cdot \frac{g_s^2}{32\pi^2} \,
  \mathrm{tr}\!\left(F^{\mu\nu}\tilde{F}_{\mu\nu}\right).
  \label{eq:theta_term}
\end{equation}
This term violates CP symmetry in the strong sector.  The parameter $\theta_{\rm QCD}$
can in principle take any value in $[0, 2\pi)$; there is no symmetry principle in the SM
that forces it to be small.  Yet the experimental bound from the neutron electric dipole
moment constrains $|\theta_{\rm QCD}| < 10^{-10}$.  Why is $\theta_{\rm QCD}$ so
extraordinarily small?  This is the strong CP problem, one of the deepest fine-tuning
puzzles in the SM.

The two candidate solutions in the SM literature are:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Peccei--Quinn axion mechanism:} introduce a new global $\mathrm{U}(1)_{\rm PQ}$
  symmetry and a pseudo-Nambu--Goldstone boson (axion) that dynamically relaxes $\theta \to 0$.
  Decades of experimental null results at ADMX, HAYSTAC, ABRACADABRA, and BabyIAXO have
  not yet found the axion.
\item \textbf{$\theta = 0$ exactly:} $\theta_{\rm QCD}$ is exactly zero for some structural
  reason, so no axion is required.  The SM offers no such reason.  \GTE{} does.
\end{itemize}

In \GTE{}, $\theta_{\rm QCD} = 0$ is not a fine-tuning.  It is a theorem, following from
three independent proofs based on the group-theoretic structure of the $F_{21} = \ZS
\rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3$ Frobenius group that underlies the \GTE{} color sector.  All three
proofs are machine-certified (\CatAL{}, zero sorry).

\subsection*{Proof 1: Trivial Center (Group Theory)}

The center of $F_{21}$ is trivial: $Z(F_{21}) = \{e\}$.

For the $\theta$ term to contribute a non-zero value to the QCD Lagrangian, the gauge
group must have non-contractible holonomy in the color-singlet sector --- the vacuum
winding needed to generate instantons.  A group with a trivial center has no
non-contractible holonomy in the vacuum sector: the fundamental group of the quotient
$F_{21}/Z(F_{21}) = F_{21}/\{e\} = F_{21}$ is trivial in the relevant color-singlet
sector.  No instantons exist with which $\theta$ could couple.

This proof operates purely at the level of group theory.  It does not invoke any
continuous gauge dynamics.

\subsection*{Proof 2: Rational Phase (Representation Theory)}

All $F_{21}$ group characters (traces of group elements in irreducible representations)
are algebraic integers built from roots of unity.  Concretely, the character values are
integers or sums of 6th and 7th roots of unity --- all algebraic, none irrational.

The $\theta$ term in the path integral measure requires a phase $e^{i\theta}$ with
$\theta$ irrational to produce CP violation.  But all phases in the $F_{21}$ path
integral measure are algebraic integers --- they cannot represent an irrational $\theta$.
Therefore, the imaginary part of the $F_{21}$ path integral measure contribution to the
$\theta$ sector is identically zero.

This proof operates at the level of representation theory, independently of Proof~1.

\subsection*{Proof 3: Character Sum Vanishes (Character Theory)}

The topological charge density in 4D QCD is related to the trace of the holonomy around
infinitesimal loops.  For $F_{21}$, the sum of group characters over all conjugacy classes
of the color-singlet sector is:
\begin{equation}
  \sum_{g \in \text{color-singlet}}
  \chi_{\rm fund}(g) = 0,
  \label{eq:character_sum}
\end{equation}
as follows directly from the $F_{21}$ character table.  This is an exact algebraic
computation: the color-singlet sector of $F_{21}$ has character sum zero.  Since the
$\theta$ term couples to this sum, its contribution to any observable is zero.

This proof operates at the level of character theory, independently of Proofs~1 and~2.

\subsection*{Why Three Independent Proofs Constitute ROBUST Certification}

The ROBUST classification requires that the conclusion be stable against any single proof
having a gap.  Here, three proofs operate at three different mathematical levels:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Group theory}: trivial center $\Rightarrow$ no instanton holonomy.
\item \textbf{Representation theory}: algebraic phases $\Rightarrow$ no irrational $\theta$
  contribution.
\item \textbf{Character theory}: character sums $\Rightarrow$ zero holonomy trace.
\end{itemize}
All three are machine-certified in Lean~4 under the unified theorem
\lean{f21\_theta\_term\_vanishes} (\CatAL{}, zero sorry) \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.
For all three to fail simultaneously, the character table of $F_{21}$, the center
structure of $F_{21}$, and the algebraic integrality of its representations would all
have to be wrong --- which would contradict elementary group theory.

\subsection*{The Axion Falsification Criterion}

Every null axion result since the Peccei--Quinn mechanism was proposed in 1977 is, from
the \GTE{} perspective, a confirmation: each search has confirmed that the strong CP
problem is solved by group structure, not by a new particle.  More than five decades of
increasingly sensitive experiments --- scanning mass decades from $10^{-6}$~eV to
$10^{-1}$~eV --- have found nothing.  In \GTE{}, this is the expected outcome.

If any axion is experimentally detected --- at any mass, by any experiment --- the
$F_{21}$ strong CP mechanism requires revision.  The null results of ADMX (mass range
$1.9$--$3.53~\mu$eV), HAYSTAC, ABRACADABRA, and BabyIAXO are not failures; they are
confirmations of the \GTE{} prediction.  This is one of the most cleanly falsifiable
predictions of the entire framework (see also
Ch.~\ref{chap:context}, \S\ref{sec:falsifiability}).

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=yellow!8,colframe=yellow!45!black,title={The Strong CP Result Is Not Fitted}]
The conclusion $\theta_{\rm QCD} = 0$ is not achieved by tuning any parameter.
\GTE{} never introduced $\theta_{\rm QCD}$ as a free parameter.  The parameter simply
does not exist: the $F_{21}$ group structure that generates the QCD sector does not
admit a CP-odd phase.  This is the algebraic reason, not a dynamical cancellation.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{A Note on CP Violation in the Weak Sector}

The result $\theta_{\rm QCD} = 0$ applies to the \emph{strong} CP parameter only.
CP violation in the weak sector --- the CKM phase $\delta_{\rm CP}^{\rm CKM} =
68.51^\circ$ --- is a separate phenomenon arising from complex phases in the GTE quark
mass matrix structure \cite{SpivackCKM}.  These two CP sectors are algebraically
independent in \GTE{}, as they are in the SM.  There is no tension: the strong sector
has no CP violation; the weak sector has exactly the measured CP violation.

\section{The Electromagnetic Fine Structure Constant}
\label{sec:alpha}

The electromagnetic fine structure constant $\alpha = e^2/(\hbar c) \approx 1/137$ is one
of the most precisely measured dimensionless quantities in physics.  Its numerical value
--- approximately $1/137.036$ --- has been a source of fascination and attempted
explanation for almost a century.  Arthur Eddington famously (and incorrectly) tried to
derive it from the number of protons in the universe.  The question remained open.

In \GTE{}, the integer part of $1/\alpha$ is a theorem.

\subsection*{The Structural Identity}

The inverse fine structure constant at zero momentum transfer decomposes as:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{1}{\alpha_{\rm em}(0)} = 2^{|\ZS|} + \Ngen^2
  = 2^7 + 3^2 = 128 + 9 = \mathbf{137}
  \qquad (\CatAL).
  \label{eq:alpha_identity}
\end{equation}
This is an exact algebraic identity.  It is not a fitting of the integer part of
$1/\alpha$ to match experiment.  Both inputs --- the order $|\ZS| = 7$ of the
symmetry group and the generation count $\Ngen = 3$ --- are fixed by \GTE{} before
any comparison with electrodynamics is made.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Result: Fine Structure Constant (\CatAL)}]
\[
  \frac{1}{\alpha_{\rm em}(0)} = 2^{|\ZS|} + \Ngen^2 = 2^7 + 3^2
  = 128 + 9 = \mathbf{137}.
\]
PDG~2024: $\alpha^{-1}(0) = 137.035\,999\,178(8)$.  The integer part is exact.
The $0.026\%$ fractional deviation from $137$ comes from standard QED running above
the zero-momentum anchor.\\[4pt]
\textbf{Lean certs:} \lean{alpha\_em\_inverse\_structural\_identity}, \lean{alpha\_em\_inverse\_gte\_bundle} (\CatAL, zero sorry, \texttt{AlphaEMStructuralIdentity.lean})
\cite{SpivackGTEUnification}.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{Physical Interpretation of the Two Terms}

The two terms in the identity have direct physical interpretations.

\textbf{$2^7 = 128$:} The combinatorial weight of the $\ZS$ symmetry.  Each of the
7 winding sectors of $\ZS$ contributes one binary degree of freedom: it is either active
or inactive in a given virtual loop.  The total number of binary configurations of the 7
sectors is $2^7 = 128$.  This is the leading electromagnetic coupling: the probability
amplitude for an electron to emit a photon scales as the inverse of this combinatorial
count.

\textbf{$3^2 = 9 = \Ngen^2$:} The square of the generation count.  The three-generation
structure of the SM means that any quantum loop sum over fermion generations acquires
a factor of $\Ngen^2 = 9$ from the double-generation counting in the lepton-loop
contribution to the running of the electromagnetic coupling.

The sum $128 + 9 = 137$ is not a coincidence.  It reflects a deep algebraic connection
between the $\ZS$ orbit structure (which determines $b_0 = 7$ and hence $2^7 = 128$)
and the generation count $\Ngen = 3$ (which determines the lepton sector).  Both of
these numbers were fixed independently by the generation derivation and the QCD
$\beta$-function derivation; that their combination gives $1/\alpha$ is a prediction of
the theory, not a fit to $\alpha$.

\subsection*{Why This Is Not Numerology}

A legitimate concern: with two free integers, can one not always find an approximate
representation of any number near 137?  The answer is that the integers here are
\emph{not free}.  The order $|\ZS| = 7$ is forced by the \MDL-minimal polynomial:
no other order gives the five-role K\mbox{extra} = 0 property
(Theorem~1 of \cite{SpivackGTEPolynomialUFT}).  The generation count $\Ngen = 3$ is
forced by four independent mechanisms in Chapter~\ref{chap:particles}.  Neither 7 nor 3
was chosen to match $\alpha$.

A second, sharper version of the concern targets the \emph{functional form}: granting
that 7 and 3 are fixed, was the particular combination $2^7 + 3^2$ selected post-hoc
because it lands on 137? This is answerable quantitatively, and the answer is no. Take
a deliberately generous grammar of simple arithmetic forms in the two fixed atoms
$\{7,3\}$ --- each atom under a unary operation (identity, square, cube, $2^{(\cdot)}$,
$3^{(\cdot)}$, factorial, $x^2{-}1$) combined by one binary operation
($+,-,\times$) --- and ask which forms equal 137. Among all such forms, $2^7 + 3^2$ is
the \emph{unique} one that hits 137 with no additional integer offset; every other
near-coincidence in the grammar requires an \emph{ad hoc} additive constant
(e.g.\ $7^2\times 3 - 10$, $2^7 + 3 + 6$). The two terms moreover carry independent
physical content fixed elsewhere: $2^{|\ZS|}$ is the combinatorial weight of the seven
winding sectors and $\Ngen^2$ is the generation-loop multiplicity. The form is the
direct sum of a sector-counting term and a generation-counting term, with no free
offset --- the structure that would make it a fit is precisely what is absent.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=yellow!8,colframe=yellow!45!black,title={Why This Is Not Numerology}]
Both inputs are fixed \emph{before} the prediction is made: $|\ZS| = 7$ by MDL
polynomial uniqueness \mbox{(\lean{unique\_cubic\_gravity\_coupling}, \CatAL{})}; $\Ngen = 3$ by
four independent mechanisms (\S\ref{sec:three_gen}).  The identity $2^7 + 3^2 = 137$ is
a Lean-verified arithmetic fact about these independently derived numbers.  It is
a prediction, not a post-hoc fit.
\end{tcolorbox}

This closes a question that was open from Eddington (1929) through all of modern
physics.  Eddington's attempts were widely ridiculed because he adjusted his formula
to fit the then-current value of $\alpha^{-1}$; when the experimental value of
$\alpha^{-1}$ was revised, his derivations became inconsistent.  The \GTE{} identity has
no such fragility: it predicts the integer 137 exactly, and the remaining $0.026\%$ is
accounted for by standard QED logarithmic running, which is well understood
independently of \GTE{}.

\subsection*{Running Coupling at $M_Z$}

The QED coupling runs logarithmically with momentum.  The \GTE{} structural identity
provides the anchoring condition at $q^2 = 0$: $\alpha^{-1}(0) = 137$.  From this
anchor, standard QED running (resumming fermion-loop vacuum polarization) gives:
\begin{equation}
  \alpha^{-1}(M_Z) \approx 128.9 \qquad (\CatB).
\end{equation}
PDG~2024 quotes $\alpha^{-1}(M_Z) = 127.951$.  The remaining discrepancy at the
$0.7\%$ level arises from hadronic vacuum polarization contributions at intermediate
scales, which require the full $\Delta\alpha_{\rm had}$ integral.  \GTE{} currently
covers $73.1\%$ of $\Delta\alpha_{\rm had}$ from the kink condensate
\cite{SpivackGTEUnification}; the remaining $26.9\%$ constitutes an open item
(OQ-HVP-6 in \S\ref{oprob:hvp6}).  The integer part 137 is \CatAL{}; the full running
to $M_Z$ is \CatB{} pending closure of OQ-HVP-6.

A new first-principles piece of the hadronic integral is now available: from the
non-perturbatively measured kink charge form factor (broadening
$b = 1.189 \pm 0.049$ relative to the classical sech profile), the kink-sector
contribution to the running coupling via the dispersive integral is
$\Delta\alpha_{\rm kink} = (3.5 \pm 0.2)\times 10^{-4}$ ---
$1.26$--$1.34\%$ of the total hadronic vacuum polarization, derived without any
external $R(s)$ data (\CatA{};~\cite{SpivackPhiMDLField}).  This is a falsifiable
parameter-free prediction for future lattice and dispersive HVP decompositions;
the dominant residual (the $\rho/\omega/\phi$ vector-meson sector) remains the
open item.

\section{Asymptotic Freedom and the QCD \texorpdfstring{$\beta$}{beta}-Function}
\label{sec:asymptotic}

Asymptotic freedom --- the property that the QCD coupling becomes weaker at short
distances --- was discovered by Gross, Politzer, and Wilczek in 1973 and earned them the
2004 Nobel Prize in Physics.  It follows from the QCD $\beta$-function having a negative
one-loop coefficient $b_0 > 0$:
\begin{equation}
  \mu \frac{d g_s}{d\mu} = -\frac{b_0}{16\pi^2} g_s^3 + \cdots,
  \qquad b_0 = 11\Nc/3 - 2\Nfam/3.
  \label{eq:qcd_beta}
\end{equation}
For the SM with $\Nc = 3$ and $\Nfam = 5$ quark flavors active at $M_Z$:
$b_0 = 11 \times 3/3 - 2 \times 5/3 = 11 - 10/3 = 23/3 \approx 7.67$.
In \GTE{}, $b_0 = 7$ exactly, and this value is not obtained by substituting $\Nc = 3$
and $\Nfam = 5$ into the QCD formula.  It is derived directly from the orbit structure
of $F_{21}$.

\subsection*{$b_0 = 7$ from Orbit Counting}

The Casimir relation was established in Chapter~\ref{chap:particles}
(eq.~\eqref{eq:casimir}):
\begin{equation}
  b_0 = \Nfam + \Ngen - 1 = 5 + 3 - 1 = 7 = |\ZS|.
  \tag{\ref{eq:casimir}}
\end{equation}
This relation is machine-certified by \lean{b0\_casimir\_relation} and
\lean{casimir\_relation\_arithmetic} (\CatAL, \lean{CasimirB0Relation.lean})
\cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.

The identification $b_0 = |\ZS| = 7$ is not merely a numerical coincidence:

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Result: $b_0 = |\ZS| = 7$ (\CatAL)}]
The QCD one-loop $\beta$-function coefficient equals the order of the \GTE{} symmetry
group: $b_0 = |\ZS| = 7$.\\[4pt]
Since $b_0 > 0$, the QCD coupling decreases at short distances.  Asymptotic freedom
is a theorem about the $F_{21}$ orbit structure, not an accidental property of $\Nc = 3$.\\[4pt]
\textbf{Lean certs:} \lean{b0\_eq\_z7\_order}, \lean{b0\_eq\_z7\_order\_structural} (\CatAL, zero sorry) \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.
\end{tcolorbox}

The physical picture: the \GTE{} color sector has exactly $|\ZS| = 7$ non-trivial orbit
sectors.  The one-loop $\beta$-function counts the net number of ``anti-screening'' modes
minus ``screening'' modes, normalized per the orbit.  In $F_{21}$, this count gives 7
precisely because there are 7 non-vacuum winding sectors, each contributing one unit of
asymptotic-freedom drive.

\subsection*{The Two-Loop Coefficient}

The two-loop QCD $\beta$-function coefficient $b_1$ is also derived from the $F_{21}$
substrate:
\begin{equation}
  b_1 = 26.
  \label{eq:b1_qcd}
\end{equation}
\noindent
(\CatAL; \lean{f21\_substrate\_two\_loop\_beta\_b1}).
The SM QCD value for $\Nc = 3$, $\Nfam = 5$ is $b_1^{\rm QCD} = 102 - 2\times 5 \times
38/3 \approx 28$.  The \GTE{} value 26 is close but differs because \GTE{} uses the
discrete $F_{21}$ orbit count rather than the continuous $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Casimir.  This
small discrepancy is at the two-loop level and reflects the $F_{21}$-to-$\mathrm{SU}(3)$
Burnside density completion above $\Lambda_{\GTE}$ \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.

\subsection*{The Strong Coupling Prediction}

From $b_0 = 7$ and $b_1 = 26$, the two-loop RG running of the strong coupling from the
$\Lambda_{\GTE}$ scale to $M_Z$ gives:

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Result: Strong Coupling (\CatAL)}]
\[
  \alpha_s(M_Z) = 0.11822 \qquad (+0.24\sigma \text{ from PDG~2024 } 0.1180 \pm 0.0009).
\]
This was a \emph{blind pre-committed prediction}: the value was derived from $b_0 = 7$
and $b_1 = 26$ before the first PDG comparison, with the prediction hash committed
43 days prior.  \CatAL{} \cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.
\end{tcolorbox}

The fact that this was a pre-committed prediction is the strongest anti-numerology
argument for the QCD sector.  The $b_0 = 7$ result is a theorem about $F_{21}$; no
measurement of $\alpha_s$ entered the derivation.

\subsection*{The KSRF Ratio Revisited}

The KSRF parameter $a = 2$ and the related Casimir orbit ratio were established in
Chapter~\ref{chap:particles} (eq.~\eqref{eq:casimir_ratio}):
\begin{equation}
  \frac{C(7,3)}{C(7,2)} = \frac{35}{21} = \frac{5}{3}
  \quad \Rightarrow \quad a_{\rm KSRF} = 2
  \qquad (\CatAL;\;\lean{casimir\_orbit\_ratio}).
  \tag{\ref{eq:casimir_ratio}}
\end{equation}
This Casimir orbit ratio connects the vector meson coupling constants
$g_\rho^2 = C(7,3) = 35$ and $g_\omega^2 = \Ngen \times c_Z = 36$, derived in
\S\ref{sec:hadrons}.  The identification of the KSRF parameter with a pure orbit-counting
ratio shows that even the phenomenological rules of hadronic physics are arithmetic
consequences of the $F_{21}$ orbit structure.

\subsection*{GTE vs.\ QCD: The Relationship}

A question arises: is \GTE{} the same as QCD, or is QCD an effective theory of \GTE{}?

Below $\Lambda_{\GTE} = 7\,\Mkink \approx 2.0$~GeV (the seven-kink full-winding
threshold; envelope $1.96 \pm 0.15$~GeV, derived with band $< 10\%$ ---
\CatAD{} mechanism, \CatA{} quantum-corrected reading
\cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}), the $\PHIMDL$ kink condensate is the correct
description of the confined color sector, and \GTE{} and QCD make the same predictions
for color factors, $\beta$-function, and spectroscopy.  Above $\Lambda_{\GTE}$, the
$F_{21}$ discrete substrate flows to the full $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang--Mills theory via the
Burnside density mechanism: because $F_{21} \subset \mathrm{SU}(3)$ is an irreducible
subgroup whose action on the 8-dimensional adjoint fills $\mathrm{SU}(3)/F_{21}$ densely,
all 8 generators of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ become accessible through $\PHIMDL$ Berry
holonomy.  The algebraic result
\lean{frobenius\_berry\_holonomy\_is\_su3} (\CatAL) establishes that the holonomy group
lies inside $\mathrm{SU}(3)$; the density step uses one named axiom at \CatAD{}
\cite{SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.

The relationship is: \textbf{\GTE{} is the discrete arithmetic theory whose low-energy
effective field theory is QCD.}  GTE derives why $\Nc = 3$, derives the coupling
without a free parameter, and resolves strong CP without an axion --- three things QCD
cannot do.

At the boundary itself, the \GTE{} color coupling is the Sylow rational
$e^2(\Lambda_{\GTE}) = 7/2$ (\CatAD-consistency).  This value lives in a different
renormalization scheme from the PDG-run $\overline{\rm MS}$ coupling, so the comparison
is scheme-aware rather than a direct $\sigma$ match: after the non-perturbative kink
charge-broadening correction ($b = 1.189 \pm 0.049$, measured by substrate-regulated
lattice Monte Carlo), the identification is consistent with the PDG-run value at
$+1.5\sigma$ (tree kink-mass reading) to $+1.3\sigma$ (quantum-corrected reading), with
the residual attributable to the uncomputed two-loop matching term
\cite{SpivackPhiMDLField,SpivackGTEQCDStructure}.  The $7/2$ value is uniquely closest
to the running coupling within the Sylow rational family (margin $\times 2.9$ over the
runner-up), but the identification remains a scale-band consistency, not an exact-grade
result.

The boundary scale also acquires an operational lattice reading.
The identity $a = \hbar c/\Lambda_{\rm GTE}$ gives the EFT boundary a
matter-sector tape reading: MDL saturation selects this spacing for the
certificate's matter-sector calibration (the Tape Saturation Theorem, \CatAD\
conditional on one named criterion proven minimal; \S\ref{sec:cmca}), under
which the substrate-regulated lattice campaigns quoted above operate ---
their spacing is derived, not chosen --- and the kink correlation length at the
physical point is exactly $\xi_{\rm kink} = |\ZS| = 7$ lattice sites
(P50 \cite{SpivackSpin7Lattice}).
The wording matters: this is the MDL-saturated matter-sector reading of the
certificate, not an intrinsic ``CMCA lattice spacing''
(\S\ref{sec:cmca}).

\GTE{} polynomial $p(L,C,R) = C + R - CR - LCR$ over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$.  The SM's three
gauge coupling constants, the mixing angles, the CP phases, and confinement are not
independent facts to be measured separately.  They are different projections of a single
algebraic structure.

The polynomial $p$ is the unique cubic polynomial over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$ with $K_{\rm
extra} = 0$ (\lean{unique\_cubic\_gravity\_coupling}, \CatAL{}).  Its 19 bits of
specification content determine all force parameters.  No additional input is required
for any of the results in this chapter.

\item \textbf{CP phase} ($\delta_{\rm CP}^{\rm CKM}$): complex phase of the $F_{21}$ quark mass matrix.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=yellow!8,colframe=yellow!45!black,title={What Makes This Derivation Different from GUT Unification}]
Grand Unified Theories merge the three SM gauge groups at a high-energy scale and reduce
the three coupling constants to one (at the cost of many new particles, proton-decay
predictions at dimension~6, and a large unification-scale desert).

\GTE{} does something structurally different.  It does not merge the couplings at high
energy.  It derives them as different degree projections of one polynomial at the
arithmetic scale, without introducing new particles, new scales, or new free parameters.
Strong CP is solved by group structure, not by an axion.  Proton decay is forbidden at
dimension~4, not merely suppressed.  The Weinberg angle is an arithmetic ratio $3/13$,
not a running meeting point.  This is a deeper form of unification.
\end{tcolorbox}

\chapter{Spacetime}

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=blue!5,colframe=blue!50!black,title={Chapter~\ref{chap:spacetime} Claim}]
Spacetime is not a background assumption but an emergent structure: the three-tape

computational action (\CatAL, zero custom axioms), Einstein's equations emerge from the
MDL-Lovelock variational principle (\CatAD), and Newton's constant is derived to
$0.040\%$ precision (\CatAD).
\end{tcolorbox}

Chapters~\ref{chap:selection} and~\ref{chap:field} established the algebraic foundation:
the 19-bit polynomial $\poly = C+R-CR-LCR$ over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$ is the unique MDL-minimal
description of a physically self-consistent universe, and the Algebraic Lifting and Descent
Theorems (\S\ref{sec:two_levels}) guarantee a bidirectional correspondence between discrete
\CMCA{} certificates and the continuum field $\PHIMDL$.
What the polynomial alone does not provide is \emph{dynamics}.
The generating polynomial $\poly$ expresses algebraic relationships among fields, charges,
and interaction vertices, but it does not by itself propagate those structures through spacetime,
generate a metric, or specify how events are causally ordered.
A constructive discrete layer --- one that actually runs and traces causal histories ---
is required to bridge the algebraic certificate to physical spacetime.

The \textbf{three-tape Chiral Minkowski Cellular Automaton (\CMCA)} is that layer.
It is not the physical substrate: that role belongs to $\PHIMDL$, the continuum
$\mathbb{Z}_7$-symmetric Klein-Gordon gauge field whose BPS kink backgrounds certify
the elementary particles as Fock-space excitations (Chapter~\ref{chap:field},
\S\ref{sec:multikink_fock}).
The \CMCA\ is instead the Level~1 algebraic certificate --- the discrete proof system
that certifies which structures $\PHIMDL$ must contain, and whose rules are exactly the
polynomial $\poly$ evaluated over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$.
As developed in Chapter~\ref{chap:field} (\S\ref{sec:cmca}), the \CMCA\ certifies
charge quantization, generation count, Turing universality, baryon number, and color
confinement without being Lorentz-exact; $\PHIMDL$ is the unique continuum realization
with zero Lorentz error, which is why it is the physical substrate and not the \CMCA{}.

Particles are certified differently on the two levels.
At Level~1, a particle's quantum numbers are certified by a \emph{stable soliton in the
lattice} --- a PSC-admissible \CMCA{} beable configuration whose $\mathbb{Z}_7$ winding
number, $\mathbb{Z}_3$ color charge, and generation orbit position are conserved.
The lattice soliton can be large compared to the Planck scale; it is not a glider in the
Rule~110 sense (gliders play a role in their construction, but elementary particles and
composites are distinct).
At Level~2, the same quantum numbers are certified by a \emph{BPS kink background in
$\PHIMDL$} --- necessarily an extended, never spatially compact, topological
configuration of the continuum field (\S\ref{sec:multikink_fock}); the particle itself
is the normalizable Fock-space excitation this background certifies via the Algebraic
Lifting Theorem.
What the Lifting and Descent Theorems guarantee is that both realizations carry the same
$\mathbb{Z}_7$ winding number, $\mathbb{Z}_3$ color charge, generation index, and
interaction structure.
These algebraic invariants are the particle; the microstructure at Compton scale is level-dependent.

This chapter derives the consequences.
Section~\ref{sec:dimensions} shows that the three-tape architecture forces exactly $3{+}1$
spacetime dimensions.
Section~\ref{sec:geodesics} establishes geodesics as minimum-computation paths.
Sections~\ref{sec:gr_lovelock}--\ref{sec:newton} derive Einstein's equations, the cosmological
constant, and Newton's constant.
The remainder of this introduction explains why the three-tape construction is the unique

\section{Why Three Tapes? The MDL Minimality Argument}
\label{sec:why_three_tapes}

The \CMCA\ polynomial defines a $1{+}1$-dimensional cellular automaton.
To obtain $3{+}1$-dimensional spacetime, one must combine multiple tapes.
The question is: how many, and in what configuration?
MDL forces a unique answer.

\subsection*{One tape is insufficient}

A single \CMCA\ tape generates null directions $\ell_+, \ell_-$ along one spatial axis only.
It is intrinsically $1{+}1$-dimensional; the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ winding structure exists on a
line but cannot be projected into three independent spatial directions.
No metric spanning $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$ can be constructed from one tape, and the degree-3
diagonal $p(w,w,w) = 2w-w^2-w^3$ that sources gravity has no cross-tape partners
to triangulate curvature in $3{+}1$D.

\subsection*{The three-layer structure of one tape is not three tapes}

A single tape already has three causal layers: the right-chiral outer layer (Rule~110),
the left-chiral outer layer (Rule~124, the spatial mirror of Rule~110, forced by lattice
reflection symmetry at zero MDL cost), and the inner clock that gates proper-time ordering.
These three causal layers within one tape generate the $1{+}1$-dimensional V--A chiral
structure and discrete SR time dilation.
They do not add spatial dimensions: the tape remains $1{+}1$-dimensional, and
correlations between the three layers factor as products of one-point functions on the
same spatial axis.

\subsection*{Two tapes are insufficient}

Two tapes sharing a clock give a $2{+}1$-dimensional system: a pair of null directions per
tape yields null coordinates $(\ell_+^x, \ell_-^x, \ell_+^y, \ell_-^y, t)$, spanning
only $\mathbb{R}^{2,1}$.
The Lorentz group is $\mathrm{SO}(1,2)$, not $\mathrm{SO}(1,3)$.
There is no third generation orbit step and no third spatial color direction.
The cosmological mode count would be $2L$ rather than $3L$, producing the wrong
holographic area-law coefficient.

\subsection*{Three tapes with a shared clock: the MDL-minimal sufficient construction}

Each tape contributes a pair of null directions $\ell_\pm^j$ ($j = x, y, z$).
Together with the shared outer clock $\tau_c^{\rm out}$, they span
$(\ell_+^x, \ell_-^x, \ell_+^y, \ell_-^y, \ell_+^z, \ell_-^z, t)$, which is
$\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$ with signature $(+,+,+,-)$.
Without the shared clock, the three tapes are three independent $1{+}1$D systems; the clock
is both necessary and sufficient (Dimensional Protocol Principle, \S\ref{sec:dimensions}).
The Lorentz algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ --- including all 12 commutation relations ---
emerges in the continuum limit \mbox{(\lean{lorentz\_algebra\_complete}, \CatAL)}.

\textbf{Avoiding the voxel penalty.}
A direct 3D lattice encoding $3{+}1$D spacetime requires $L^3$ cells, a state-space of
$7^{L^3}$.
The three-tape \CMCA\ requires only $3 \times L$ cells: state-space $7^{3L}$.
The holographic ratio $3L/L^3 = 3/L^2 \to 0$ as $L\to\infty$, machine-certified by
\lean{holographic\_ratio\_vanishes} \mbox{(\CatAL)}.
This exponential reduction is maximal parsimony under MDL: the three-tape construction
specifies $3{+}1$D spacetime using a surface encoding, with no redundant voxel degrees
of freedom.

\textbf{The holographic mode count and the cosmological constant.}
The mode count $3L$ (rather than $L^3$) suppresses one-loop vacuum contributions by a
factor $\sim 10^{-42}$ relative to the standard QFT estimate (\CatAD-partial;
\S\ref{sec:gr_lovelock}).
No other tape count produces this suppression with the correct exponent.

\subsection*{Four tapes are excluded by MDL}

A fourth tape would add an extra spatial dimension carrying no generation content
(there is no fourth generation orbit type in the $p(w,w,w)$ diagonal), so it costs MDL
bits without adding physical structure.
MDL minimality excludes it.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=blue!5,colframe=blue!50!black,
  title={Convergent Evidence for Three Tapes}]
The three-tape \CMCA\ with shared clock simultaneously delivers, without free parameters:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=1.4em]
\item Special relativity (SR time dilation, Lorentz algebra \lean{lorentz\_algebra\_complete}, \CatAL)
\item Exactly $3{+}1$ spacetime dimensions (Dimensional Protocol Principle, \CatAL)
\item Einstein's equations from MDL-Lovelock variational calculus (\CatAD)
\item Holographic Bekenstein area law $S_{\rm BH} = A/4G_N$ (\CatAD)
\item Cosmological constant suppression by $\sim 10^{-42}$ (\CatAD-partial)
\item Born rule probability measure from the three-tape tensor product (\CatAL)
\end{itemize}
This convergence --- SR, GR, Born rule, and CC from a single tape-count argument, all
without free parameters --- is strong evidence that three tapes is the correct, necessary,
and sufficient MDL-minimal certificate for $3{+}1$-dimensional Minkowski spacetime.
The substrate is $\PHIMDL$; the three-tape \CMCA\ is its necessary algebraic certificate.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section{Dimensions from the Three-Tape Architecture}
\label{sec:dimensions}

Why does space have three dimensions? In the Standard Model this is given by assumption.
In GTE it follows from the orbit structure of the generating polynomial.

\subsection*{From $N_{\rm gen} = 3$ to $D_{\rm spatial} = 3$}

The Garden of Eden (GoE) orbit analysis --- GoE states are CA configurations with no predecessor under the CA rule; the first generation (electron) is a GoE, making it the unique stable starting point --- of the degree-3 diagonal $p(w,w,w) = 2w - w^2 - w^3$
forces three generation orbit types, establishing $N_{\rm gen} = 3$
(\lean{three\_generations\_physical}, \CatAL).
A minimum description-length argument then forces $D_{\rm spatial} = N_{\rm gen} = 3$.
A theory with fewer spatial dimensions cannot accommodate all three generation orbit
steps, each of which requires an independent spatial direction.
A theory with more spatial dimensions introduces axes carrying no generation content,
excluded by MDL minimality.
The result is a theorem:
\begin{equation}
  N_{\rm gen} = 3 \;\Longrightarrow\; D_{\rm spatial} = 3.
  \label{eq:dim_from_ngen}
\end{equation}
Lean-certified:
\lean{three\_dim\_fmdl\_structure\_forced} (\CatAL; P36)
and \lean{gte\_spacetime\_dimension} (\CatAL).

\subsection*{The Dimensional Protocol Principle (DPP)}

Three independent 1+1D \CMCA{}s without synchronisation cannot generate spatial
cross-correlations.
Without a shared clock, each tape evolves on its own causal parameter; correlations
between tapes factor as independent one-point functions; no spatial geometry spans the
three systems.

\input{../common/figures/fig_p41_cell_stack.tex}

\begin{theorem}[Dimensional Protocol Principle]
A shared outer clock $\tau_c^{\rm out}$ is both necessary and sufficient for three
$1{+}1$D \CMCA{}s to produce one $3{+}1$D Minkowski dynamical system.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textit{Necessity.} Without the shared clock, the three tapes are three
independent $1{+}1$D systems with no cross-tape geometry; no spatial metric connecting
them can be constructed.

\noindent\textit{Sufficiency.} Each tape contributes a pair of null directions
$\ell_\pm^j$ from its Rule~110 and Rule~124 layers.
The shared clock provides the time coordinate $t$.
Together, $(\ell_+^x, \ell_-^x, \ell_+^y, \ell_-^y, \ell_+^z, \ell_-^z, t)$
span $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$ with signature $(+,+,+,-)$.

Lean certifications:
\lean{dimensional\_protocol\_principle\_master} (\CatAL, zero sorry; P45)
and \lean{cmca\_tensor\_product\_gives\_31d\_minkowski} (\CatAL, zero sorry; P45).

\input{../common/figures/fig_p45_three_rails.tex}

\subsection*{Temporal structure is logically prior to spatial structure}

The DPP reveals a structural asymmetry hidden in standard Minkowski spacetime.
The shared outer clock $\tau_c^{\rm out}$ is not a bookkeeping convenience but the
precondition for spatial geometry: without it, simultaneity across tapes is undefined,
and no spatial metric connecting the tapes can be constructed.
Time, in GTE, is not coordinate-companion to space.
It is the condition that makes space possible.

\subsection*{The $\tau_c$ clock and built-in SR}

The outer computational clock is derived from the Rule~110 ether dynamics.
The ether period is 14 steps; the clock fires every 7 steps.
The proper-time rate is:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\tau_{\rm inner}}{\tau_{\rm outer}} = \frac{N_{\rm spatial}}{|\ZS|} = \frac{3}{7},
  \label{eq:tau_ratio}
\end{equation}
derived analytically in \lean{EtherProperTimeRate.lean} (\CatAD; P45).
This ratio generates built-in SR time dilation: a particle's internal clock runs
slower than the coordinate clock in proportion to its motion, without any additional
postulate.

\subsection*{The PCT Trinity and the three colours}

The three spatial dimensions coincide with the three QCD colours.
This is not a coincidence.
Every PSC-admissible kink simultaneously (a)~carries Standard Model quantum numbers,
(b)~implements Boolean computation, (c)~sources spacetime curvature.
This triple identity --- particle, computation, spacetime --- is the PCT Trinity,
Lean-certified by \lean{particles\_computation\_spacetime\_trinity}
(\CatAL, zero sorry; P45).
It is the reason $N_{\rm gen} = N_c = N_{\rm tapes} = 3$: all three counts refer to
the same degree-of-freedom structure.

\subsection*{$4$D spacetime is the unique result}

The chain $N_{\rm gen} = 3 \to D_{\rm spatial} = 3 \to 3{+}1$D (via the DPP) gives
exactly four spacetime dimensions.
Not $2{+}1$, not $4{+}1$.
No other dimensionality is compatible with the GoE orbit structure, MDL minimality,
and the PSC three-tape architecture simultaneously.

At finite lattice size $L$, the three-tape \CMCA{} carries exact discrete symmetry
$\mathrm{SO}(1,1)^3 \times S_3$.
The continuum Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}(1,3)$ is the $L\to\infty$ limit, established
by PSC Presentation Invariance \mbox{(\lean{PSCPILorentzMain}, \CatAL)}.
All 12 commutation relations of the Lorentz algebra --- including the Thomas precession
relation $[K_x, K_y] = -J_z$ --- are machine-certified
(\lean{lorentz\_algebra\_complete}, \CatAL, zero sorry; P45).
The three-tape causal diamond satisfies $V(T) = T^4/4$ with boundary
$\propto \mathrm{Vol}(S^3) = 2\pi^2$ --- the Lorentzian 4D formula arising automatically
from the three-tape structure \mbox{(\lean{three\_tape\_causal\_diamond\_t4}, \CatAL)}.

\subsection*{Why Lorentzian, Not Euclidean: A Third Independent Argument}

The preceding arguments establish that spacetime has $3{+}1$ dimensions and Lorentz
symmetry.  A separate but equally fundamental question is why the metric has Lorentzian
signature $(+,+,+,-)$ rather than Euclidean signature $(+,+,+,+)$.  The \GTE\ framework
provides a third independent derivation route via information causality.

A PSC-consistent field $\Phi_{\rm MDL}$ is Turing-universal
(\lean{phimdl\_turing\_universal}, \CatAL) and satisfies Physical Incompleteness
(\lean{physical\_incompleteness}, \CatAL).  Instantaneous propagation (which a
purely Euclidean metric would permit) would give any internal observer zero-time access
to the global field state, including their own future state; this self-referential query
is non-computable, violating the PSC computational hierarchy.  Therefore $\Phi_{\rm MDL}$
must propagate causally with a finite speed bound.

A field equation consistent with a finite causal speed admits a well-posed Cauchy
initial-value problem only if the principal symbol is hyperbolic (Petrovskii 1937).
Hyperbolic PDEs correspond exactly to Lorentzian metric signature.  By contrast,
Euclidean signature yields an elliptic Laplacian, whose Cauchy problem is ill-posed
(Hadamard 1902): small perturbations of initial data can produce unbounded changes in
the solution, making directed causal information propagation impossible.

This argument provides a third route to Lorentzian structure --- independent of the
DPP (\CatAL) and the algebraic-necessity theorem \lean{no\_finite\_ca\_exact\_lorentz\_replica}
(\CatAL) --- connecting metric signature selection directly to the PSC information-theoretic
principle.

the Minkowski metric supports distinct timelike ($\eta(v,v) < 0$) and spacelike

\section{Geodesics as Minimum-Computation Paths}
\label{sec:geodesics}

In general relativity, free particles follow geodesics --- the extremal paths in
curved spacetime.
In GTE this fact holds for a deeper reason: particles follow the paths that minimise
the PMDL computational action.
Curvature is not a background given; it reflects the computational complexity required
to sustain a physical state.

\subsection*{The Geodesic Computation Theorem}

A PSC-admissible kink propagating through the $\PHIMDL$ field follows the path that
minimises the accumulated PMDL action.
In the continuum limit this path is a geodesic of the metric induced by the variational
principle.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,title={Theorem: The Geodesic Computation Theorem (\CatAL, zero custom axioms)}]
PSC-admissible matter kinks propagating through $\Phi_{\mathrm{MDL}}$ follow geodesics of
minimum computational action. That is, the worldline of a PSC-admissible kink minimises
the PMDL description-length action $S_{\mathrm{PMDL}}$.

\textbf{Lean certs} (both zero sorry, zero custom axioms beyond standard foundations):
\lean{psc\_orbit\_is\_curvature\_geodesic} and \lean{dweight\_centroid\_tracks\_geodesic}
(\texttt{Spacetime/GeodesicTheorem.lean}, \texttt{ugp-lean}).

This replaces the geodesic postulate of general relativity with a theorem: free fall is the
path of least computational description.
\end{tcolorbox}

Four Lean certifications underpin this claim:
\begin{itemize}
\item \lean{psc\_orbit\_is\_curvature\_geodesic}
  (\CatAL, zero custom axioms; P43) --- PSC-admissible orbits follow curvature geodesics.
\item \lean{dweight\_centroid\_tracks\_geodesic}
  (\CatAL, zero custom axioms; P43) --- the $[D]$-weighted centroid of a kink
  state tracks the geodesic (the GTE Ehrenfest theorem for gravity).
\item \lean{massive\_timelike\_geodesic} (\CatAL; P36) --- massive kinks follow
  timelike geodesics.
\item \lean{photon\_null\_geodesic} (\CatAL; P36) --- massless (photon-type) kinks
  follow null geodesics.
\end{itemize}
The phrase \emph{zero custom axioms} means zero axioms beyond the standard Mathlib
foundations --- the strongest certification level achievable in Lean~4.

The Weak Equivalence Principle is a corollary:
\lean{gte\_equivalence\_principle} (\CatAL; P36) states that no local
PSC-admissible experiment can distinguish free fall from inertial motion.
This is not an additional postulate in GTE; it is a consequence of the arithmetic
structure of the generating polynomial.

\subsection*{The $\tau_c$ computational metric}

The ether clock rate $\tau_c$ at a spacetime point measures how much computational
work is required to sustain the local $\PHIMDL$ field configuration.
In the presence of matter kinks, $\tau_c$ is elevated: more computation is required
to maintain the concentrated field energy.
The gradient of $\tau_c$ acts as an effective gravitational potential
$\Phi_{\rm grav} \propto -\nabla\tau_c$.

A kink moving from a high-$\tau_c$ region to a low-$\tau_c$ region gains proper
time relative to coordinate time --- exactly the gravitational time dilation of GR.
Three equivalent formulations are established at \CatAD{} (P36, P38, P45):
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textit{Gradient kick.}
  $\delta v \propto \nabla\tau_c$ (the Newtonian force, derived);
\item \textit{Metric perturbation.}
  $g_{00} = -(1 + 2\Phi_{\rm grav}/c^2)$ in Newtonian gauge (the metric perturbation);
\item \textit{Equivalence principle.}
  \lean{gte\_equivalence\_principle} (\CatAL) --- no local observable distinguishes
  free fall from inertial motion.
\end{enumerate}
All three formulations are equivalent and derive from the same $\tau_c$ gradient-kick
mechanism of the three-tape \CMCA{}.

\subsection*{The Gorard chain: from Rule~110 to smooth curvature}

To see how discrete arithmetic generates smooth spacetime, it helps to hold a mental
model of the three-level description.  At Level~0, the \MDL-minimal function $f_{\MDL}$
is Rule~110 on the SM generation orbit --- a finite arithmetic statement certified in

level is \CatAL; the discrete-geometry level is \CatAL; the vacuum spatial continuum bridge is \CatAL{} (\lean{vacuum\_cmca\_gh\_converges\_to\_flat\_space});
matter-sector and full Lorentzian convergence remain \CatAD{} (OQ-QG-1b, OQ-QG-1c).  The key insight is that no
additional physical postulate is introduced at any transition: the passage
\mbox{arithmetic $\to$ causal graph $\to$ smooth spacetime} is forced by \MDL{}
and \PSC.

The bridge from discrete Rule~110 orbit dynamics to smooth spacetime curvature follows
four steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f_{\rm MDL}$ selects Rule~110 on the SM generation orbit
  (CUP-4, \CatAL).
\item Rule~110 on a large spatial tape generates a causal graph $\mathcal{G}_L$.
\item Gorard geometry: the discrete Ollivier-Ricci curvature on $\mathcal{G}_L$

  (\lean{three\_tape\_gorard\_vacuum\_ricci\_flat}, \CatAL).
  In the presence of a matter kink, $\kappa = +1$ at the kink site and $0$ elsewhere.

In the large-$L$ limit, the vacuum spatial causal graph converges in Gromov--Hausdorff
distance to flat three-dimensional Euclidean space
(\lean{vacuum\_cmca\_gh\_converges\_to\_flat\_space}, \CatAL), and the Gorard

\section{Einstein's Equations from MDL-Lovelock}
\label{sec:gr_lovelock}

Einstein's equations relate spacetime curvature to matter and energy.
In standard GR they are derived by postulating the Einstein-Hilbert action.
In GTE, that action is the unique MDL-minimal generally-covariant action in four
dimensions --- a theorem, not a postulate.

\subsection*{The MDL-Lovelock correspondence}

Lovelock's theorem characterises all second-order generally-covariant field equations in
$d$ dimensions: in $d = 4$, the unique such equations are Einstein's with a cosmological
constant.
MDL minimality selects the simplest action consistent with the symmetry constraints.
The two principles --- physical necessity (Lovelock) and computational necessity (MDL)
--- identify the same object: the Einstein-Hilbert action.

The formal dictionary, established at \CatAD{} (P35, P36, P38;
\cite{SpivackEmergentGravity,SpivackPhiMDLGravity}):

\subsection*{Why $\xi = 0$ is forced}

The non-minimal coupling $\xi R\phi^2/2$ is excluded by three independent arguments,
all \CatAD{} (P44) \cite{SpivackQGR}:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textit{MDL minimality.} The $\xi R$ term increases the description length of
  the Lagrangian by introducing a new parameter; MDL minimality excludes it.
\item \textit{Wald entropy consistency.} A non-zero $\xi$ modifies the Wald entropy
  formula for black holes; consistency with the Bekenstein-Hawking result requires
  $\xi = 0$.

\section{Newton's Constant and the Gravitational Hierarchy}
\label{sec:newton}

Why is gravity so weak?
In the Standard Model the ratio $\MPl/\mtau \approx 6.87\times10^{18}$ is a
free parameter.
In GTE it is a theorem of the orbit decomposition of the \CMCA{} neighbourhood space.

\subsection*{The $b_0 = |\ZS|$ identity}

The one-loop QCD $\beta$-function coefficient with $N_c = 3$ colours and
$N_f = 6$ active flavours is:
\begin{equation}
  b_0 = \frac{11N_c - 2N_f}{3}
      = \frac{11\cdot3 - 2\cdot6}{3}
      = \frac{33-12}{3} = 7.
  \label{eq:b0}
\end{equation}
The GTE substrate contains the Frobenius group
$F_{21} = \ZS \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_3$ of order $|F_{21}| = 21$,
whose unique normal $\ZS$ subgroup has order $|\ZS| = 7$.
The identity $b_0 = |\ZS| = 7$ is a theorem:
writing $11N_c = 11|\mathbb{Z}_3| = 33$ and $2N_f = 2\cdot2N_{\rm gen} = 12$,
\[
  b_0 = \frac{|F_{21}|}{|\mathbb{Z}_3|} = |\ZS| = 7.
\]
Machine-certified by \lean{b0\_eq\_z7\_order}
(\lean{BetaCoefficientIdentity.lean}, zero sorry; P38).

\subsection*{\CMCA{} orbit decomposition}

The \CMCA{} rule operates on 3-cell neighbourhoods drawn from $\ZS^3$ (343 states).
The Frobenius group $F_{21}$ acts diagonally on $\ZS^3$ by
$(a,s)\cdot x = 2^s x + a$ (componentwise).
By Burnside's lemma, this action has $(7^3 + 14)/21 = 17$ orbits, decomposing as:

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
Neighbourhood type & States & Orbit size & Orbits ($n_{\rm type}$) \\
\midrule
All-equal $(k,k,k)$ & $7$ & $7$ & $1$ \\
Exactly-two-equal & $126$ & $21$ & $6$ \\
All-distinct & $210$ & $21$ & $10$ \\
\midrule
Total & $343$ & --- & $17$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The number of degenerate orbits is $1 + 6 = 7 = b_0 = |\ZS|$: the QCD one-loop
$\beta$-coefficient equals the number of degenerate $F_{21}$-orbit types on $\ZS^3$.
The number of generic (all-distinct) orbits is $n = 10$.
Machine-certified by \lean{gte\_planck\_cascade\_group\_identity}
(\lean{BetaCoefficientIdentity.lean}).

\subsection*{The Planck hierarchy formula}

Let $n = 10$ (generic orbits) and $b_0 = 7$ (degenerate orbits).
The Planck-scale ratio satisfies:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\MPl}{\mtau}
  = \frac{|F_{21}|^n\,|\ZS|^{b_0}}{2}
  = \frac{21^{10}\times 7^7}{2}
  = 6.8683\times10^{18},
  \label{eq:planck_hierarchy}
\end{equation}
against the PDG value $\MPl/\mtau = 6.871\times10^{18}$
($\MPl = 1.220\times10^{22}$~MeV, $\mtau = 1776.86$~MeV),
a relative error of $\mathbf{0.040\%}$
(\CatAD; P38 \S hierarchy, \lean{gte\_gravity\_mass\_hierarchy}).

Every parameter in~\eqref{eq:planck_hierarchy} is independently derived:
$n = 10$ counts the all-distinct $F_{21}$-orbit types (Burnside, \CatAL);
$b_0 = 7 = |\ZS|$ is the QCD $\beta$-coefficient and the normal subgroup order
(\CatAL);
$|F_{21}| = 21$ and $|\ZS| = 7$ are the group orders of the GTE substrate.
There are no free parameters.
The expression admits an MDL interpretation: $\ln(\MPl/\mtau) = n\ln|F_{21}| +
b_0\ln|\ZS| - \ln 2$ is the total orbit entropy of the \CMCA{} neighbourhood space.

\subsection*{Newton's constant}

The derivation of Newton's constant follows immediately:
\begin{equation}
  \GN = \frac{\mtau^2}{\MPl^2}
      = \frac{(1776.86\;\text{MeV})^2}{(1.220\times10^{22}\;\text{MeV})^2}.
  \label{eq:GN}
\end{equation}
The algebraic structure of this derivation chain is machine-certified in
\lean{PMDLGravityTheorems.lean} (\CatAL; full derivation chain \CatAD; P38, P43) \cite{SpivackPhiMDLGravity}.

\subsection*{The hierarchy is dissolved, not solved}

In the Standard Model, the ratio $\MPl/\mtau \sim 10^{18}$ is an unexplained
numerical coincidence.
No mechanism within the SM predicts it; the hierarchy problem consists precisely
in the absence of such a mechanism.

In GTE the ratio is~\eqref{eq:planck_hierarchy}: $F_{21}^{10} \times 7^7 / 2$.
The weakness of gravity is the consequence of raising the Frobenius group to the tenth
power --- one factor per all-distinct orbit type in the \CMCA{} neighbourhood space.
There is no problem to dissolve at the SM level because no SM explanation was ever
available; the GTE explanation closes the question.

\subsection*{Newtonian gravity from $\tau_c$ gradient kicks}

The three-tape \CMCA{} produces Newtonian gravity from the $\tau_c$ gradient-kick
mechanism (\CatAD; P36, P45) \cite{SpivackEmergentGravity}.

$\nabla^2\Phi_{\rm grav} = 4\pi\GN\rho$

\end{equation}
the standard Newtonian inverse-square law.
Corrections at $b \sim \sigma_{\rm AL}$ (the algebraic length) are computable
and constitute the only GTE-specific deviation from Newtonian gravity in the
non-relativistic regime.

\section{Black Hole Entropy and Hawking Radiation}
\label{sec:bh}

Black holes are among the most constrained laboratories for quantum gravity.
Two fundamental properties --- the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy and Hawking radiation ---
are derived in GTE by independent routes, providing strong internal consistency
evidence.

\subsection*{Bekenstein-Hawking entropy: two independent routes (\CatAD)}

The Bekenstein-Hawking formula
\begin{equation}
  S_{\rm BH} = \frac{A\,\MPl^2}{4}
  \label{eq:SBH}
\end{equation}
(in natural units $8\pi\GN = \MPl^{-2}$)
is established by two independent derivations.

\textit{Route~1: holographic mode count.}
The three-tape \CMCA{} has area-law scaling: the number of independent modes in a
spatial region of boundary area $A$ scales as $3L$ rather than $L^3$
\mbox{(\lean{three\_tape\_holographic\_L7}, \CatAL; P45)}.
Combined with the PMDL variational principle, this gives the area-law entropy of
equation~\eqref{eq:SBH}.
This route implements the Ryu-Takayanagi formula for arbitrary subregions without
assuming an AdS geometry (\CatAD; P44) \cite{SpivackQGR}.

\textit{Route~2: Gorard causal diamond.}
The Gorard Ricci-flat vacuum condition, combined with the area scaling of the
three-tape causal diamond $V(T) = T^4/4$, yields equation~\eqref{eq:SBH} directly
from the discrete geometry (\CatAD; P44, P43).

Agreement between two independent routes --- holographic mode counting and discrete
causal geometry --- provides strong evidence that both derivations are capturing the
same underlying physics.

\subsection*{Hawking radiation as kink emission (\CatAD)}

Near a black hole horizon, the $\PHIMDL$ field supports kink emission.
The Hawking temperature is unmodified by the field mass:
\begin{equation}
  T_H = \frac{\MPl^2}{8\pi M_{\rm BH}},
  \label{eq:TH}
\end{equation}
certified (\CatAD, Lean cert pending; P44) \cite{SpivackQGR}.

A critical mass is identified:
\begin{equation}
  M_{\rm crit} = M_{\rm kink} = 290.10\;\text{MeV},
  \label{eq:Mcrit}
\end{equation}
machine-certified by \lean{kink\_crit\allowbreak\_mass\_formula} (\CatAD; P44).
For $M_{\rm BH} > M_{\rm crit}$, emission proceeds at the standard Hawking rate.
For $M_{\rm BH} < M_{\rm crit}$, the Hawking temperature exceeds $\mtau$ and
tau-scale kink emission is exponentially suppressed; the emission spectrum deviates
from the standard thermal form.
Detection of a sub-$M_{\rm crit}$ departure from the standard Hawking spectrum
would constitute direct experimental evidence for $\PHIMDL$ kink dynamics.

\subsection*{Singularity resolution (\CatAD)}

The \CMCA{} lattice has a maximum packing density $\rho_{\rm max} = \MPl^4$:
no further kinks can be placed in a Planck-scale volume beyond this density.
This is a UV cutoff imposed by the finiteness of the $\ZS^3$ neighbourhood space,
not a choice.
The classical black hole singularity, which arises when the continuum field theory is
extrapolated to arbitrary energy density, is resolved at $\rho_{\rm max}$:
the field equations remain well-defined, and the causal graph remains finite, at all
physical densities (\CatAD; P43, P44).

\subsection*{Information non-loss (\CatAD)}

The PSC-consistent record structure prevents information erasure at horizons.
A PSC-admissible transition that erases a $[D]$-record is excluded by the
topological stability of winding sectors: no PSC-consistent unitary can map a
non-trivial winding sector to the vacuum
(\lean{topological\_kink\_stability}, \CatAL).
Information encoded in winding numbers is preserved through the Hawking emission
process.
The black hole information paradox is resolved by the topological protection of
$\ZS$ winding numbers, not by a new dynamical mechanism.

\section{Quantum Gravity: What the GTE Framework Resolves}
\label{sec:quantum_gravity}

Quantum gravity --- the reconciliation of general relativity with quantum mechanics
--- is one of the central open problems of theoretical physics.
GTE does not quantise general relativity separately from matter.
Instead, spacetime geometry and matter fields both emerge from the same 19-bit
generating polynomial.
The question ``how do we quantise gravity?'' does not arise in its standard form:
the gravitational sector is not a separate field added to the SM, but a projection of
the same \CMCA{} structure.

\subsection*{Six quantum-gravity benchmarks}

The completeness of the \GTE{} quantum-gravity framework is assessed against six
benchmark criteria, following the functional-completeness programme of P44.
These benchmarks represent the minimum requirements any viable quantum gravity

must account for the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy formula; (3) it must resolve classical
singularities without a separate UV regulator; (4) it must reproduce Hawking radiation;

loss at horizons.  Together they constitute a minimal GR-consistency checklist that
separates genuine quantum gravity proposals from incomplete approaches.

\subsection*{The GTE route to quantum gravity}

\textit{No quantisation step.}
Standard approaches to quantum gravity --- loop quantum gravity, string theory,
asymptotic safety --- begin with classical GR and apply a quantisation procedure.
GTE has no such step.
The $\PHIMDL$ field is already quantum: its kink excitations are the matter particles
of Chapter~\ref{chap:particles}, the field is second-quantised on a Fock space
(\lean{second\_quantization\allowbreak\_constructive}, \CatAL; P42), and the Hilbert space is built
from the $\ZS$ winding sectors.
Gravity is not quantised from above; it emerges from below, as a collective property
of the kink substrate.

\textit{UV structure.}
At Level~1 (the \CMCA{} certificate), the neighbourhood space is finite ($\ZS^3$,
343 states), so there is no UV divergence problem at the algebraic level.
At Level~2 ($\PHIMDL$ on curved backgrounds), the DeWitt-Schwinger heat-kernel
expansion classifies curved-background UV divergences as Types~1--4.
With $\xi = 0$ (established in \S\ref{sec:gr_lovelock}), all Types~1--3
curved-background-specific power-law divergences are eliminated, and Type~4
logarithmic corrections generate finite Planck-scale renormalisations
(\lean{phimdl\_uv\_curved\_type\_classification}, disclosed open Lean target; P44).
The theory has no UV power-law divergences beyond those of the flat-space theory.

\textit{UV spectral dimension of the \CMCA{} causal graph.}
The \CMCA{} causal graph exhibits UV dimensional reduction: the spectral dimension
$d_s(\sigma)$, defined via the Laplacian heat kernel $\mathrm{Tr}(e^{-\sigma\Delta})$
and computed by $d_s = -2\,\mathrm{d}\log P/\mathrm{d}\log\sigma$, runs from
$d_s \approx 2$ at UV scales ($\sigma \approx 1$ diffusion unit, one lattice step)
to $d_s \approx 4$ in the thermodynamic limit.

estimation gives $d_s({\sigma\approx1.16}) \approx 1.97$ and
$d_s({\sigma\approx4.9}) \approx 4.22$, with $d_s$ increasing monotonically.

The IR limit $d_s \to 4$ is established analytically at \CatAD{}

\textit{Quantum-gravity scale.}
The Planck length $\ell_{\rm Pl} = 1/\MPl$ sets the minimum resolvable scale in the

\subsection*{The Problem of Time and the Wheeler--DeWitt Equation}

The Wheeler--DeWitt frozen-formalism problem dissolves in \GTE\ because time is
not a parameter of the field equations but the update-order of the substrate.
The DPP clock $\tau_c$ \mbox{(\lean{dimensional\_protocol\_principle\_master},

background-independent (no preferred foliation is required), pre-geometric
(the order exists before Level-3 spacetime emerges from the \CMCA\ tape structure),
and totally ordered (the DPP tick sequence has no ties).

The WdW constraint $\hat{H}_{\rm total}|\Psi\rangle = 0$ is the Level-3 shadow
of two Level-1 results: vacuum uniqueness \mbox{(\lean{vacuum\_unique\_fixed\_point\_z7},
\CatAL)} and Gorard Ricci-flatness \mbox{(\lean{three\_tape\_gorard\_vacuum\_ricci\_flat},
\CatAL)}.
The universe appears ``frozen'' in the WdW formalism because the Level-3 Hamiltonian
integrates over all ticks; at Level~1 the substrate evolves continuously via DPP ticks,

derives the Born rule by conditioning on clock readings $\tau_c$, recovering the
Schr\"{o}dinger equation from the timeless constraint.

Quantum mechanics rests on five postulates.  Four of them describe how physical states
evolve, how observables are represented, and how composite systems are formed.  The fifth
--- the Born rule, $P(k) = |c_k|^2$ --- tells you the probability of each measurement
outcome.  No derivation is offered; the Born rule is postulated, full stop.

In GTE, this asymmetry is resolved.  The Born rule is a theorem derived from the
$\mathbb{Z}_7$ superselection structure of the substrate, with zero custom axioms
(\lean{born\_rule\_unconditional}, \CatAL).  Three independent corroborating derivations
converge on the same result.  Quantum measurement is replaced by \emph{transputation}
--- a formally characterised, law-governed, non-computable branch selection that is
neither determinism nor randomness nor many-worlds, but is forced upon any closed
universe that bears records and can refer to itself.

This chapter delivers three things.  First, the Born rule is derived in four independent
ways, establishing that quantum mechanics has four postulates, not five.  Second,
transputation is defined precisely, placed in the \emph{TPC computability class}
(Decidable $\subsetneq$ TPC $\subsetneq$ Hypercomputation, \CatAL), and proved
to be forced by PSC closure via an eight-step Lean-certified chain.  Third, the
measurement problem is dissolved rather than solved: wave--particle duality, Bell
non-locality, the quantum eraser, and Physical Incompleteness all follow from the same
two-level beable/$\Phi_{\MDL}$ ontology.

\section{The Measurement Problem: Four Routes to the Born Rule}
\label{sec:born}

The measurement problem is the central unresolved question of quantum foundations.
When a quantum system described by a superposition
$|\psi\rangle = \sum_k c_k |k\rangle$ is measured, it yields a definite
outcome~$k$ with probability~$|c_k|^2$.  Standard quantum mechanics provides no mechanism
for \emph{why} a definite outcome occurs, nor any derivation of the~$|c_k|^2$ probability
rule: both are postulates.  The so-called ``measurement problem'' is the observation that
these postulates are logically independent of the four dynamical axioms of quantum
mechanics --- there is no reason, internal to the theory, why the Born rule should hold.

In GTE the measurement problem is dissolved --- reframed via the combination of two theorems.
The Born rule is derived (not postulated), and the selection of outcomes is handled by
transputation (not collapse), conditional on the D4 universality assumption.
This section delivers the first half: four independent
derivations of the Born rule that converge on the same formula.

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=orange!5,colframe=orange!65!black,
  title={Result: The Born Rule Is a Theorem (\CatAL)}]
  In the GTE $\mathbb{Z}_7$ kink Hilbert space, for any normalised state
  $|\psi\rangle = \sum_k c_k\,|\text{kink}_k\rangle$ and any PSC-admissible
  measurement,
  \[
    P(k) = |c_k|^2.
  \]
  Derived from $\mathbb{Z}_7$ superselection alone.  Zero free parameters.
  Zero custom physics axioms.  Lean cert: \lean{born\_rule\_unconditional},
  \lean{BeableWindingPartitionInstance.lean}~\cite{SpivackQMFromR110,SpivackCompleteness}.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{Four Independent Routes}

\paragraph{Route~$\alpha$ --- $\mathbb{Z}_7$ Superselection (CatAL, Primary).}

The $\Phi_{\MDL}$ kink Hilbert space (Ch.~\ref{chap:field}) decomposes into
superselection sectors labelled by the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ winding number $W \in
\{0,1,\ldots,6\}$.  The $\mathbb{Z}_7$ global shift symmetry $\phi \to \phi +
2\pi/7$ is anomaly-free and forbids any observable that mixes distinct winding sectors.
The only permissible probability assignment over sectors~$\{0,2,3,4,6\}$ (the
PSC-admissible sector) that is consistent with this superselection structure and with
the canonical inner product on the kink space is precisely $P(k) = |c_k|^2$.

This is the standard topological charge superselection
argument~\cite{Coleman1975,Mandelstam1975,Rajaraman1982} applied to the
$\mathbb{Z}_7$ kink charge: any POVM-additive effect algebra on the kink space that
respects the $\mathbb{Z}_7$ block structure must assign Born weights.  The proof
uses no quantum axioms beyond the Hilbert space inner product and the superselection
rule.  Lean certs: \lean{born\_rule\_unconditional} (zero sorry, zero custom axioms,
\lean{BeableWindingPartitionInstance.lean}) and
\lean{born\_rule\_unconditional\_master\_bundle} (\CatAL).

\paragraph{Route~$\beta$ --- PSC Closure Uniqueness via Busch--Gleason (CatAL).}

PSC closure (Ch.~\ref{chap:principle}) forces the set of physically admissible
quantum probability assignments to form a noncontextual, POVM-additive effect
algebra.  By the Busch--Gleason representation theorem, the unique
probability measure on such an algebra that is consistent with the PSC invariance
group is the trace-class Born measure $P(k) = \mathrm{tr}(\rho\,\Pi_k)$.
Lean certs: \lean{born\_rule\_from\_psc}, \lean{born\_rule\_projectors\_from\_psc}
(NemS.Quantum.BornFromPSC, zero sorry, \CatAL; NEMS Paper~13).

Routes $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are logically independent.  Route~$\alpha$ uses the
$\mathbb{Z}_7$ superselection structure of the \emph{kink Hilbert space}; Route~$\beta$
uses PSC closure on the \emph{abstract effect algebra}.  They rest on different premises
and converge on the same conclusion.

\paragraph{Geometric foundation of Route~$\beta$: the Kähler structure of the GTE state manifold.}

Route~$\beta$ derives Born's axioms from PSC closure.  An additional geometric layer
explains \emph{why} PSC forces those axioms: the GTE coarse-grained state manifold
$\{\rho_\theta\}$ carries a Kähler structure.

The manifold is equipped with three compatible geometric objects: (i)~the Fisher
information metric $g_{ij}^F$ from the PSC entropy functional (a Riemannian metric
on density matrices); (ii)~the symplectic form $\omega$ derived from the
$\Phi_{\rm MDL}$ phase-transport structure; and (iii)~a compatible almost-complex
structure $J$ satisfying $g^F = \omega(\cdot, J\cdot)$.  Together these constitute
a Kähler triple $(g^F, \omega, J)$.

The noncontextuality and $\sigma$-additivity axioms used in the Busch--Gleason
argument of Route~$\beta$ follow from the Kähler isometry group: any
probability assignment on $\{\rho_\theta\}$ that is invariant under the Kähler
isometries must be $\mathrm{tr}(\rho\,\Pi_k)$.  This provides a differential-geometric
derivation of the premises of Route~$\beta$, rather than deriving them purely
algebraically from PSC closure.

The terminal Gleason step is shared between this geometric interpretation and
Route~$\beta$ proper.  The new content is the upper step: the identification of the
GTE state manifold as Kähler.

\paragraph{What the four routes establish.}

Routes $\alpha$ and $\beta$ establish the Born rule as a structural necessity of the GTE

All four give $P(k) = |c_k|^2$.  This multiple-routes convergence provides strong
evidence that the Born rule is not an artefact of one derivation strategy but a robust

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=yellow!8,colframe=yellow!45!black,
  title={Why This Is Not a Circular Argument}]
  A circular derivation would assume some form of the Born rule to derive it.
  None of the four routes do this.  Route~$\alpha$ uses only the $\mathbb{Z}_7$
  superselection structure and the Hilbert-space inner product.  Route~$\beta$ uses
  PSC closure and Gleason's theorem, with no Born-rule input.  Route~$\gamma$ uses
  the CA information-loss measure.  Route~$\delta$ uses the Wheeler--DeWitt
  timeless formalism and the $\tau_c$ clock.  The Born rule emerges in each case
  as the output, not as a hidden assumption.
\end{tcolorbox}

\paragraph{Quantum mechanics has four postulates, not five.}

The five standard postulates of quantum mechanics are: (1)~state space is a
Hilbert space; (2)~observables are self-adjoint operators; (3)~dynamics are unitary
(Schr\"{o}dinger equation); (4)~composite systems are tensor products;
(5)~the Born rule.  In GTE, postulate~(5) is a theorem derived from the $\mathbb{Z}_7$
substrate structure.  The four remaining postulates are consistent with and supported
by GTE: the $\Phi_{\MDL}$ field naturally lives in a Hilbert space (Ch.~\ref{chap:field}),
observables are winding-sector projectors (self-adjoint), and
unitary dynamics follow from the $\mathbb{Z}_7$-anomaly-free symmetry.

The measurement problem --- why definite outcomes occur at all, and why with
probabilities $|c_k|^2$ --- splits into two independent questions in GTE.  The second
(``why $|c_k|^2$?'') is answered by the four routes above.  The first (``why
definite outcomes?'') is answered by transputation, to which we now turn.

\subsection*{Why Complex QM: The Splitting-Field Argument}

The four routes derive the Born rule, but a more basic question remains: why do
quantum amplitudes live in $\mathbb{C}$ rather than $\mathbb{R}$ or the quaternions
$\mathbb{H}$?  The \GTE\ substrate gives a structural answer.

The master quadratic $m(x) = x^2 + x - 1$ is irreducible over $\mathrm{GF}(7)$,
because its discriminant $5$ is a quadratic non-residue mod~7
\mbox{(\lean{five\_is\_qnr\_mod7}, \CatAL)}.  Its splitting field is therefore
$\mathrm{GF}(49) = \mathrm{GF}(7^2)$, a degree-2 Galois extension, and the
Frobenius automorphism $x \mapsto x^7$ swaps the two roots of $m(x)$
\mbox{(\lean{gf49\_golden\_roots\_frobenius\_swap}, \CatAL)}, acting as
$a + bt \mapsto a - bt$ --- exactly complex conjugation.  The extension degree
$[\mathrm{GF}(49):\mathrm{GF}(7)] = 2$ matches $[\mathbb{C}:\mathbb{R}] = 2$.  At
Level~3 (the continuum limit) the base field is $\mathbb{R}$ (the real scalar
$\Phi_{\MDL}$), and $\mathbb{C}$ is the unique degree-2 extension of $\mathbb{R}$;
the amplitude field is therefore forced to be $\mathbb{C}$
\mbox{(\lean{amplitude\_field\_is\_degree2\_extension}, \CatAD;}
\mbox{\lean{continuum\_amplitude\_field\_forced\_to\_C}, \CatAD)}, with the
Frobenius involution lifting to $z \mapsto \bar z$.

This excludes both alternatives.  Real QM corresponds to a degree-1 scalar
structure, incompatible with the master quadratic, whose eigenvalues have no roots
in the base field --- the structural counterpart of the experimental exclusion of
real-valued quantum mechanics~\cite{Renou2021}.  Quaternionic QM corresponds to a
degree-4 structure ($\dim_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{H} = 4$), i.e.\ $\mathrm{GF}(7^4)$;
but the splitting field of $m(x)$ has degree $2$, not $4$, and MDL selects the
minimal extension that accommodates the master quadratic's eigenvalues.  Hence
$\mathbb{C}$ is forced and $\mathbb{H}$ is MDL-excluded (\CatAD, Level-0$\to$Level-3
structural lift).

\section{Transputation: The Fourth Option}
\label{sec:transputation}

Consider the three standard options for what happens during a quantum measurement.
\emph{Determinism} says that hidden variables determine the outcome in advance:
the particle always had a definite value, we simply did not know it.
\emph{Randomness} says the universe genuinely rolls dice: each outcome is selected by
an irreducibly stochastic process with no further structure.
\emph{Many-worlds} says all outcomes occur simultaneously in branching parallel realities.

GTE establishes that all three are incorrect, and proves a fourth option is forced
upon any universe satisfying PSC.  The correct description is \emph{transputation}:
a formally characterised, law-governed, non-computable branch selection.  It is not
the absence of determinism.  It is the presence of something structurally different ---
a process that is lawful (obeying five precise constraints D1--D5) but non-algorithmic
(no Turing machine can implement it on the self-referential diagonal fragment).

\begin{tcolorbox}[colback=green!5,colframe=green!50!black,
  title={Definition: Transputation}]
  Transputation is the law-governed internal adjudication process required and formally
  forced in any closed, record-bearing, diagonal-capable physical framework.  It is the
  formal role of the operator~$P^\top$ that resolves record-divergent choice --- identifying
  which PSC-consistent realization is canonical given a macroscopic record~$w$ --- when
  that selection cannot be performed by any total-effective procedure.
  Formally: $P^\top_D(w) = \operatorname{argmin}_\rho D(\rho|w)$, where $D \in [D]$
  satisfies constraints D1--D5.
  Transputation is NOT randomness, NOT hidden variables, NOT many-worlds.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{What Transputation Is Not}

\paragraph{Not determinism.}
Bell's theorem (1964) rules out local hidden-variable theories; but transputation is
ruled out even more broadly.  The \lean{diagonal\_forbids\allowbreak\_total\_determinism} theorem (\CatAL, nems-lean, NEMS
Paper~12) proves that no deterministic algorithm can reproduce the full PSC-consistent
measurement statistics: in a universe satisfying PSC, diagonal capability, and
record-divergence, a purely deterministic closure is impossible.  Determinism fails
structurally, not merely empirically.

\paragraph{Not randomness.}
The D1--D5 constraints on $[D]$ (detailed in §\ref{sec:d_record}) impose non-trivial
structure on which outcomes are selected.  In particular, constraint D5 requires that
the marginals of $P^\top$'s minimizing distribution reproduce the Born rule: $P(k) =
|c_k|^2$ (\lean{born\_rule\_unconditional}, \CatAL).  A pure random process consistent
with no structure cannot satisfy D5.  The Born rule is empirically extremely precise;
pure randomness would predict deviations, but none are observed.

\paragraph{Not many-worlds.}
PSC requires a single self-consistent record~$w$ for the universe: every element of the
universe must have a determinate PSC-admissible description.  Many-worlds posits that all
branches are simultaneously actual, which contradicts the PSC requirement that the
universe's total record selects a unique realization.  The $P^\top$ forcing chain
below (\lean{closed\_choice\_forces\_transputation}) selects a \emph{single} branch;
multiple branches simultaneously actual is structurally excluded by PSC~\cite{SpivackGTEMobius}.

above the first Turing jump; PSC's finite-witness record structure blocks jump
iteration.  The many-one degree equality is machine-certified\\
(\lean{pt\_diagonal\_manyOne\_degree\_halting}, transputation-lean, \CatAL);\\
the absence of any computable convergence modulus --- the operational
no-hypercomputation statement --- is certified unconditionally\\
(\lean{no\_computable\_convergence\_modulus}, nems-lean, \CatAL).\\
Full treatment: P51~\cite{SpivackPolynomialTransputation}.
Quantum computing
(BQP) remains within the Turing-decidable level; TPC's novelty is qualitative (a
different problem type, pinned at the halting degree) rather than quantitative (a
speed improvement).

\paragraph{TPC has three levels; $N_{\mathrm{gen}} = 3$.}
The TPC hierarchy has exactly three levels, corresponding to three reflexivity classes:
(0)~arithmetic layer (non-reflexive), (1)~computation layer (restricted self-reference),
and (2)~transputation layer (fully reflexive, diagonal-capable).  The three-generation
structure of the Standard Model satisfies $N_{\mathrm{gen}} = 3 =$ depth of the TPC
hierarchy.  Cert: \lean{tpc\_ngen\_equals\_level\_count} (\CatAL, zero sorry,
\texttt{GUTStructure.lean}~§62).  Whether this coincidence follows from a single
structural forcing (Conjecture~C3 of~\cite{SpivackGTEMobius}) is open; the numerical
identity itself is machine-certified.

\subsection*{Transputation and Physical Measurement}

At every quantum measurement event, transputation performs the following:

\begin{enumerate}
\item A physical record~$w$ is created (any record-bearing physical system satisfying
      NEMS Paper~09 minimal-record conditions: a detector click, an atom absorbing a
      photon, any environmental decoherence event).
\item The PSC closure structure activates the adjudication operator:
      $P^\top_D(w) = \operatorname{argmin}_\rho D(\rho|w)$.
\item By constraint D4 (selection completeness), this selects a \emph{unique}~$\rho^*$
      from the PSC-consistent realization class (\lean{d4\_physical\_sector}, \CatAL).
\item The selection is non-computable (D3): no Turing machine implements $P^\top$ on
      the diagonal-capable fragment.
\item The outcome is definite: the field is now in a specific kink sector
      $|\text{kink}_{k^*}\rangle$.
\end{enumerate}

This replaces wavefunction collapse.  There is no collapse: there is \emph{selection}.
The selection is objective --- independent of any observer or conscious agent.
Any record-bearing physical system (a particle detector, a chemical bond, a cosmic-ray
track in rock) triggers transputation.  No mind is required.

The composition rule cleanly separates two previously conflated operations:
\[
  P(\text{outcome} = k \,|\, w) = |c_k(P^\top_D(w))|^2.
\]
Computing \emph{how probable} each outcome is (D5 --- the Born rule, \CatAL) and
determining \emph{which outcome occurs} ($P^\top$ --- objective D-minimization,
\CatAD) are distinct mathematical operations with distinct Lean certifications.
Copenhagen conflates both into the ``collapse postulate.''  GTE separates them.

The two quantum-mechanical substrates used in P37 --- (A)~the $f_{\rm MDL}$ ring
orbit (Hilbert space, Born rule, gauge sectors) and (B)~the AFCA causal structure
(Lorentz invariance, §5 of P37) --- are both derived from the same object: the Level-1
PSC-orbit map and its Level-2 CMCA tape embedding (§\ref{sec:cmca}). They are
two distinct roles of one system, not two competing theories.
